declarations.name: BondThenPingWithWrongFrom
declarations.doc: This test verifies that the default behaviour of ignoring 'from' fields is unaffected by the bonding process. After bonding, it pings the target with a different from endpoint.

declarations.name: FindnodeAmplificationInvalidPongHash
declarations.doc: This test attempts to perform a traffic amplification attack against a 'victim' endpoint using FINDNODE. In this attack scenario, the attacker attempts to complete the endpoint proof non-interactively by sending a PONG with mismatching reply token from the 'victim' endpoint. The attack works if the remote node does not verify the PONG reply token field correctly. The attacker could then perform traffic amplification by sending many FINDNODE requests to the discovery node, which would reply to the 'victim' address.

declarations.name: FindnodeAmplificationWrongIP

declarations.name: FindnodeWithoutEndpointProof

declarations.name: PingExtraData

declarations.name: PingExtraDataWrongFrom

declarations.name: PingPastExpiration

declarations.name: WrongPacketType

declarations.doc: Fatalf formats a message to standard error and exits the program. The message is also printed to standard output if standard error is redirected to a different file.

declarations.name: ImportLDBData
declarations.doc: ImportLDBData imports a batch of snapshot data into the database

declarations.name: ImportPreimages
declarations.doc: ImportPreimages imports a batch of exported hash preimages into the database. It's a part of the deprecated functionality, should be removed in the future.

declarations.name: ChainDataIterator
declarations.doc: ChainDataIterator is an interface wraps all necessary functions to iterate the exporting chain data.

declarations.name: exportHeader
declarations.doc: exportHeader is used in the export/import flow. When we do an export, the first element we output is the exportHeader. Whenever a backwards-incompatible change is made, the Version header should be bumped. If the importer sees a higher version, it should reject the import.

declarations.name: Apply
declarations.doc: called by cli library, grabs variable from environment (if in env) and adds variable to flag set for parsing.

declarations.name: GlobalBig
declarations.doc: GlobalBig returns the value of a BigFlag from the global flag set.

declarations.name: GlobalTextMarshaler
declarations.doc: GlobalTextMarshaler returns the value of a TextMarshalerFlag from the global flag set.

declarations.name: expandPath
declarations.doc: Expands a file path 1. replace tilde with users home dir 2. expands embedded environment variables 3. cleans the path, e.g. /a/b/../c -> /a/c Note, it has limitations, e.g. ~someuser/tmp will not be expanded

declarations.name: BigFlag
declarations.doc: BigFlag is a command line flag that accepts 256 bit big integers in decimal or hexadecimal syntax.

declarations.name: DirectoryFlag
declarations.doc: Custom cli.Flag type which expand the received string to an absolute path. e.g. ~/.ethereum -> /home/username/.ethereum

declarations.name: DirectoryString
declarations.doc: Custom type which is registered in the flags library which cli uses for argument parsing. This allows us to expand Value to an absolute path when the argument is parsed

declarations.name: TextMarshalerFlag
declarations.doc: TextMarshalerFlag wraps a TextMarshaler value.

declarations.name: bigValue
declarations.doc: bigValue turns *big.Int into a flag.Value

declarations.name: textMarshalerVal
declarations.doc: textMarshalerVal turns a TextMarshaler into a flag.Value

declarations.name: TestDeletionExport
declarations.doc: testDeletion tests if the deletion markers can be exported/imported correctly

declarations.name: TestDeletionExportGzip
declarations.doc: TestDeletionExportGzip tests if the deletion markers can be exported/imported correctly with gz compression.

declarations.name: TestExport
declarations.doc: TestExport does basic sanity checks on the export/import functionality

declarations.name: TestImportFutureFormat
declarations.doc: TestImportFutureFormat tests that we reject unsupported future versions.

declarations.name: CheckExclusive
declarations.doc: CheckExclusive verifies that only a single instance of the provided flags was set by the user. Each flag might optionally be followed by a string type to specialize it further.

declarations.name: GroupFlags
declarations.doc: GroupFlags combines the given flag slices together and returns the merged one.

declarations.name: MakeAddress
declarations.doc: MakeAddress converts an account specified directly as a hex encoded string or a key index in the key store to an internal account representation.

declarations.name: MakeChain
declarations.doc: MakeChain creates a chain manager from set command line flags.

declarations.name: MakeChainDatabase
declarations.doc: MakeChainDatabase open an LevelDB using the flags passed to the client and will hard crash if it fails.

declarations.name: MakeConsolePreloads
declarations.doc: MakeConsolePreloads retrieves the absolute paths for the console JavaScript scripts to preload before starting.

declarations.name: MakeDataDir
declarations.doc: MakeDataDir retrieves the currently requested data directory, terminating if none (or the empty string) is specified. If the node is starting a testnet, then a subdirectory of the specified datadir will be used.

declarations.name: MakeDatabaseHandles
declarations.doc: MakeDatabaseHandles raises out the number of allowed file handles per process for Geth and returns half of the allowance to assign to the database.

declarations.name: MakePasswordList
declarations.doc: MakePasswordList reads password lines from the file specified by the global --password flag.

declarations.name: MigrateFlags
declarations.doc: MigrateFlags sets the global flag from a local flag when it's set. This is a temporary function used for migrating old command/flags to the new format. e.g. geth account new --keystore /tmp/mykeystore --lightkdf is equivalent after calling this method with: geth --keystore /tmp/mykeystore --lightkdf account new This allows the use of the existing configuration functionality. When all flags are migrated this function can be removed and the existing configuration functionality must be changed that is uses local flags

declarations.name: RegisterEthService
declarations.doc: RegisterEthService adds an Ethereum client to the stack. The second return value is the full node instance, which may be nil if the node is running as a light client.

declarations.name: RegisterEthStatsService
declarations.doc: RegisterEthStatsService configures the Ethereum Stats daemon and adds it to the given node.

declarations.name: RegisterGraphQLService
declarations.doc: RegisterGraphQLService is a utility function to construct a new service and register it against a node.

declarations.name: SetDNSDiscoveryDefaults
declarations.doc: SetDNSDiscoveryDefaults configures DNS discovery with the given URL if no URLs are set.

declarations.name: SetEthConfig
declarations.doc: SetEthConfig applies eth-related command line flags to the config.

declarations.name: SetNodeConfig
declarations.doc: SetNodeConfig applies node-related command line flags to the config.

declarations.name: SetWemixConfig
declarations.doc: SetWemixConfig applies wemix related command line flags to the config.

declarations.name: SplitAndTrim
declarations.doc: SplitAndTrim splits input separated by a comma and trims excessive white space from the substrings.

declarations.name: setBootstrapNodes
declarations.doc: setBootstrapNodes creates a list of bootstrap nodes from the command line flags, reverting to pre-configured ones if none have been specified.

declarations.name: setBootstrapNodesV5
declarations.doc: setBootstrapNodesV5 creates a list of bootstrap nodes from the command line flags, reverting to pre-configured ones if none have been specified.

declarations.name: setEtherbase
declarations.doc: setEtherbase retrieves the etherbase either from the directly specified command line flags or from the keystore if CLI indexed.

declarations.name: setGraphQL
declarations.doc: setGraphQL creates the GraphQL listener interface string from the set command line flags, returning empty if the GraphQL endpoint is disabled.

declarations.name: setHTTP
declarations.doc: setHTTP creates the HTTP RPC listener interface string from the set command line flags, returning empty if the HTTP endpoint is disabled.

declarations.name: setIPC
declarations.doc: setIPC creates an IPC path configuration from the set command line flags, returning an empty string if IPC was explicitly disabled, or the set path.

declarations.name: setLes
declarations.doc: setLes configures the les server and ultra light client settings from the command line flags.

declarations.name: setListenAddress
declarations.doc: setListenAddress creates a TCP listening address string from set command line flags.

declarations.name: setNAT
declarations.doc: setNAT creates a port mapper from command line flags.

declarations.name: setNodeKey
declarations.doc: setNodeKey creates a node key from set command line flags, either loading it from a file or as a specified hex value. If neither flags were provided, this method returns nil and an emphemeral key is to be generated.

declarations.name: setNodeUserIdent
declarations.doc: setNodeUserIdent creates the user identifier from CLI flags.

declarations.name: setRandomBootstrapNodes
declarations.doc: setRandomBootstrapNodes setting a random list of bootstrap nodes using the command line

declarations.name: setWS
declarations.doc: setWS creates the WebSocket RPC listener interface string from the set command line flags, returning empty if the HTTP endpoint is disabled.

declarations.name: showDeprecated
declarations.doc: showDeprecated displays deprecated flags that will be soon removed from the codebase.

declarations.name: GetPassPhrase
declarations.doc: GetPassPhrase displays the given text(prompt) to the user and requests some textual data to be entered, but one which must not be echoed out into the terminal. The method returns the input provided by the user.

declarations.name: GetPassPhraseWithList
declarations.doc: GetPassPhraseWithList retrieves the password associated with an account, either fetched from a list of preloaded passphrases, or requested interactively from the user.

declarations.name: ChainHeaderReader
declarations.doc: ChainHeaderReader defines a small collection of methods needed to access the local blockchain during header verification.

declarations.name: ChainReader
declarations.doc: ChainReader defines a small collection of methods needed to access the local blockchain during header and/or uncle verification.

declarations.name: Engine
declarations.doc: Engine is an algorithm agnostic consensus engine.

declarations.name: PoW
declarations.doc: PoW is a consensus engine based on proof-of-work.

declarations.name: FinalizePoS
declarations.doc: FinalizePoS is called whenever the first FinalisedBlock message received from the consensus-layer.

declarations.name: NewMerger
declarations.doc: NewMerger creates a new Merger which stores its transition status in the provided db.

declarations.name: PoSFinalized
declarations.doc: PoSFinalized reports whether the chain has entered the PoS stage.

declarations.name: ReachTTD
declarations.doc: ReachTTD is called whenever the first NewHead message received from the consensus-layer.

declarations.name: TDDReached
declarations.doc: TDDReached reports whether the chain has left the PoW stage.

declarations.name: Merger
declarations.doc: Merger is an internal help structure used to track the eth1/2 transition status. It's a common structure can be used in both full node and light client.

declarations.name: transitionStatus
declarations.doc: transitionStatus describes the status of eth1/2 transition. This switch between modes is a one-way action which is triggered by corresponding consensus-layer message.

declarations.name: APIs
declarations.doc: APIs implements consensus.Engine, returning the user facing RPC APIs.

declarations.name: Author
declarations.doc: Author implements consensus.Engine, returning the verified author of the block.

declarations.name: CalcDifficulty
declarations.doc: CalcDifficulty is the difficulty adjustment algorithm. It returns the difficulty that a new block should have when created at time given the parent block's time and difficulty.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close shutdowns the consensus engine

declarations.name: Finalize
declarations.doc: Finalize implements consensus.Engine, setting the final state on the header

declarations.name: FinalizeAndAssemble
declarations.doc: FinalizeAndAssemble implements consensus.Engine, setting the final state and assembling the block.

declarations.name: InnerEngine
declarations.doc: InnerEngine returns the embedded eth1 consensus engine.

declarations.name: IsPoSHeader
declarations.doc: IsPoSHeader reports the header belongs to the PoS-stage with some special fields. This function is not suitable for a part of APIs like Prepare or CalcDifficulty because the header difficulty is not set yet.

declarations.name: IsTTDReached
declarations.doc: IsTTDReached checks if the TotalTerminalDifficulty has been surpassed on the `parentHash` block. It depends on the parentHash already being stored in the database. If the parentHash is not stored in the database a UnknownAncestor error is returned.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New creates a consensus engine with the given embedded eth1 engine.

declarations.name: Prepare
declarations.doc: Prepare implements consensus.Engine, initializing the difficulty field of a header to conform to the beacon protocol. The changes are done inline.

declarations.name: Seal
declarations.doc: Seal generates a new sealing request for the given input block and pushes the result into the given channel. Note, the method returns immediately and will send the result async. More than one result may also be returned depending on the consensus algorithm.

declarations.name: SealHash
declarations.doc: SealHash returns the hash of a block prior to it being sealed.

declarations.name: SetThreads
declarations.doc: SetThreads updates the mining threads. Delegate the call to the eth1 engine if it's threaded.

declarations.name: VerifyHeader
declarations.doc: VerifyHeader checks whether a header conforms to the consensus rules of the stock Ethereum consensus engine.

declarations.name: VerifyHeaders
declarations.doc: VerifyHeaders is similar to VerifyHeader, but verifies a batch of headers concurrently. The method returns a quit channel to abort the operations and a results channel to retrieve the async verifications. VerifyHeaders expect the headers to be ordered and continuous.

declarations.name: VerifyUncles
declarations.doc: VerifyUncles verifies that the given block's uncles conform to the consensus rules of the Ethereum consensus engine.

declarations.name: verifyHeader
declarations.doc: verifyHeader checks whether a header conforms to the consensus rules of the stock Ethereum consensus engine. The difference between the beacon and classic is (a) The following fields are expected to be constants: - difficulty is expected to be 0 - nonce is expected to be 0 - unclehash is expected to be Hash(emptyHeader) to be the desired constants (b) the timestamp is not verified anymore (c) the extradata is limited to 32 bytes

declarations.name: verifyHeaders
declarations.doc: verifyHeaders is similar to verifyHeader, but verifies a batch of headers concurrently. The method returns a quit channel to abort the operations and a results channel to retrieve the async verifications. An additional parent header will be passed if the relevant header is not in the database yet.

declarations.name: Beacon
declarations.doc: Beacon is a consensus engine that combines the eth1 consensus and proof-of-stake algorithm. There is a special flag inside to decide whether to use legacy consensus rules or new rules. The transition rule is described in the eth1/2 merge spec. https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-3675.md The beacon here is a half-functional consensus engine with partial functions which is only used for necessary consensus checks. The legacy consensus engine can be any engine implements the consensus interface (except the beacon itself).

declarations.name: Discard
declarations.doc: Discard drops a currently running proposal, stopping the signer from casting further votes (either for or against).

declarations.name: GetSigner
declarations.doc: GetSigner returns the signer for a specific clique block. Can be called with either a blocknumber, blockhash or an rlp encoded blob. The RLP encoded blob can either be a block or a header.

declarations.name: GetSigners
declarations.doc: GetSigners retrieves the list of authorized signers at the specified block.

declarations.name: GetSignersAtHash
declarations.doc: GetSignersAtHash retrieves the list of authorized signers at the specified block.

declarations.name: GetSnapshot
declarations.doc: GetSnapshot retrieves the state snapshot at a given block.

declarations.name: GetSnapshotAtHash
declarations.doc: GetSnapshotAtHash retrieves the state snapshot at a given block.

declarations.name: Proposals
declarations.doc: Proposals returns the current proposals the node tries to uphold and vote on.

declarations.name: Propose
declarations.doc: Propose injects a new authorization proposal that the signer will attempt to push through.

declarations.name: Status
declarations.doc: Status returns the status of the last N blocks, - the number of active signers, - the number of signers, - the percentage of in-turn blocks

declarations.name: API
declarations.doc: API is a user facing RPC API to allow controlling the signer and voting mechanisms of the proof-of-authority scheme.

declarations.name: APIs
declarations.doc: APIs implements consensus.Engine, returning the user facing RPC API to allow controlling the signer voting.

declarations.name: Author
declarations.doc: Author implements consensus.Engine, returning the Ethereum address recovered from the signature in the header's extra-data section.

declarations.name: Authorize
declarations.doc: Authorize injects a private key into the consensus engine to mint new blocks with.

declarations.name: CalcDifficulty
declarations.doc: CalcDifficulty is the difficulty adjustment algorithm. It returns the difficulty that a new block should have: * DIFF_NOTURN(2) if BLOCK_NUMBER % SIGNER_COUNT != SIGNER_INDEX * DIFF_INTURN(1) if BLOCK_NUMBER % SIGNER_COUNT == SIGNER_INDEX

declarations.name: CliqueRLP
declarations.doc: CliqueRLP returns the rlp bytes which needs to be signed for the proof-of-authority sealing. The RLP to sign consists of the entire header apart from the 65 byte signature contained at the end of the extra data. Note, the method requires the extra data to be at least 65 bytes, otherwise it panics. This is done to avoid accidentally using both forms (signature present or not), which could be abused to produce different hashes for the same header.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close implements consensus.Engine. It's a noop for clique as there are no background threads.

declarations.name: Finalize
declarations.doc: Finalize implements consensus.Engine, ensuring no uncles are set, nor block rewards given.

declarations.name: FinalizeAndAssemble
declarations.doc: FinalizeAndAssemble implements consensus.Engine, ensuring no uncles are set, nor block rewards given, and returns the final block.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New creates a Clique proof-of-authority consensus engine with the initial signers set to the ones provided by the user.

declarations.name: Prepare
declarations.doc: Prepare implements consensus.Engine, preparing all the consensus fields of the header for running the transactions on top.

declarations.name: Seal
declarations.doc: Seal implements consensus.Engine, attempting to create a sealed block using the local signing credentials.

declarations.name: SealHash
declarations.doc: SealHash returns the hash of a block prior to it being sealed.

declarations.name: SealHash
declarations.doc: SealHash returns the hash of a block prior to it being sealed.

declarations.name: VerifyHeader
declarations.doc: VerifyHeader checks whether a header conforms to the consensus rules.

declarations.name: VerifyHeaders
declarations.doc: VerifyHeaders is similar to VerifyHeader, but verifies a batch of headers. The method returns a quit channel to abort the operations and a results channel to retrieve the async verifications (the order is that of the input slice).

declarations.name: VerifyUncles
declarations.doc: VerifyUncles implements consensus.Engine, always returning an error for any uncles as this consensus mechanism doesn't permit uncles.

declarations.name: ecrecover
declarations.doc: ecrecover extracts the Ethereum account address from a signed header.

declarations.name: snapshot
declarations.doc: snapshot retrieves the authorization snapshot at a given point in time.

declarations.name: verifyCascadingFields
declarations.doc: verifyCascadingFields verifies all the header fields that are not standalone, rather depend on a batch of previous headers. The caller may optionally pass in a batch of parents (ascending order) to avoid looking those up from the database. This is useful for concurrently verifying a batch of new headers.

declarations.name: verifyHeader
declarations.doc: verifyHeader checks whether a header conforms to the consensus rules.The caller may optionally pass in a batch of parents (ascending order) to avoid looking those up from the database. This is useful for concurrently verifying a batch of new headers.

declarations.name: verifySeal
declarations.doc: verifySeal checks whether the signature contained in the header satisfies the consensus protocol requirements. The method accepts an optional list of parent headers that aren't yet part of the local blockchain to generate the snapshots from.

declarations.name: Clique
declarations.doc: Clique is the proof-of-authority consensus engine proposed to support the Ethereum testnet following the Ropsten attacks.

declarations.name: SignerFn
declarations.doc: SignerFn hashes and signs the data to be signed by a backing account.

declarations.name: TestReimportMirroredState
declarations.doc: This test case is a repro of an annoying bug that took us forever to catch. In Clique PoA networks (Rinkeby, Görli, etc), consecutive blocks might have the same state root (no block subsidy, empty block). If a node crashes, the chain ends up losing the recent state and needs to regenerate it from blocks already in the database. The bug was that processing the block *prior* to an empty one **also completes** the empty one, ending up in a known-block error.

declarations.name: apply
declarations.doc: apply creates a new authorization snapshot by applying the given headers to the original one.

declarations.name: cast
declarations.doc: cast adds a new vote into the tally.

declarations.name: copy
declarations.doc: copy creates a deep copy of the snapshot, though not the individual votes.

declarations.name: inturn
declarations.doc: inturn returns if a signer at a given block height is in-turn or not.

declarations.name: loadSnapshot
declarations.doc: loadSnapshot loads an existing snapshot from the database.

declarations.name: newSnapshot
declarations.doc: newSnapshot creates a new snapshot with the specified startup parameters. This method does not initialize the set of recent signers, so only ever use if for the genesis block.

declarations.name: signers
declarations.doc: signers retrieves the list of authorized signers in ascending order.

declarations.name: store
declarations.doc: store inserts the snapshot into the database.

declarations.name: uncast
declarations.doc: uncast removes a previously cast vote from the tally.

declarations.name: validVote
declarations.doc: validVote returns whether it makes sense to cast the specified vote in the given snapshot context (e.g. don't try to add an already authorized signer).

declarations.name: Snapshot
declarations.doc: Snapshot is the state of the authorization voting at a given point in time.

declarations.name: Tally
declarations.doc: Tally is a simple vote tally to keep the current score of votes. Votes that go against the proposal aren't counted since it's equivalent to not voting.

declarations.name: Vote
declarations.doc: Vote represents a single vote that an authorized signer made to modify the list of authorizations.

declarations.name: signersAscending
declarations.doc: signersAscending implements the sort interface to allow sorting a list of addresses

declarations.name: TestClique
declarations.doc: Tests that Clique signer voting is evaluated correctly for various simple and complex scenarios, as well as that a few special corner cases fail correctly.

declarations.name: address
declarations.doc: address retrieves the Ethereum address of a tester account by label, creating a new account if no previous one exists yet.

declarations.name: checkpoint
declarations.doc: checkpoint creates a Clique checkpoint signer section from the provided list of authorized signers and embeds it into the provided header.

declarations.name: sign
declarations.doc: sign calculates a Clique digital signature for the given block and embeds it back into the header.

declarations.name: testerAccountPool
declarations.doc: testerAccountPool is a pool to maintain currently active tester accounts, mapped from textual names used in the tests below to actual Ethereum private keys capable of signing transactions.

declarations.name: testerVote
declarations.doc: testerVote represents a single block signed by a parcitular account, where the account may or may not have cast a Clique vote.

declarations.name: cacheSize
declarations.doc: cacheSize returns the size of the ethash verification cache that belongs to a certain block number.

declarations.name: calcCacheSize
declarations.doc: calcCacheSize calculates the cache size for epoch. The cache size grows linearly, however, we always take the highest prime below the linearly growing threshold in order to reduce the risk of accidental regularities leading to cyclic behavior.

declarations.name: calcDatasetSize
declarations.doc: calcDatasetSize calculates the dataset size for epoch. The dataset size grows linearly, however, we always take the highest prime below the linearly growing threshold in order to reduce the risk of accidental regularities leading to cyclic behavior.

declarations.name: datasetSize
declarations.doc: datasetSize returns the size of the ethash mining dataset that belongs to a certain block number.

declarations.name: fnv
declarations.doc: fnv is an algorithm inspired by the FNV hash, which in some cases is used as a non-associative substitute for XOR. Note that we multiply the prime with the full 32-bit input, in contrast with the FNV-1 spec which multiplies the prime with one byte (octet) in turn.

declarations.name: fnvHash
declarations.doc: fnvHash mixes in data into mix using the ethash fnv method.

declarations.name: generateCache
declarations.doc: generateCache creates a verification cache of a given size for an input seed. The cache production process involves first sequentially filling up 32 MB of memory, then performing two passes of Sergio Demian Lerner's RandMemoHash algorithm from Strict Memory Hard Hashing Functions (2014). The output is a set of 524288 64-byte values. This method places the result into dest in machine byte order.

declarations.name: generateDataset
declarations.doc: generateDataset generates the entire ethash dataset for mining. This method places the result into dest in machine byte order.

declarations.name: generateDatasetItem
declarations.doc: generateDatasetItem combines data from 256 pseudorandomly selected cache nodes, and hashes that to compute a single dataset node.

declarations.name: hashimeta
declarations.doc: a simple sha256 hash from seed & nonce

declarations.name: hashimoto
declarations.doc: hashimoto aggregates data from the full dataset in order to produce our final value for a particular header hash and nonce.

declarations.name: hashimotoFull
declarations.doc: hashimotoFull aggregates data from the full dataset (using the full in-memory dataset) in order to produce our final value for a particular header hash and nonce.

declarations.name: hashimotoLight
declarations.doc: hashimotoLight aggregates data from the full dataset (using only a small in-memory cache) in order to produce our final value for a particular header hash and nonce.

declarations.name: makeHasher
declarations.doc: makeHasher creates a repetitive hasher, allowing the same hash data structures to be reused between hash runs instead of requiring new ones to be created. The returned function is not thread safe!

declarations.name: seedHash
declarations.doc: seedHash is the seed to use for generating a verification cache and the mining dataset.

declarations.name: swap
declarations.doc: swap changes the byte order of the buffer assuming a uint32 representation.

declarations.name: hasher
declarations.doc: hasher is a repetitive hasher allowing the same hash data structures to be reused between hash runs instead of requiring new ones to be created.

declarations.name: BenchmarkCacheGeneration
declarations.doc: Benchmarks the cache generation performance.

declarations.name: BenchmarkHashimotoFullMmap
declarations.doc: Benchmarks the full verification performance for mmap

declarations.name: BenchmarkHashimotoFullSmall
declarations.doc: Benchmarks the full (small) verification performance.

declarations.name: BenchmarkHashimotoLight
declarations.doc: Benchmarks the light verification performance.

declarations.name: BenchmarkSmallDatasetGeneration
declarations.doc: Benchmarks the dataset (small) generation performance.

declarations.name: TestCacheGeneration
declarations.doc: Tests that verification caches can be correctly generated.

declarations.name: TestConcurrentDiskCacheGeneration
declarations.doc: Tests that caches generated on disk may be done concurrently.

declarations.name: TestHashimoto
declarations.doc: Tests whether the hashimoto lookup works for both light as well as the full datasets.

declarations.name: TestSizeCalculations
declarations.doc: Tests whether the dataset size calculator works correctly by cross checking the hard coded lookup table with the value generated by it.

declarations.name: prepare
declarations.doc: prepare converts an ethash cache or dataset from a byte stream into the internal int representation. All ethash methods work with ints to avoid constant byte to int conversions as well as to handle both little and big endian systems.

declarations.name: GetHashrate
declarations.doc: GetHashrate returns the current hashrate for local CPU miner and remote miner.

declarations.name: GetWork
declarations.doc: GetWork returns a work package for external miner. The work package consists of 3 strings: result[0] - 32 bytes hex encoded current block header pow-hash result[1] - 32 bytes hex encoded seed hash used for DAG result[2] - 32 bytes hex encoded boundary condition ("target"), 2^256/difficulty result[3] - hex encoded block number

declarations.name: SubmitHashrate
declarations.doc: SubmitHashrate can be used for remote miners to submit their hash rate. This enables the node to report the combined hash rate of all miners which submit work through this node. It accepts the miner hash rate and an identifier which must be unique between nodes.

declarations.name: SubmitWork
declarations.doc: SubmitWork can be used by external miner to submit their POW solution. It returns an indication if the work was accepted. Note either an invalid solution, a stale work a non-existent work will return false.

declarations.name: API
declarations.doc: API exposes ethash related methods for the RPC interface.

declarations.name: Author
declarations.doc: Author implements consensus.Engine, returning the header's coinbase as the proof-of-work verified author of the block.

declarations.name: CalcDifficulty
declarations.doc: CalcDifficulty is the difficulty adjustment algorithm. It returns the difficulty that a new block should have when created at time given the parent block's time and difficulty.

declarations.name: CalcDifficulty
declarations.doc: CalcDifficulty is the difficulty adjustment algorithm. It returns the difficulty that a new block should have when created at time given the parent block's time and difficulty.

declarations.name: Finalize
declarations.doc: Finalize implements consensus.Engine, accumulating the block and uncle rewards, setting the final state on the header

declarations.name: FinalizeAndAssemble
declarations.doc: FinalizeAndAssemble implements consensus.Engine, accumulating the block and uncle rewards, setting the final state and assembling the block.

declarations.name: Prepare
declarations.doc: Prepare implements consensus.Engine, initializing the difficulty field of a header to conform to the ethash protocol. The changes are done inline.

declarations.name: SealHash
declarations.doc: SealHash returns the hash of a block prior to it being sealed.

declarations.name: VerifyHeader
declarations.doc: VerifyHeader checks whether a header conforms to the consensus rules of the stock Ethereum ethash engine.

declarations.name: VerifyHeaders
declarations.doc: VerifyHeaders is similar to VerifyHeader, but verifies a batch of headers concurrently. The method returns a quit channel to abort the operations and a results channel to retrieve the async verifications.

declarations.name: VerifyUncles
declarations.doc: VerifyUncles verifies that the given block's uncles conform to the consensus rules of the stock Ethereum ethash engine.

declarations.name: accumulateRewards
declarations.doc: AccumulateRewards credits the coinbase of the given block with the mining reward. The total reward consists of the static block reward and rewards for included uncles. The coinbase of each uncle block is also rewarded.

declarations.name: calcDifficultyFrontier
declarations.doc: calcDifficultyFrontier is the difficulty adjustment algorithm. It returns the difficulty that a new block should have when created at time given the parent block's time and difficulty. The calculation uses the Frontier rules.

declarations.name: calcDifficultyHomestead
declarations.doc: calcDifficultyHomestead is the difficulty adjustment algorithm. It returns the difficulty that a new block should have when created at time given the parent block's time and difficulty. The calculation uses the Homestead rules.

declarations.name: makeDifficultyCalculator
declarations.doc: makeDifficultyCalculator creates a difficultyCalculator with the given bomb-delay. the difficulty is calculated with Byzantium rules, which differs from Homestead in how uncles affect the calculation

declarations.name: verifyHeader
declarations.doc: verifyHeader checks whether a header conforms to the consensus rules of the stock Ethereum ethash engine. See YP section 4.3.4. "Block Header Validity"

declarations.name: verifySeal
declarations.doc: verifySeal checks whether a block satisfies the PoW difficulty requirements, either using the usual ethash cache for it, or alternatively using a full DAG to make remote mining fast.

declarations.name: CalcDifficultyFrontierU256
declarations.doc: CalcDifficultyFrontierU256 is the difficulty adjustment algorithm. It returns the difficulty that a new block should have when created at time given the parent block's time and difficulty. The calculation uses the Frontier rules.

declarations.name: CalcDifficultyHomesteadU256
declarations.doc: CalcDifficultyHomesteadU256 is the difficulty adjustment algorithm. It returns the difficulty that a new block should have when created at time given the parent block's time and difficulty. The calculation uses the Homestead rules.

declarations.name: MakeDifficultyCalculatorU256
declarations.doc: MakeDifficultyCalculatorU256 creates a difficultyCalculator with the given bomb-delay. the difficulty is calculated with Byzantium rules, which differs from Homestead in how uncles affect the calculation

declarations.name: APIs
declarations.doc: APIs implements consensus.Engine, returning the user facing RPC APIs.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close closes the exit channel to notify all backend threads exiting.

declarations.name: Hashrate
declarations.doc: Hashrate implements PoW, returning the measured rate of the search invocations per second over the last minute. Note the returned hashrate includes local hashrate, but also includes the total hashrate of all remote miner.

declarations.name: MakeCache
declarations.doc: MakeCache generates a new ethash cache and optionally stores it to disk.

declarations.name: MakeDataset
declarations.doc: MakeDataset generates a new ethash dataset and optionally stores it to disk.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New creates a full sized ethash PoW scheme and starts a background thread for remote mining, also optionally notifying a batch of remote services of new work packages.

declarations.name: NewFakeDelayer
declarations.doc: NewFakeDelayer creates a ethash consensus engine with a fake PoW scheme that accepts all blocks as valid, but delays verifications by some time, though they still have to conform to the Ethereum consensus rules.

declarations.name: NewFakeFailer
declarations.doc: NewFakeFailer creates a ethash consensus engine with a fake PoW scheme that accepts all blocks as valid apart from the single one specified, though they still have to conform to the Ethereum consensus rules.

declarations.name: NewFaker
declarations.doc: NewFaker creates a ethash consensus engine with a fake PoW scheme that accepts all blocks' seal as valid, though they still have to conform to the Ethereum consensus rules.

declarations.name: NewFullFaker
declarations.doc: NewFullFaker creates an ethash consensus engine with a full fake scheme that accepts all blocks as valid, without checking any consensus rules whatsoever.

declarations.name: NewShared
declarations.doc: NewShared creates a full sized ethash PoW shared between all requesters running in the same process.

declarations.name: NewTester
declarations.doc: NewTester creates a small sized ethash PoW scheme useful only for testing purposes.

declarations.name: SeedHash
declarations.doc: SeedHash is the seed to use for generating a verification cache and the mining dataset.

declarations.name: SetThreads
declarations.doc: SetThreads updates the number of mining threads currently enabled. Calling this method does not start mining, only sets the thread count. If zero is specified, the miner will use all cores of the machine. Setting a thread count below zero is allowed and will cause the miner to idle, without any work being done.

declarations.name: StopRemoteSealer
declarations.doc: StopRemoteSealer stops the remote sealer

declarations.name: Threads
declarations.doc: Threads returns the number of mining threads currently enabled. This doesn't necessarily mean that mining is running!

declarations.name: cache
declarations.doc: cache tries to retrieve a verification cache for the specified block number by first checking against a list of in-memory caches, then against caches stored on disk, and finally generating one if none can be found.

declarations.name: dataset
declarations.doc: dataset tries to retrieve a mining dataset for the specified block number by first checking against a list of in-memory datasets, then against DAGs stored on disk, and finally generating one if none can be found. If async is specified, not only the future but the current DAG is also generates on a background thread.

declarations.name: finalizer
declarations.doc: finalizer unmaps the memory and closes the file.

declarations.name: finalizer
declarations.doc: finalizer closes any file handlers and memory maps open.

declarations.name: generate
declarations.doc: generate ensures that the cache content is generated before use.

declarations.name: generate
declarations.doc: generate ensures that the dataset content is generated before use.

declarations.name: generated
declarations.doc: generated returns whether this particular dataset finished generating already or not (it may not have been started at all). This is useful for remote miners to default to verification caches instead of blocking on DAG generations.

declarations.name: get
declarations.doc: get retrieves or creates an item for the given epoch. The first return value is always non-nil. The second return value is non-nil if lru thinks that an item will be useful in the near future.

declarations.name: isLittleEndian
declarations.doc: isLittleEndian returns whether the local system is running in little or big endian byte order.

declarations.name: memoryMap
declarations.doc: memoryMap tries to memory map a file of uint32s for read only access.

declarations.name: memoryMapAndGenerate
declarations.doc: memoryMapAndGenerate tries to memory map a temporary file of uint32s for write access, fill it with the data from a generator and then move it into the final path requested.

declarations.name: memoryMapFile
declarations.doc: memoryMapFile tries to memory map an already opened file descriptor.

declarations.name: newCache
declarations.doc: newCache creates a new ethash verification cache and returns it as a plain Go interface to be usable in an LRU cache.

declarations.name: newDataset
declarations.doc: newDataset creates a new ethash mining dataset and returns it as a plain Go interface to be usable in an LRU cache.

declarations.name: newlru
declarations.doc: newlru create a new least-recently-used cache for either the verification caches or the mining datasets.

declarations.name: Config
declarations.doc: Config are the configuration parameters of the ethash.

declarations.name: Ethash
declarations.doc: Ethash is a consensus engine based on proof-of-work implementing the ethash algorithm.

declarations.name: Mode
declarations.doc: Mode defines the type and amount of PoW verification an ethash engine makes.

declarations.name: cache
declarations.doc: cache wraps an ethash cache with some metadata to allow easier concurrent use.

declarations.name: dataset
declarations.doc: dataset wraps an ethash dataset with some metadata to allow easier concurrent use.

declarations.name: lru
declarations.doc: lru tracks caches or datasets by their last use time, keeping at most N of them.

declarations.name: TestCacheFileEvict
declarations.doc: This test checks that cache lru logic doesn't crash under load. It reproduces https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/14943

declarations.name: TestTestMode
declarations.doc: Tests that ethash works correctly in test mode.

declarations.name: ensureSize
declarations.doc: ensureSize expands the file to the given size. This is to prevent runtime errors later on, if the underlying file expands beyond the disk capacity, even though it ostensibly is already expanded, but due to being sparse does not actually occupy the full declared size on disk.

declarations.name: ensureSize
declarations.doc: ensureSize expands the file to the given size. This is to prevent runtime errors later on, if the underlying file expands beyond the disk capacity, even though it ostensibly is already expanded, but due to being sparse does not actually occupy the full declared size on disk.

declarations.name: Seal
declarations.doc: Seal implements consensus.Engine, attempting to find a nonce that satisfies the block's difficulty requirements.

declarations.name: makeWork
declarations.doc: makeWork creates a work package for external miner. The work package consists of 3 strings: result[0], 32 bytes hex encoded current block header pow-hash result[1], 32 bytes hex encoded seed hash used for DAG result[2], 32 bytes hex encoded boundary condition ("target"), 2^256/difficulty result[3], hex encoded block number

declarations.name: mine
declarations.doc: mine is the actual proof-of-work miner that searches for a nonce starting from seed that results in correct final block difficulty.

declarations.name: notifyWork
declarations.doc: notifyWork notifies all the specified mining endpoints of the availability of new work to be processed.

declarations.name: submitWork
declarations.doc: submitWork verifies the submitted pow solution, returning whether the solution was accepted or not (not can be both a bad pow as well as any other error, like no pending work or stale mining result).

declarations.name: hashrate
declarations.doc: hashrate wraps the hash rate submitted by the remote sealer.

declarations.name: mineResult
declarations.doc: mineResult wraps the pow solution parameters for the specified block.

declarations.name: sealTask
declarations.doc: sealTask wraps a seal block with relative result channel for remote sealer thread.

declarations.name: sealWork
declarations.doc: sealWork wraps a seal work package for remote sealer.

declarations.name: TestRemoteMultiNotify
declarations.doc: Tests that pushing work packages fast to the miner doesn't cause any data race issues in the notifications.

declarations.name: TestRemoteMultiNotifyFull
declarations.doc: Tests that pushing work packages fast to the miner doesn't cause any data race issues in the notifications. Full pending block body / --miner.notify.full)

declarations.name: TestRemoteNotify
declarations.doc: Tests whether remote HTTP servers are correctly notified of new work.

declarations.name: TestRemoteNotifyFull
declarations.doc: Tests whether remote HTTP servers are correctly notified of new work. (Full pending block body / --miner.notify.full)

declarations.name: TestStaleSubmission
declarations.doc: Tests whether stale solutions are correctly processed.

declarations.name: ApplyDAOHardFork
declarations.doc: ApplyDAOHardFork modifies the state database according to the DAO hard-fork rules, transferring all balances of a set of DAO accounts to a single refund contract.

declarations.name: VerifyDAOHeaderExtraData
declarations.doc: VerifyDAOHeaderExtraData validates the extra-data field of a block header to ensure it conforms to DAO hard-fork rules. DAO hard-fork extension to the header validity: a) if the node is no-fork, do not accept blocks in the [fork, fork+10) range with the fork specific extra-data set b) if the node is pro-fork, require blocks in the specific range to have the unique extra-data set.

declarations.name: CalcBaseFee
declarations.doc: CalcBaseFee calculates the basefee of the header.

declarations.name: VerifyEip1559Header
declarations.doc: VerifyEip1559Header verifies some header attributes which were changed in EIP-1559, - gas limit check - basefee check

declarations.name: TestBlockGasLimits
declarations.doc: TestBlockGasLimits tests the gasLimit checks for blocks both across the EIP-1559 boundary and post-1559 blocks

declarations.name: TestCalcBaseFee
declarations.doc: TestCalcBaseFee assumes all blocks are 1559-blocks

declarations.name: copyConfig
declarations.doc: copyConfig does a _shallow_ copy of a given config. Safe to set new values, but do not use e.g. SetInt() on the numbers. For testing only

declarations.name: VerifyForkHashes
declarations.doc: VerifyForkHashes verifies that blocks conforming to network hard-forks do have the correct hashes, to avoid clients going off on different chains. This is an optional feature.

declarations.name: VerifyGaslimit
declarations.doc: VerifyGaslimit verifies the header gas limit according increase/decrease in relation to the parent gas limit.

declarations.name: genTxRing
declarations.doc: genTxRing returns a block generator that sends ether in a ring among n accounts. This is creates n entries in the state database and fills the blocks with many small transactions.

declarations.name: genUncles
declarations.doc: genUncles generates blocks with two uncle headers.

declarations.name: genValueTx
declarations.doc: genValueTx returns a block generator that includes a single value-transfer transaction with n bytes of extra data in each block.

declarations.name: makeChainForBench
declarations.doc: makeChainForBench writes a given number of headers or empty blocks/receipts into a database.

declarations.name: CalcGasLimit
declarations.doc: CalcGasLimit computes the gas limit of the next block after parent. It aims to keep the baseline gas close to the provided target, and increase it towards the target if the baseline gas is lower.

declarations.name: NewBlockValidator
declarations.doc: NewBlockValidator returns a new block validator which is safe for re-use

declarations.name: ValidateBody
declarations.doc: ValidateBody validates the given block's uncles and verifies the block header's transaction and uncle roots. The headers are assumed to be already validated at this point.

declarations.name: ValidateState
declarations.doc: ValidateState validates the various changes that happen after a state transition, such as amount of used gas, the receipt roots and the state root itself. ValidateState returns a database batch if the validation was a success otherwise nil and an error is returned.

declarations.name: BlockValidator
declarations.doc: BlockValidator is responsible for validating block headers, uncles and processed state. BlockValidator implements Validator.

declarations.name: TestHeaderConcurrentAbortion2
declarations.doc: Tests that aborting a header validation indeed prevents further checks from being run, as well as checks that no left-over goroutines are leaked.

declarations.name: TestHeaderConcurrentVerification2
declarations.doc: Tests that concurrent header verification works, for both good and bad blocks.

declarations.name: TestHeaderVerification
declarations.doc: Tests that simple header verification works, for both good and bad blocks.

declarations.name: testHeaderVerificationForMerging
declarations.doc: Tests the verification for eth1/2 merging, including pre-merge and post-merge

declarations.name: Export
declarations.doc: Export writes the active chain to the given writer.

declarations.name: ExportN
declarations.doc: ExportN writes a subset of the active chain to the given writer.

declarations.name: InsertBlockWithoutSetHead
declarations.doc: InsertBlockWithoutSetHead executes the block, runs the necessary verification upon it and then persist the block and the associate state into the database. The key difference between the InsertChain is it won't do the canonical chain updating. It relies on the additional SetCanonical call to finalize the entire procedure.

declarations.name: InsertChain
declarations.doc: InsertChain attempts to insert the given batch of blocks in to the canonical chain or, otherwise, create a fork. If an error is returned it will return the index number of the failing block as well an error describing what went wrong. After insertion is done, all accumulated events will be fired.

declarations.name: InsertHeaderChain
declarations.doc: InsertHeaderChain attempts to insert the given header chain in to the local chain, possibly creating a reorg. If an error is returned, it will return the index number of the failing header as well an error describing what went wrong. The verify parameter can be used to fine tune whether nonce verification should be done or not. The reason behind the optional check is because some of the header retrieval mechanisms already need to verify nonces, as well as because nonces can be verified sparsely, not needing to check each.

declarations.name: InsertReceiptChain
declarations.doc: InsertReceiptChain attempts to complete an already existing header chain with transaction and receipt data.

declarations.name: NewBlockChain
declarations.doc: NewBlockChain returns a fully initialised block chain using information available in the database. It initialises the default Ethereum Validator and Processor.

declarations.name: Reset
declarations.doc: Reset purges the entire blockchain, restoring it to its genesis state.

declarations.name: ResetWithGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: ResetWithGenesisBlock purges the entire blockchain, restoring it to the specified genesis state.

declarations.name: SetCanonical
declarations.doc: SetCanonical rewinds the chain to set the new head block as the specified block. It's possible that the state of the new head is missing, and it will be recovered in this function as well.

declarations.name: SetFinalized
declarations.doc: SetFinalized sets the finalized block.

declarations.name: SetHead
declarations.doc: SetHead rewinds the local chain to a new head. Depending on whether the node was fast synced or full synced and in which state, the method will try to delete minimal data from disk whilst retaining chain consistency.

declarations.name: SnapSyncCommitHead
declarations.doc: SnapSyncCommitHead sets the current head block to the one defined by the hash irrelevant what the chain contents were prior.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop stops the blockchain service. If any imports are currently in progress it will abort them using the procInterrupt.

declarations.name: StopInsert
declarations.doc: StopInsert interrupts all insertion methods, causing them to return errInsertionInterrupted as soon as possible. Insertion is permanently disabled after calling this method.

declarations.name: WriteBlockAndSetHead
declarations.doc: WriteBlockAndSetHead writes the given block and all associated state to the database, and applies the block as the new chain head.

declarations.name: addFutureBlock
declarations.doc: addFutureBlock checks if the block is within the max allowed window to get accepted for future processing, and returns an error if the block is too far ahead and was not added. TODO after the transition, the future block shouldn't be kept. Because it's not checked in the Geth side anymore.

declarations.name: collectLogs
declarations.doc: collectLogs collects the logs that were generated or removed during the processing of the block that corresponds with the given hash. These logs are later announced as deleted or reborn.

declarations.name: empty
declarations.doc: empty returns an indicator whether the blockchain is empty. Note, it's a special case that we connect a non-empty ancient database with an empty node, so that we can plugin the ancient into node seamlessly.

declarations.name: insertChain
declarations.doc: insertChain is the internal implementation of InsertChain, which assumes that 1) chains are contiguous, and 2) The chain mutex is held. This method is split out so that import batches that require re-injecting historical blocks can do so without releasing the lock, which could lead to racey behaviour. If a sidechain import is in progress, and the historic state is imported, but then new canon-head is added before the actual sidechain completes, then the historic state could be pruned again

declarations.name: insertSideChain
declarations.doc: insertSideChain is called when an import batch hits upon a pruned ancestor error, which happens when a sidechain with a sufficiently old fork-block is found. The method writes all (header-and-body-valid) blocks to disk, then tries to switch over to the new chain if the TD exceeded the current chain. insertSideChain is only used pre-merge.

declarations.name: insertStopped
declarations.doc: insertStopped returns true after StopInsert has been called.

declarations.name: loadLastState
declarations.doc: loadLastState loads the last known chain state from the database. This method assumes that the chain manager mutex is held.

declarations.name: maintainTxIndex
declarations.doc: maintainTxIndex is responsible for the construction and deletion of the transaction index. User can use flag `txlookuplimit` to specify a "recentness" block, below which ancient tx indices get deleted. If `txlookuplimit` is 0, it means all tx indices will be reserved. The user can adjust the txlookuplimit value for each launch after fast sync, Geth will automatically construct the missing indices and delete the extra indices.

declarations.name: mergeLogs
declarations.doc: mergeLogs returns a merged log slice with specified sort order.

declarations.name: recoverAncestors
declarations.doc: recoverAncestors finds the closest ancestor with available state and re-execute all the ancestor blocks since that. recoverAncestors is only used post-merge. We return the hash of the latest block that we could correctly validate.

declarations.name: reorg
declarations.doc: reorg takes two blocks, an old chain and a new chain and will reconstruct the blocks and inserts them to be part of the new canonical chain and accumulates potential missing transactions and post an event about them. Note the new head block won't be processed here, callers need to handle it externally.

declarations.name: reportBlock
declarations.doc: reportBlock logs a bad block error.

declarations.name: setHeadBeyondRoot
declarations.doc: setHeadBeyondRoot rewinds the local chain to a new head with the extra condition that the rewind must pass the specified state root. This method is meant to be used when rewinding with snapshots enabled to ensure that we go back further than persistent disk layer. Depending on whether the node was fast synced or full, and in which state, the method will try to delete minimal data from disk whilst retaining chain consistency. The method returns the block number where the requested root cap was found.

declarations.name: skipBlock
declarations.doc: skipBlock returns 'true', if the block being imported can be skipped over, meaning that the block does not need to be processed but can be considered already fully 'done'.

declarations.name: writeBlockAndSetHead
declarations.doc: writeBlockAndSetHead is the internal implementation of WriteBlockAndSetHead. This function expects the chain mutex to be held.

declarations.name: writeBlockWithState
declarations.doc: writeBlockWithState writes block, metadata and corresponding state data to the database.

declarations.name: writeBlockWithoutState
declarations.doc: writeBlockWithoutState writes only the block and its metadata to the database, but does not write any state. This is used to construct competing side forks up to the point where they exceed the canonical total difficulty.

declarations.name: writeHeadBlock
declarations.doc: writeHeadBlock injects a new head block into the current block chain. This method assumes that the block is indeed a true head. It will also reset the head header and the head fast sync block to this very same block if they are older or if they are on a different side chain. Note, this function assumes that the `mu` mutex is held!

declarations.name: writeKnownBlock
declarations.doc: writeKnownBlock updates the head block flag with a known block and introduces chain reorg if necessary.

declarations.name: BlockChain
declarations.doc: BlockChain represents the canonical chain given a database with a genesis block. The Blockchain manages chain imports, reverts, chain reorganisations. Importing blocks in to the block chain happens according to the set of rules defined by the two stage Validator. Processing of blocks is done using the Processor which processes the included transaction. The validation of the state is done in the second part of the Validator. Failing results in aborting of the import. The BlockChain also helps in returning blocks from **any** chain included in the database as well as blocks that represents the canonical chain. It's important to note that GetBlock can return any block and does not need to be included in the canonical one where as GetBlockByNumber always represents the canonical chain.

declarations.name: CacheConfig
declarations.doc: CacheConfig contains the configuration values for the trie caching/pruning that's resident in a blockchain.

declarations.name: WriteStatus
declarations.doc: WriteStatus status of write

declarations.name: current
declarations.doc: current returns the current header that is being processed, or nil.

declarations.name: first
declarations.doc: first returns the first block in the it.

declarations.name: newInsertIterator
declarations.doc: newInsertIterator creates a new iterator based on the given blocks, which are assumed to be a contiguous chain.

declarations.name: next
declarations.doc: next returns the next block in the iterator, along with any potential validation error for that block. When the end is reached, it will return (nil, nil).

declarations.name: peek
declarations.doc: peek returns the next block in the iterator, along with any potential validation error for that block, but does **not** advance the iterator. Both header and body validation errors (nil too) is cached into the iterator to avoid duplicating work on the following next() call.

declarations.name: previous
declarations.doc: previous returns the previous header that was being processed, or nil.

declarations.name: processed
declarations.doc: processed returns the number of processed blocks.

declarations.name: remaining
declarations.doc: remaining returns the number of remaining blocks.

declarations.name: report
declarations.doc: report prints statistics if some number of blocks have been processed or more than a few seconds have passed since the last message.

declarations.name: insertIterator
declarations.doc: insertIterator is a helper to assist during chain import.

declarations.name: insertStats
declarations.doc: insertStats tracks and reports on block insertion.

declarations.name: Config
declarations.doc: Config retrieves the chain's fork configuration.

declarations.name: ContractCode
declarations.doc: ContractCode retrieves a blob of data associated with a contract hash either from ephemeral in-memory cache, or from persistent storage.

declarations.name: ContractCodeWithPrefix
declarations.doc: ContractCodeWithPrefix retrieves a blob of data associated with a contract hash either from ephemeral in-memory cache, or from persistent storage. If the code doesn't exist in the in-memory cache, check the storage with new code scheme.

declarations.name: CurrentBlock
declarations.doc: CurrentBlock retrieves the current head block of the canonical chain. The block is retrieved from the blockchain's internal cache.

declarations.name: CurrentFastBlock
declarations.doc: CurrentFastBlock retrieves the current fast-sync head block of the canonical chain. The block is retrieved from the blockchain's internal cache.

declarations.name: CurrentFinalizedBlock
declarations.doc: CurrentFinalizedBlock retrieves the current finalized block of the canonical chain. The block is retrieved from the blockchain's internal cache.

declarations.name: CurrentHeader
declarations.doc: CurrentHeader retrieves the current head header of the canonical chain. The header is retrieved from the HeaderChain's internal cache.

declarations.name: Engine
declarations.doc: Engine retrieves the blockchain's consensus engine.

declarations.name: GasLimit
declarations.doc: GasLimit returns the gas limit of the current HEAD block.

declarations.name: Genesis
declarations.doc: Genesis retrieves the chain's genesis block.

declarations.name: GetAncestor
declarations.doc: GetAncestor retrieves the Nth ancestor of a given block. It assumes that either the given block or a close ancestor of it is canonical. maxNonCanonical points to a downwards counter limiting the number of blocks to be individually checked before we reach the canonical chain. Note: ancestor == 0 returns the same block, 1 returns its parent and so on.

declarations.name: GetBlock
declarations.doc: GetBlock retrieves a block from the database by hash and number, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetBlockByHash
declarations.doc: GetBlockByHash retrieves a block from the database by hash, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetBlockByNumber
declarations.doc: GetBlockByNumber retrieves a block from the database by number, caching it (associated with its hash) if found.

declarations.name: GetBlocksFromHash
declarations.doc: GetBlocksFromHash returns the block corresponding to hash and up to n-1 ancestors. [deprecated by eth/62]

declarations.name: GetBody
declarations.doc: GetBody retrieves a block body (transactions and uncles) from the database by hash, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetBodyRLP
declarations.doc: GetBodyRLP retrieves a block body in RLP encoding from the database by hash, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetCanonicalHash
declarations.doc: GetCanonicalHash returns the canonical hash for a given block number

declarations.name: GetHeader
declarations.doc: GetHeader retrieves a block header from the database by hash and number, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByHash
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByHash retrieves a block header from the database by hash, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByNumber
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByNumber retrieves a block header from the database by number, caching it (associated with its hash) if found.

declarations.name: GetHeadersFrom
declarations.doc: GetHeadersFrom returns a contiguous segment of headers, in rlp-form, going backwards from the given number.

declarations.name: GetReceiptsByHash
declarations.doc: GetReceiptsByHash retrieves the receipts for all transactions in a given block.

declarations.name: GetTd

declarations.name: TestIssue23496
declarations.doc: TestIssue23496 tests scenario described in https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/23496#issuecomment-926393893 Credits to @zzyalbert for finding the issue. Local chain owns these blocks: G B1 B2 B3 B4 B1: state committed B2: snapshot disk layer B3: state committed B4: head block Crash happens without fully persisting snapshot and in-memory states, chain rewinds itself to the B1 (skip B3 in order to recover snapshot) In this case the snapshot layer of B3 is not created because of existent state.

Everything above the sethead point should be deleted. In between the committed block and the requested head the data can remain as "fast sync" data to avoid redownloading it. The side chain should be left alone as it was shorter.

declarations.name: TestShortOldForkedSnapSyncedSetHead
declarations.doc: Tests a sethead for a short canonical chain and a shorter side chain, where the fast sync pivot point was already committed to disk and then sethead was called. In this test scenario the side chain is below the committed block. In this case we expect the canonical full chain to be rolled back to the committed block. Everything above the sethead point should be deleted. In between the committed block and the requested head the data can remain as "fast sync" data to avoid redownloading it. The side chain should be left alone as it was shorter.

declarations.name: TestShortOldForkedSnapSyncingSetHead
declarations.doc: Tests a sethead for a short canonical chain and a shorter side chain, where the fast sync pivot point was not yet committed, but sethead was called. In this test scenario the side chain is below the committed block. In this case we expect the chain to detect that it was fast syncing and delete everything from the new head, since we can just pick up fast syncing from there. The head full block should be set to the genesis.

declarations.name: TestShortReorgedSetHead
declarations.doc: Tests a sethead for a short canonical chain and a longer side chain, where a recent block was already committed to disk and then sethead was called. In this case we expect the canonical full chain to be rolled back to the committed block. All data above the sethead point should be deleted. In between the committed block and the requested head the data can remain as "fast sync" data to avoid having to redownload it. The side chain should be truncated to the head set. The side chain could be left to be if the fork point was before the new head we are deleting to, but it would be exceedingly hard to detect that case and properly handle it, so we'll trade extra work in exchange for simpler code.

declarations.name: TestShortReorgedSnapSyncedSetHead
declarations.doc: Tests a sethead for a short canonical chain and a longer side chain, where the fast sync pivot point was already committed to disk and then sethead was called. In this case we expect the canonical full chain to be rolled back to the committed block. All data above the sethead point should be deleted. In between the committed block and the requested head the data can remain as "fast sync" data to avoid having to redownload it. The side chain should be truncated to the head set. The side chain could be left to be if the fork point was before the new head we are deleting to, but it would be exceedingly hard to detect that case and properly handle it, so we'll trade extra work in exchange for simpler code.

declarations.name: TestShortReorgedSnapSyncingSetHead
declarations.doc: Tests a sethead for a short canonical chain and a longer side chain, where the fast sync pivot point was not yet committed, but sethead was called. In this case we expect the chain to detect that it was fast syncing and delete everything from the new head, since we can just pick up fast syncing from there. The side chain could be left to be if the fork point was before the new head we are deleting to, but it would be exceedingly hard to detect that case and properly handle it, so we'll trade extra work in exchange for simpler code.

declarations.name: TestShortSetHead
declarations.doc: Tests a sethead for a short canonical chain where a recent block was already committed to disk and then the sethead called. In this case we expect the full chain to be rolled back to the committed block. Everything above the sethead point should be deleted. In between the committed block and the requested head the data can remain as "fast sync" data to avoid redownloading it.

declarations.name: TestShortSnapSyncedSetHead
declarations.doc: Tests a sethead for a short canonical chain where the fast sync pivot point was already committed, after which sethead was called. In this case we expect the chain to behave like in full sync mode, rolling back to the committed block Everything above the sethead point should be deleted. In between the committed block and the requested head the data can remain as "fast sync" data to avoid redownloading it.

declarations.name: TestShortSnapSyncingSetHead
declarations.doc: Tests a sethead for a short canonical chain where the fast sync pivot point was not yet committed, but sethead was called. In this case we expect the chain to detect that it was fast syncing and delete everything from the new head, since we can just pick up fast syncing from there. The head full block should be set to the genesis.

declarations.name: uint64ptr
declarations.doc: uint64ptr is a weird helper to allow 1-line constant pointer creation.

declarations.name: verifyCutoff
declarations.doc: verifyCutoff checks that there are no chain data available in the chain after the specified limit, but that it is available before.

declarations.name: verifyNoGaps
declarations.doc: verifyNoGaps checks that there are no gaps after the initial set of blocks in the database and errors if found.

declarations.name: rewindTest
declarations.doc: rewindTest is a test case for chain rollback upon user request.

declarations.name: TestGappedNewSnapshot
declarations.doc: Tests a Geth was running with snapshot enabled. Then restarts without enabling snapshot and after that re-enable the snapshot again. In this case the snapshot should be rebuilt with latest chain head.

declarations.name: TestHighCommitCrashWithNewSnapshot
declarations.doc: Tests a Geth was crashed and restarts with a broken snapshot. In this case the chain head should be rewound to the point with available state. And also the new head should must be lower than disk layer. But there is only a high committed point so the chain should be rewound to genesis and the disk layer should be left for recovery.

declarations.name: TestLowCommitCrashWithNewSnapshot
declarations.doc: Tests a Geth was crashed and restarts with a broken snapshot. In this case the chain head should be rewound to the point with available state. And also the new head should must be lower than disk layer. But there is only a low committed point so the chain should be rewound to committed point and the disk layer should be left for recovery.

declarations.name: TestNoCommitCrashWithNewSnapshot
declarations.doc: Tests a Geth was crashed and restarts with a broken snapshot. In this case the chain head should be rewound to the point with available state. And also the new head should must be lower than disk layer. But there is no committed point so the chain should be rewound to genesis and the disk layer should be left for recovery.

declarations.name: TestRecoverSnapshotFromWipingCrash
declarations.doc: Tests the Geth was running with a complete snapshot and then imports a few more new blocks on top without enabling the snapshot. After the restart, crash happens. Check everything is ok after the restart.

declarations.name: TestRestartWithNewSnapshot
declarations.doc: Tests a Geth restart with valid snapshot. Before the shutdown, all snapshot journal will be persisted correctly. In this case no snapshot recovery is required.

declarations.name: TestSetHeadWithNewSnapshot
declarations.doc: Tests the Geth was running with snapshot enabled and resetHead is applied. In this case the head is rewound to the target(with state available). After that the chain is restarted and the original disk layer is kept.

declarations.name: crashSnapshotTest
declarations.doc: crashSnapshotTest is a test case type for innormal snapshot recovery. It can be used for testing that restart Geth after the crash.

declarations.name: gappedSnapshotTest
declarations.doc: gappedSnapshotTest is a test type used to test this scenario: - have a complete snapshot - restart without enabling the snapshot - insert a few blocks - restart with enabling the snapshot again

declarations.name: restartCrashSnapshotTest
declarations.doc: restartCrashSnapshotTest is the test type used to test this scenario: - have a complete snapshot - restart chain - insert more blocks with enabling the snapshot - commit the snapshot - crash - restart again

declarations.name: setHeadSnapshotTest
declarations.doc: setHeadSnapshotTest is the test type used to test this scenario: - have a complete snapshot - set the head to a lower point - restart

declarations.name: snapshotTest
declarations.doc: snapshotTest is a test case type for normal snapshot recovery. It can be used for testing that restart Geth normally.

declarations.name: snapshotTestBasic
declarations.doc: snapshotTestBasic wraps the common testing fields in the snapshot tests.

declarations.name: wipeCrashSnapshotTest
declarations.doc: wipeCrashSnapshotTest is the test type used to test this scenario: - have a complete snapshot - restart, insert more blocks without enabling the snapshot - restart again with enabling the snapshot - crash

declarations.name: TestBadHeaderHashes
declarations.doc: Tests that the insertion functions detect banned hashes.

declarations.name: TestBlockchainHeaderchainReorgConsistency
declarations.doc: This is a regression test (i.e. as weird as it is, don't delete it ever), which tests that under weird reorg conditions the blockchain and its internal header- chain return the same latest block/header. https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/15941

declarations.name: TestBrokenHeaderChain
declarations.doc: Tests that chains missing links do not get accepted by the processor.

declarations.name: TestCanonicalBlockRetrieval
declarations.doc: Tests if the canonical block can be fetched from the database during chain insertion.

declarations.name: TestChainTxReorgs
declarations.doc: Tests that chain reorganisations handle transaction removals and reinsertions.

declarations.name: TestDeleteCreateRevert
declarations.doc: TestDeleteCreateRevert tests a weird state transition corner case that we hit while changing the internals of statedb. The workflow is that a contract is self destructed, then in a followup transaction (but same block) it's created again and the transaction reverted. The original statedb implementation flushed dirty objects to the tries after each transaction, so this works ok. The rework accumulated writes in memory first, but the journal wiped the entire state object on create-revert.

declarations.name: TestDeleteRecreateAccount
declarations.doc: TestDeleteRecreateAccount tests a state-transition that contains deletion of a contract with storage, and a recreate of the same contract via a regular value-transfer Expected outcome is that _all_ slots are cleared from A

declarations.name: TestDeleteRecreateSlots
declarations.doc: TestDeleteRecreateSlots tests a state-transition that contains both deletion and recreation of contract state. Contract A exists, has slots 1 and 2 set Tx 1: Selfdestruct A Tx 2: Re-create A, set slots 3 and 4 Expected outcome is that _all_ slots are cleared from A, due to the selfdestruct, and then the new slots exist

declarations.name: TestDeleteRecreateSlotsAcrossManyBlocks
declarations.doc: TestDeleteRecreateSlotsAcrossManyBlocks tests multiple state-transition that contains both deletion and recreation of contract state. Contract A exists, has slots 1 and 2 set Tx 1: Selfdestruct A Tx 2: Re-create A, set slots 3 and 4 Expected outcome is that _all_ slots are cleared from A, due to the selfdestruct, and then the new slots exist

declarations.name: TestEIP1559Transition
declarations.doc: TestEIP1559Transition tests the following: 1. A transaction whose gasFeeCap is greater than the baseFee is valid. 2. Gas accounting for access lists on EIP-1559 transactions is correct. 3. Only the transaction's tip will be received by the coinbase. 4. The transaction sender pays for both the tip and baseFee. 5. The coinbase receives only the partially realized tip when gasFeeCap - gasTipCap < baseFee. 6. Legacy transaction behave as expected (e.g. gasPrice = gasFeeCap = gasTipCap).

declarations.name: TestEIP2718Transition
declarations.doc: TestEIP2718Transition tests that an EIP-2718 transaction will be accepted after the fork block has passed. This is verified by sending an EIP-2930 access list transaction, which specifies a single slot access, and then checking that the gas usage of a hot SLOAD and a cold SLOAD are calculated correctly.

declarations.name: TestEqualForkHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, creating equal forks do take canonical ownership.

declarations.name: TestEqualForkHeadersAfterMerge
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, creating equal forks do take canonical ownership.

declarations.name: TestExtendCanonicalHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, it can be extended with various length chains.

declarations.name: TestExtendCanonicalHeadersAfterMerge
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, it can be extended with various length chains.

declarations.name: TestFastVsFullChains
declarations.doc: Tests that fast importing a block chain produces the same chain data as the classical full block processing.

declarations.name: TestHeadersInsertNonceError
declarations.doc: Tests chain insertions in the face of one entity containing an invalid nonce.

declarations.name: TestInitThenFailCreateContract
