declarations.doc: TestInitThenFailCreateContract tests a pretty notorious case that happened on mainnet over blocks 7338108, 7338110 and 7338115. - Block 7338108: address e771789f5cccac282f23bb7add5690e1f6ca467c is initiated with 0.001 ether (thus created but no code) - Block 7338110: a CREATE2 is attempted. The CREATE2 would deploy code on the same address e771789f5cccac282f23bb7add5690e1f6ca467c. However, the deployment fails due to OOG during initcode execution - Block 7338115: another tx checks the balance of e771789f5cccac282f23bb7add5690e1f6ca467c, and the snapshotter returned it as zero. The problem being that the snapshotter maintains a destructset, and adds items to the destructset in case something is created "onto" an existing item. We need to either roll back the snapDestructs, or not place it into snapDestructs in the first place.

declarations.name: TestInsertReceiptChainRollback
declarations.doc: This test checks that InsertReceiptChain will roll back correctly when attempting to insert a side chain.

declarations.name: TestLargeReorgTrieGC
declarations.doc: Tests that doing large reorgs works even if the state associated with the forking point is not available any more.

declarations.name: TestLightVsFastVsFullChainHeads
declarations.doc: Tests that various import methods move the chain head pointers to the correct positions.

declarations.name: TestLogRebirth
declarations.doc: This test checks that log events and RemovedLogsEvent are sent when the chain reorganizes.

declarations.name: TestLongerForkHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, creating longer forks do take canonical ownership.

declarations.name: TestLongerForkHeadersAfterMerge
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, creating longer forks do take canonical ownership.

declarations.name: TestLowDiffLongChain
declarations.doc: Tests that importing a very large side fork, which is larger than the canon chain, but where the difficulty per block is kept low: this means that it will not overtake the 'canon' chain until after it's passed canon by about 200 blocks. Details at: - https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/18977 - https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/18988

declarations.name: TestPrunedImportSide
declarations.doc: Tests that importing a sidechain (S), where - S is sidechain, containing blocks [Sn...Sm] - C is canon chain, containing blocks [G..Cn..Cm] - The common ancestor Cc is pruned - The first block in S: Sn, is == Cn That is: the sidechain for import contains some blocks already present in canon chain. So the blocks are [ Cn, Cn+1, Cc, Sn+3 ... Sm] ^ ^ ^ pruned

declarations.name: TestReorgBadHeaderHashes
declarations.doc: Tests that bad hashes are detected on boot, and the chain rolled back to a good state prior to the bad hash.

declarations.name: TestReorgLongHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that reorganising a long difficult chain after a short easy one overwrites the canonical numbers and links in the database.

declarations.name: TestReorgShortHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that reorganising a short difficult chain after a long easy one overwrites the canonical numbers and links in the database.

declarations.name: TestReorgToShorterRemovesCanonMapping
declarations.doc: TestReorgToShorterRemovesCanonMapping tests that if we 1. Have a chain [0 ... N .. X] 2. Reorg to shorter but heavier chain [0 ... N ... Y] 3. Then there should be no canon mapping for the block at height X 4. The forked block should still be retrievable by hash

declarations.name: TestReorgToShorterRemovesCanonMappingHeaderChain
declarations.doc: TestReorgToShorterRemovesCanonMappingHeaderChain is the same scenario as TestReorgToShorterRemovesCanonMapping, but applied on headerchain imports -- that is, for fast sync

declarations.name: TestSetCanonical
declarations.doc: Tests the scenario the chain is requested to another point with the missing state. It expects the state is recovered and all relevant chain markers are set correctly.

declarations.name: TestShorterForkHeaders
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, creating shorter forks do not take canonical ownership.

declarations.name: TestShorterForkHeadersAfterMerge
declarations.doc: Tests that given a starting canonical chain of a given size, creating shorter forks do not take canonical ownership.

declarations.name: TestSideImportPrunedBlocks
declarations.doc: Tests that importing a some old blocks, where all blocks are before the pruning point. This internally leads to a sidechain import, since the blocks trigger an ErrPrunedAncestor error. This may e.g. happen if 1. Downloader rollbacks a batch of inserted blocks and exits 2. Downloader starts to sync again 3. The blocks fetched are all known and canonical blocks

declarations.name: TestSideLogRebirth
declarations.doc: This test is a variation of TestLogRebirth. It verifies that log events are emitted when a side chain containing log events overtakes the canonical chain.

declarations.name: TestTrieForkGC
declarations.doc: Tests that importing small side forks doesn't leave junk in the trie database cache (which would eventually cause memory issues).

declarations.name: benchmarkLargeNumberOfValueToNonexisting
declarations.doc: Benchmarks large blocks with value transfers to non-existing accounts

declarations.name: getLongAndShortChains
declarations.doc: getLongAndShortChains returns two chains: A is longer, B is heavier.

declarations.name: newCanonical
declarations.doc: newCanonical creates a chain database, and injects a deterministic canonical chain. Depending on the full flag, if creates either a full block chain or a header only chain.

declarations.name: testBlockChainImport
declarations.doc: testBlockChainImport tries to process a chain of blocks, writing them into the database if successful.

declarations.name: testFork
declarations.doc: Test fork of length N starting from block i

declarations.name: testHeaderChainImport
declarations.doc: testHeaderChainImport tries to process a chain of header, writing them into the database if successful.

declarations.name: testInsertAfterMerge
declarations.doc: Test inserts the blocks/headers after the fork choice rule is changed. The chain is reorged to whatever specified.

declarations.name: testInsertKnownChainDataWithMerging
declarations.doc: mergeHeight can be assigned in these values: 0: means the merging is applied since genesis 1: means the merging is applied after the first segment

declarations.name: testSideImport
declarations.doc: Tests that importing a sidechain (S), where - S is sidechain, containing blocks [Sn...Sm] - C is canon chain, containing blocks [G..Cn..Cm] - A common ancestor is placed at prune-point + blocksBetweenCommonAncestorAndPruneblock - The sidechain S is prepended with numCanonBlocksInSidechain blocks from the canon chain The mergePoint can be these values: -1: the transition won't happen 0: the transition happens since genesis 1: the transition happens after some chain segments

declarations.name: Commit
declarations.doc: Commit implements core.ChainIndexerBackend, finalizing the bloom section and writing it out into the database.

declarations.name: NewBloomIndexer
declarations.doc: NewBloomIndexer returns a chain indexer that generates bloom bits data for the canonical chain for fast logs filtering.

declarations.name: Process
declarations.doc: Process implements core.ChainIndexerBackend, adding a new header's bloom into the index.

declarations.name: Prune
declarations.doc: Prune returns an empty error since we don't support pruning here.

declarations.name: Reset
declarations.doc: Reset implements core.ChainIndexerBackend, starting a new bloombits index section.

declarations.name: BloomIndexer
declarations.doc: BloomIndexer implements a core.ChainIndexer, building up a rotated bloom bits index for the Ethereum header bloom filters, permitting blazing fast filtering.

declarations.name: AddCheckpoint
declarations.doc: AddCheckpoint adds a checkpoint. Sections are never processed and the chain is not expected to be available before this point. The indexer assumes that the backend has sufficient information available to process subsequent sections. Note: knownSections == 0 and storedSections == checkpointSections until syncing reaches the checkpoint

declarations.name: AddChildIndexer
declarations.doc: AddChildIndexer adds a child ChainIndexer that can use the output of this one

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close tears down all goroutines belonging to the indexer and returns any error that might have occurred internally.

declarations.name: NewChainIndexer
declarations.doc: NewChainIndexer creates a new chain indexer to do background processing on chain segments of a given size after certain number of confirmations passed. The throttling parameter might be used to prevent database thrashing.

declarations.name: Prune
declarations.doc: Prune deletes all chain data older than given threshold.

declarations.name: SectionHead
declarations.doc: SectionHead retrieves the last block hash of a processed section from the index database.

declarations.name: Sections
declarations.doc: Sections returns the number of processed sections maintained by the indexer and also the information about the last header indexed for potential canonical verifications.

declarations.name: Start
declarations.doc: Start creates a goroutine to feed chain head events into the indexer for cascading background processing. Children do not need to be started, they are notified about new events by their parents.

declarations.name: eventLoop
declarations.doc: eventLoop is a secondary - optional - event loop of the indexer which is only started for the outermost indexer to push chain head events into a processing queue.

declarations.name: loadValidSections
declarations.doc: loadValidSections reads the number of valid sections from the index database and caches is into the local state.

declarations.name: newHead
declarations.doc: newHead notifies the indexer about new chain heads and/or reorgs.

declarations.name: processSection
declarations.doc: processSection processes an entire section by calling backend functions while ensuring the continuity of the passed headers. Since the chain mutex is not held while processing, the continuity can be broken by a long reorg, in which case the function returns with an error.

declarations.name: removeSectionHead
declarations.doc: removeSectionHead removes the reference to a processed section from the index database.

declarations.name: setSectionHead
declarations.doc: setSectionHead writes the last block hash of a processed section to the index database.

declarations.name: setValidSections
declarations.doc: setValidSections writes the number of valid sections to the index database

declarations.name: updateLoop
declarations.doc: updateLoop is the main event loop of the indexer which pushes chain segments down into the processing backend.

declarations.name: verifyLastHead
declarations.doc: verifyLastHead compares last stored section head with the corresponding block hash in the actual canonical chain and rolls back reorged sections if necessary to ensure that stored sections are all valid

declarations.name: ChainIndexer
declarations.doc: ChainIndexer does a post-processing job for equally sized sections of the canonical chain (like BlooomBits and CHT structures). A ChainIndexer is connected to the blockchain through the event system by starting a ChainHeadEventLoop in a goroutine. Further child ChainIndexers can be added which use the output of the parent section indexer. These child indexers receive new head notifications only after an entire section has been finished or in case of rollbacks that might affect already finished sections.

declarations.name: ChainIndexerBackend
declarations.doc: ChainIndexerBackend defines the methods needed to process chain segments in the background and write the segment results into the database. These can be used to create filter blooms or CHTs.

declarations.name: ChainIndexerChain
declarations.doc: ChainIndexerChain interface is used for connecting the indexer to a blockchain

declarations.name: TestChainIndexerSingle
declarations.doc: Runs multiple tests with randomized parameters.

declarations.name: TestChainIndexerWithChildren
declarations.doc: Runs multiple tests with randomized parameters and different number of chain backends.

declarations.name: assertBlocks
declarations.doc: assertBlocks expects processing calls after new blocks have arrived. If the failNum < headNum then we are simulating a scenario where a reorg has happened after the processing has started and the processing of a section fails.

declarations.name: assertSections
declarations.doc: assertSections verifies if a chain indexer has the correct number of section.

declarations.name: testChainIndexer
declarations.doc: testChainIndexer runs a test with either a single chain indexer or a chain of multiple backends. The section size and required confirmation count parameters are randomized.

declarations.name: testChainIndexBackend
declarations.doc: testChainIndexBackend implements ChainIndexerBackend

declarations.name: AddTx
declarations.doc: AddTx adds a transaction to the generated block. If no coinbase has been set, the block's coinbase is set to the zero address. AddTx panics if the transaction cannot be executed. In addition to the protocol-imposed limitations (gas limit, etc.), there are some further limitations on the content of transactions that can be added. Notably, contract code relying on the BLOCKHASH instruction will panic during execution.

declarations.name: AddTxWithChain
declarations.doc: AddTxWithChain adds a transaction to the generated block. If no coinbase has been set, the block's coinbase is set to the zero address. AddTxWithChain panics if the transaction cannot be executed. In addition to the protocol-imposed limitations (gas limit, etc.), there are some further limitations on the content of transactions that can be added. If contract code relies on the BLOCKHASH instruction, the block in chain will be returned.

declarations.name: AddUncheckedReceipt
declarations.doc: AddUncheckedReceipt forcefully adds a receipts to the block without a backing transaction. AddUncheckedReceipt will cause consensus failures when used during real chain processing. This is best used in conjunction with raw block insertion.

declarations.name: AddUncheckedTx
declarations.doc: AddUncheckedTx forcefully adds a transaction to the block without any validation. AddUncheckedTx will cause consensus failures when used during real chain processing. This is best used in conjunction with raw block insertion.

declarations.name: AddUncle
declarations.doc: AddUncle adds an uncle header to the generated block.

declarations.name: BaseFee
declarations.doc: BaseFee returns the EIP-1559 base fee of the block being generated.

declarations.name: Config
declarations.doc: Config returns the chain configuration.

declarations.name: GenerateChain
declarations.doc: GenerateChain creates a chain of n blocks. The first block's parent will be the provided parent. db is used to store intermediate states and should contain the parent's state trie. The generator function is called with a new block generator for every block. Any transactions and uncles added to the generator become part of the block. If gen is nil, the blocks will be empty and their coinbase will be the zero address. Blocks created by GenerateChain do not contain valid proof of work values. Inserting them into BlockChain requires use of FakePow or a similar non-validating proof of work implementation.

declarations.name: GetBalance
declarations.doc: GetBalance returns the balance of the given address at the generated block.

declarations.name: Number
declarations.doc: Number returns the block number of the block being generated.

declarations.name: OffsetTime
declarations.doc: OffsetTime modifies the time instance of a block, implicitly changing its associated difficulty. It's useful to test scenarios where forking is not tied to chain length directly.

declarations.name: PrevBlock
declarations.doc: PrevBlock returns a previously generated block by number. It panics if num is greater or equal to the number of the block being generated. For index -1, PrevBlock returns the parent block given to GenerateChain.

declarations.name: SetCoinbase
declarations.doc: SetCoinbase sets the coinbase of the generated block. It can be called at most once.

declarations.name: SetDifficulty
declarations.doc: SetDifficulty sets the difficulty field of the generated block. This method is useful for Clique tests where the difficulty does not depend on time. For the ethash tests, please use OffsetTime, which implicitly recalculates the diff.

declarations.name: SetExtra
declarations.doc: SetExtra sets the extra data field of the generated block.

declarations.name: SetNonce
declarations.doc: SetNonce sets the nonce field of the generated block.

declarations.name: TxNonce
declarations.doc: TxNonce returns the next valid transaction nonce for the account at addr. It panics if the account does not exist.

declarations.name: makeBlockChain
declarations.doc: makeBlockChain creates a deterministic chain of blocks rooted at parent.

declarations.name: makeHeaderChain
declarations.doc: makeHeaderChain creates a deterministic chain of headers rooted at parent.

declarations.name: BlockGen
declarations.doc: BlockGen creates blocks for testing. See GenerateChain for a detailed explanation.

declarations.name: TestDAOForkRangeExtradata
declarations.doc: Tests that DAO-fork enabled clients can properly filter out fork-commencing blocks based on their extradata fields.

declarations.name: NewMinedBlockEvent
declarations.doc: NewMinedBlockEvent is posted when a block has been imported.

declarations.name: NewTxsEvent
declarations.doc: NewTxsEvent is posted when a batch of transactions enter the transaction pool.

declarations.name: RemovedLogsEvent
declarations.doc: RemovedLogsEvent is posted when a reorg happens

declarations.name: CanTransfer
declarations.doc: CanTransfer checks whether there are enough funds in the address' account to make a transfer. This does not take the necessary gas in to account to make the transfer valid.

declarations.name: GetHashFn
declarations.doc: GetHashFn returns a GetHashFunc which retrieves header hashes by number

declarations.name: NewEVMBlockContext
declarations.doc: NewEVMBlockContext creates a new context for use in the EVM.

declarations.name: NewEVMTxContext
declarations.doc: NewEVMTxContext creates a new transaction context for a single transaction.

declarations.name: Transfer
declarations.doc: Transfer subtracts amount from sender and adds amount to recipient using the given Db

declarations.name: ChainContext
declarations.doc: ChainContext supports retrieving headers and consensus parameters from the current blockchain to be used during transaction processing.

declarations.name: ReorgNeeded
declarations.doc: ReorgNeeded returns whether the reorg should be applied based on the given external header and local canonical chain. In the td mode, the new head is chosen if the corresponding total difficulty is higher. In the extern mode, the trusted header is always selected as the head.

declarations.name: ChainReader
declarations.doc: ChainReader defines a small collection of methods needed to access the local blockchain during header verification. It's implemented by both blockchain and lightchain.

declarations.name: ForkChoice
declarations.doc: ForkChoice is the fork chooser based on the highest total difficulty of the chain(the fork choice used in the eth1) and the external fork choice (the fork choice used in the eth2). This main goal of this ForkChoice is not only for offering fork choice during the eth1/2 merge phase, but also keep the compatibility for all other proof-of-work networks.

declarations.name: AddGas
declarations.doc: AddGas makes gas available for execution.

declarations.name: Gas
declarations.doc: Gas returns the amount of gas remaining in the pool.

declarations.name: SubGas
declarations.doc: SubGas deducts the given amount from the pool if enough gas is available and returns an error otherwise.

declarations.name: GasPool
declarations.doc: GasPool tracks the amount of gas available during execution of the transactions in a block. The zero value is a pool with zero gas available.

declarations.name: MarshalJSON
declarations.doc: MarshalJSON marshals as JSON.

declarations.name: UnmarshalJSON
declarations.doc: UnmarshalJSON unmarshals from JSON.

declarations.name: MarshalJSON
declarations.doc: MarshalJSON marshals as JSON.

declarations.name: UnmarshalJSON
declarations.doc: UnmarshalJSON unmarshals from JSON.

declarations.name: Commit
declarations.doc: Commit writes the block and state of a genesis specification to the database. The block is committed as the canonical head block.

declarations.name: CommitGenesisState
declarations.doc: CommitGenesisState loads the stored genesis state with the given block hash and commits them into the given database handler.

declarations.name: DefaultGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: DefaultGenesisBlock returns the Ethereum main net genesis block.

declarations.name: DefaultGoerliGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: DefaultGoerliGenesisBlock returns the Görli network genesis block.

declarations.name: DefaultRinkebyGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: DefaultRinkebyGenesisBlock returns the Rinkeby network genesis block.

declarations.name: DefaultRopstenGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: DefaultRopstenGenesisBlock returns the Ropsten network genesis block.

declarations.name: DefaultSepoliaGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: DefaultSepoliaGenesisBlock returns the Sepolia network genesis block.

declarations.name: DefaultTestnetGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: DefaultTestnetGenesisBlock returns the Ropsten network genesis block.

declarations.name: DeveloperGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: DeveloperGenesisBlock returns the 'geth --dev' genesis block.

declarations.name: GenesisBlockForTesting
declarations.doc: GenesisBlockForTesting creates and writes a block in which addr has the given wei balance.

declarations.name: MustCommit
declarations.doc: MustCommit writes the genesis block and state to db, panicking on error. The block is committed as the canonical head block.

declarations.name: SetupGenesisBlock
declarations.doc: SetupGenesisBlock writes or updates the genesis block in db. The block that will be used is: genesis == nil genesis != nil +------------------------------------------ db has no genesis | main-net default | genesis db has genesis | from DB | genesis (if compatible) The stored chain configuration will be updated if it is compatible (i.e. does not specify a fork block below the local head block). In case of a conflict, the error is a *params.ConfigCompatError and the new, unwritten config is returned. The returned chain configuration is never nil.

declarations.name: ToBlock
declarations.doc: ToBlock creates the genesis block and writes state of a genesis specification to the given database (or discards it if nil).

declarations.name: flush
declarations.doc: flush adds allocated genesis accounts into a fresh new statedb and commit the state changes into the given database handler.

declarations.name: write
declarations.doc: write writes the json marshaled genesis state into database with the given block hash as the unique identifier.

declarations.name: Genesis
declarations.doc: Genesis specifies the header fields, state of a genesis block. It also defines hard fork switch-over blocks through the chain configuration.

declarations.name: GenesisAccount
declarations.doc: GenesisAccount is an account in the state of the genesis block.

declarations.name: GenesisAlloc
declarations.doc: GenesisAlloc specifies the initial state that is part of the genesis block.

declarations.name: GenesisMismatchError
declarations.doc: GenesisMismatchError is raised when trying to overwrite an existing genesis block with an incompatible one.

declarations.name: genesisSpecMarshaling
declarations.doc: field type overrides for gencodec

declarations.name: storageJSON
declarations.doc: storageJSON represents a 256 bit byte array, but allows less than 256 bits when unmarshaling from hex.

declarations.name: TestGenesisHashes
declarations.doc: TestGenesisHashes checks the congruity of default genesis data to corresponding hardcoded genesis hash values.

declarations.name: Config
declarations.doc: Config retrieves the header chain's chain configuration.

declarations.name: CurrentHeader
declarations.doc: CurrentHeader retrieves the current head header of the canonical chain. The header is retrieved from the HeaderChain's internal cache.

declarations.name: Engine
declarations.doc: Engine retrieves the header chain's consensus engine.

declarations.name: GetAncestor
declarations.doc: GetAncestor retrieves the Nth ancestor of a given block. It assumes that either the given block or a close ancestor of it is canonical. maxNonCanonical points to a downwards counter limiting the number of blocks to be individually checked before we reach the canonical chain. Note: ancestor == 0 returns the same block, 1 returns its parent and so on.

declarations.name: GetBlock
declarations.doc: GetBlock implements consensus.ChainReader, and returns nil for every input as a header chain does not have blocks available for retrieval.

declarations.name: GetBlockNumber
declarations.doc: GetBlockNumber retrieves the block number belonging to the given hash from the cache or database

declarations.name: GetHeader
declarations.doc: GetHeader retrieves a block header from the database by hash and number, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByHash
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByHash retrieves a block header from the database by hash, caching it if found.

declarations.name: GetHeaderByNumber
declarations.doc: GetHeaderByNumber retrieves a block header from the database by number, caching it (associated with its hash) if found.

declarations.name: GetHeadersFrom
declarations.doc: GetHeadersFrom returns a contiguous segment of headers, in rlp-form, going backwards from the given number. If the 'number' is higher than the highest local header, this method will return a best-effort response, containing the headers that we do have.

declarations.name: GetTd
declarations.doc: GetTd retrieves a block's total difficulty in the canonical chain from the database by hash and number, caching it if found.

declarations.name: HasHeader
declarations.doc: HasHeader checks if a block header is present in the database or not. In theory, if header is present in the database, all relative components like td and hash->number should be present too.

declarations.name: InsertHeaderChain
declarations.doc: InsertHeaderChain inserts the given headers and does the reorganisations. The validity of the headers is NOT CHECKED by this method, i.e. they need to be validated by ValidateHeaderChain before calling InsertHeaderChain. This insert is all-or-nothing. If this returns an error, no headers were written, otherwise they were all processed successfully. The returned 'write status' says if the inserted headers are part of the canonical chain or a side chain.

declarations.name: NewHeaderChain
declarations.doc: NewHeaderChain creates a new HeaderChain structure. ProcInterrupt points to the parent's interrupt semaphore.

declarations.name: Reorg
declarations.doc: Reorg reorgs the local canonical chain into the specified chain. The reorg can be classified into two cases: (a) extend the local chain (b) switch the head to the given header.

declarations.name: SetCurrentHeader
declarations.doc: SetCurrentHeader sets the in-memory head header marker of the canonical chan as the given header.

declarations.name: SetGenesis
declarations.doc: SetGenesis sets a new genesis block header for the chain

declarations.name: SetHead
declarations.doc: SetHead rewinds the local chain to a new head. Everything above the new head will be deleted and the new one set.

declarations.name: WriteHeaders
declarations.doc: WriteHeaders writes a chain of headers into the local chain, given that the parents are already known. The chain head header won't be updated in this function, the additional SetCanonical is expected in order to finish the entire procedure.

declarations.name: writeHeadersAndSetHead
declarations.doc: writeHeadersAndSetHead writes a batch of block headers and applies the last header as the chain head if the fork choicer says it's ok to update the chain. Note: This method is not concurrent-safe with inserting blocks simultaneously into the chain, as side effects caused by reorganisations cannot be emulated without the real blocks. Hence, writing headers directly should only be done in two scenarios: pure-header mode of operation (light clients), or properly separated header/block phases (non-archive clients).

declarations.name: DeleteBlockContentCallback
declarations.doc: DeleteBlockContentCallback is a callback function that is called by SetHead before each header is deleted.

declarations.name: HeaderChain
declarations.doc: HeaderChain implements the basic block header chain logic that is shared by core.BlockChain and light.LightChain. It is not usable in itself, only as a part of either structure. HeaderChain is responsible for maintaining the header chain including the header query and updating. The components maintained by headerchain includes: (1) total difficulty (2) header (3) block hash -> number mapping (4) canonical number -> hash mapping and (5) head header flag. It is not thread safe either, the encapsulating chain structures should do the necessary mutex locking/unlocking.

declarations.name: UpdateHeadBlocksCallback
declarations.doc: UpdateHeadBlocksCallback is a callback function that is called by SetHead before head header is updated. The method will return the actual block it updated the head to (missing state) and a flag if setHead should continue rewinding till that forcefully (exceeded ancient limits)

declarations.name: TestHeaderInsertion
declarations.doc: This test checks status reporting of InsertHeaderChain.

declarations.name: BenchmarkHashing
declarations.doc: BenchmarkHashing compares the speeds of hashing a rlp raw data directly without the unmarshalling/marshalling step

declarations.name: TestRlpIterator
declarations.doc: TestRlpIterator tests that individual transactions can be picked out from blocks without full unmarshalling/marshalling

declarations.name: Prefetch
declarations.doc: Prefetch processes the state changes according to the Ethereum rules by running the transaction messages using the statedb, but any changes are discarded. The only goal is to pre-cache transaction signatures and state trie nodes.

declarations.name: newStatePrefetcher
declarations.doc: newStatePrefetcher initialises a new statePrefetcher.

declarations.name: precacheTransaction
declarations.doc: precacheTransaction attempts to apply a transaction to the given state database and uses the input parameters for its environment. The goal is not to execute the transaction successfully, rather to warm up touched data slots.

declarations.name: statePrefetcher
declarations.doc: statePrefetcher is a basic Prefetcher, which blindly executes a block on top of an arbitrary state with the goal of prefetching potentially useful state data from disk before the main block processor start executing.

declarations.name: ApplyTransaction
declarations.doc: ApplyTransaction attempts to apply a transaction to the given state database and uses the input parameters for its environment. It returns the receipt for the transaction, gas used and an error if the transaction failed, indicating the block was invalid.

declarations.name: NewStateProcessor
declarations.doc: NewStateProcessor initialises a new StateProcessor.

declarations.name: Process
declarations.doc: Process processes the state changes according to the Ethereum rules by running the transaction messages using the statedb and applying any rewards to both the processor (coinbase) and any included uncles. Process returns the receipts and logs accumulated during the process and returns the amount of gas that was used in the process. If any of the transactions failed to execute due to insufficient gas it will return an error.

declarations.name: StateProcessor
declarations.doc: StateProcessor is a basic Processor, which takes care of transitioning state from one point to another. StateProcessor implements Processor.

declarations.name: GenerateBadBlock
declarations.doc: GenerateBadBlock constructs a "block" which contains the transactions. The transactions are not expected to be valid, and no proper post-state can be made. But from the perspective of the blockchain, the block is sufficiently valid to be considered for import: - valid pow (fake), ancestry, difficulty, gaslimit etc

declarations.name: TestStateProcessorErrors
declarations.doc: TestStateProcessorErrors tests the output from the 'core' errors as defined in core/error.go. These errors are generated when the blockchain imports bad blocks, meaning blocks which have valid headers but contain invalid transactions

declarations.name: ApplyMessage
declarations.doc: ApplyMessage computes the new state by applying the given message against the old state within the environment. ApplyMessage returns the bytes returned by any EVM execution (if it took place), the gas used (which includes gas refunds) and an error if it failed. An error always indicates a core error meaning that the message would always fail for that particular state and would never be accepted within a block.

declarations.name: Failed
declarations.doc: Failed returns the indicator whether the execution is successful or not

declarations.name: IntrinsicGas
declarations.doc: IntrinsicGas computes the 'intrinsic gas' for a message with the given data.

declarations.name: NewStateTransition
declarations.doc: NewStateTransition initialises and returns a new state transition object.

declarations.name: Return
declarations.doc: Return is a helper function to help caller distinguish between revert reason and function return. Return returns the data after execution if no error occurs.

declarations.name: Revert
declarations.doc: Revert returns the concrete revert reason if the execution is aborted by `REVERT` opcode. Note the reason can be nil if no data supplied with revert opcode.

declarations.name: TransitionDb
declarations.doc: TransitionDb will transition the state by applying the current message and returning the evm execution result with following fields. - used gas: total gas used (including gas being refunded) - returndata: the returned data from evm - concrete execution error: various **EVM** error which aborts the execution, e.g. ErrOutOfGas, ErrExecutionReverted However if any consensus issue encountered, return the error directly with nil evm execution result.

declarations.name: Unwrap
declarations.doc: Unwrap returns the internal evm error which allows us for further analysis outside.

declarations.name: gasUsed
declarations.doc: gasUsed returns the amount of gas used up by the state transition.

declarations.name: to
declarations.doc: to returns the recipient of the message.

declarations.name: ExecutionResult
declarations.doc: ExecutionResult includes all output after executing given evm message no matter the execution itself is successful or not.

declarations.name: Message
declarations.doc: Message represents a message sent to a contract.

declarations.name: StateTransition
declarations.doc: The State Transitioning Model A state transition is a change made when a transaction is applied to the current world state The state transitioning model does all the necessary work to work out a valid new state root. 1) Nonce handling 2) Pre pay gas 3) Create a new state object if the recipient is \0*32 4) Value transfer == If contract creation == 4a) Attempt to run transaction data 4b) If valid, use result as code for the new state object == end == 5) Run Script section 6) Derive new state root

declarations.name: cache
declarations.doc: cache is an infinite loop, caching transaction senders from various forms of data structures.

declarations.name: newTxSenderCacher
declarations.doc: newTxSenderCacher creates a new transaction sender background cacher and starts as many processing goroutines as allowed by the GOMAXPROCS on construction.

declarations.name: recover
declarations.doc: recover recovers the senders from a batch of transactions and caches them back into the same data structures. There is no validation being done, nor any reaction to invalid signatures. That is up to calling code later.

declarations.name: recoverFromBlocks
declarations.doc: recoverFromBlocks recovers the senders from a batch of blocks and caches them back into the same data structures. There is no validation being done, nor any reaction to invalid signatures. That is up to calling code later.

declarations.name: txSenderCacher
declarations.doc: txSenderCacher is a helper structure to concurrently ecrecover transaction senders from digital signatures on background threads.

declarations.name: txSenderCacherRequest
declarations.doc: txSenderCacherRequest is a request for recovering transaction senders with a specific signature scheme and caching it into the transactions themselves. The inc field defines the number of transactions to skip after each recovery, which is used to feed the same underlying input array to different threads but ensure they process the early transactions fast.

declarations.name: close
declarations.doc: close flushes the transaction journal contents to disk and closes the file.

declarations.name: insert
declarations.doc: insert adds the specified transaction to the local disk journal.

declarations.name: load
declarations.doc: load parses a transaction journal dump from disk, loading its contents into the specified pool.

declarations.name: newTxJournal
declarations.doc: newTxJournal creates a new transaction journal to

declarations.name: rotate
declarations.doc: rotate regenerates the transaction journal based on the current contents of the transaction pool.

declarations.name: devNull
declarations.doc: devNull is a WriteCloser that just discards anything written into it. Its goal is to allow the transaction journal to write into a fake journal when loading transactions on startup without printing warnings due to no file being read for write.

declarations.name: txJournal
declarations.doc: txJournal is a rotating log of transactions with the aim of storing locally created transactions to allow non-executed ones to survive node restarts.

declarations.name: Add
declarations.doc: Add tries to insert a new transaction into the list, returning whether the transaction was accepted, and if yes, any previous transaction it replaced. If the new transaction is accepted into the list, the lists' cost and gas thresholds are also potentially updated.

declarations.name: Cap
declarations.doc: Cap places a hard limit on the number of items, returning all transactions exceeding that limit.

declarations.name: Cap
declarations.doc: Cap places a hard limit on the number of items, returning all transactions exceeding that limit.

declarations.name: Discard
declarations.doc: Discard finds a number of most underpriced transactions, removes them from the priced list and returns them for further removal from the entire pool. Note local transaction won't be considered for eviction.

declarations.name: Empty
declarations.doc: Empty returns whether the list of transactions is empty or not.

declarations.name: Filter
declarations.doc: Filter removes all transactions from the list with a cost or gas limit higher than the provided thresholds. Every removed transaction is returned for any post-removal maintenance. Strict-mode invalidated transactions are also returned. This method uses the cached costcap and gascap to quickly decide if there's even a point in calculating all the costs or if the balance covers all. If the threshold is lower than the costgas cap, the caps will be reset to a new high after removing the newly invalidated transactions.

declarations.name: Filter
declarations.doc: Filter iterates over the list of transactions and removes all of them for which the specified function evaluates to true. Filter, as opposed to 'filter', re-initialises the heap after the operation is done. If you want to do several consecutive filterings, it's therefore better to first do a .filter(func1) followed by .Filter(func2) or reheap()

declarations.name: Flatten
declarations.doc: Flatten creates a nonce-sorted slice of transactions based on the loosely sorted internal representation. The result of the sorting is cached in case it's requested again before any modifications are made to the contents.

declarations.name: Flatten
declarations.doc: Flatten creates a nonce-sorted slice of transactions based on the loosely sorted internal representation. The result of the sorting is cached in case it's requested again before any modifications are made to the contents.

declarations.name: Forward
declarations.doc: Forward removes all transactions from the list with a nonce lower than the provided threshold. Every removed transaction is returned for any post-removal maintenance.

declarations.name: Forward
declarations.doc: Forward removes all transactions from the map with a nonce lower than the provided threshold. Every removed transaction is returned for any post-removal maintenance.

declarations.name: Get
declarations.doc: Get retrieves the current transactions associated with the given nonce.

declarations.name: LastElement
declarations.doc: LastElement returns the last element of a flattened list, thus, the transaction with the highest nonce

declarations.name: LastElement
declarations.doc: LastElement returns the last element of a flattened list, thus, the transaction with the highest nonce

declarations.name: Len
declarations.doc: Len returns the length of the transaction list.

declarations.name: Len
declarations.doc: Len returns the length of the transaction map.

declarations.name: Overlaps
declarations.doc: Overlaps returns whether the transaction specified has the same nonce as one already contained within the list.

declarations.name: Put
declarations.doc: Put inserts a new transaction into the heap.

declarations.name: Put
declarations.doc: Put inserts a new transaction into the map, also updating the map's nonce index. If a transaction already exists with the same nonce, it's overwritten.

declarations.name: Ready
declarations.doc: Ready retrieves a sequentially increasing list of transactions starting at the provided nonce that is ready for processing. The returned transactions will be removed from the list. Note, all transactions with nonces lower than start will also be returned to prevent getting into and invalid state. This is not something that should ever happen but better to be self correcting than failing!

declarations.name: Ready
declarations.doc: Ready retrieves a sequentially increasing list of transactions starting at the provided nonce that is ready for processing. The returned transactions will be removed from the list. Note, all transactions with nonces lower than start will also be returned to prevent getting into and invalid state. This is not something that should ever happen but better to be self correcting than failing!

declarations.name: Reheap
declarations.doc: Reheap forcibly rebuilds the heap based on the current remote transaction set.

declarations.name: Remove
declarations.doc: Remove deletes a transaction from the maintained list, returning whether the transaction was found, and also returning any transaction invalidated due to the deletion (strict mode only).

declarations.name: Remove
declarations.doc: Remove deletes a transaction from the maintained map, returning whether the transaction was found.

declarations.name: Removed
declarations.doc: Removed notifies the prices transaction list that an old transaction dropped from the pool. The list will just keep a counter of stale objects and update the heap if a large enough ratio of transactions go stale.

declarations.name: SetBaseFee
declarations.doc: SetBaseFee updates the base fee and triggers a re-heap. Note that Removed is not necessary to call right before SetBaseFee when processing a new block.

declarations.name: Underpriced
declarations.doc: Underpriced checks whether a transaction is cheaper than (or as cheap as) the lowest priced (remote) transaction currently being tracked.

declarations.name: filter
declarations.doc: filter is identical to Filter, but **does not** regenerate the heap. This method should only be used if followed immediately by a call to Filter or reheap()

declarations.name: newTxList
declarations.doc: newTxList create a new transaction list for maintaining nonce-indexable fast, gapped, sortable transaction lists.

declarations.name: newTxPricedList
declarations.doc: newTxPricedList creates a new price-sorted transaction heap.

declarations.name: newTxSortedMap
declarations.doc: newTxSortedMap creates a new nonce-sorted transaction map.

declarations.name: underpricedFor
declarations.doc: underpricedFor checks whether a transaction is cheaper than (or as cheap as) the lowest priced (remote) transaction in the given heap.

declarations.name: nonceHeap
declarations.doc: nonceHeap is a heap.Interface implementation over 64bit unsigned integers for retrieving sorted transactions from the possibly gapped future queue.

declarations.name: priceHeap
declarations.doc: priceHeap is a heap.Interface implementation over transactions for retrieving price-sorted transactions to discard when the pool fills up. If baseFee is set then the heap is sorted based on the effective tip based on the given base fee. If baseFee is nil then the sorting is based on gasFeeCap.

declarations.name: txList
declarations.doc: txList is a "list" of transactions belonging to an account, sorted by account nonce. The same type can be used both for storing contiguous transactions for the executable/pending queue; and for storing gapped transactions for the non- executable/future queue, with minor behavioral changes.

declarations.name: txPricedList
declarations.doc: txPricedList is a price-sorted heap to allow operating on transactions pool contents in a price-incrementing way. It's built opon the all transactions in txpool but only interested in the remote part. It means only remote transactions will be considered for tracking, sorting, eviction, etc. Two heaps are used for sorting: the urgent heap (based on effective tip in the next block) and the floating heap (based on gasFeeCap). Always the bigger heap is chosen for eviction. Transactions evicted from the urgent heap are first demoted into the floating heap. In some cases (during a congestion, when blocks are full) the urgent heap can provide better candidates for inclusion while in other cases (at the top of the baseFee peak) the floating heap is better. When baseFee is decreasing they behave similarly.

declarations.name: txSortedMap
declarations.doc: txSortedMap is a nonce->transaction hash map with a heap based index to allow iterating over the contents in a nonce-incrementing way.

declarations.name: TestStrictTxListAdd
declarations.doc: Tests that transactions can be added to strict lists and list contents and nonce boundaries are correctly maintained.

declarations.name: get
declarations.doc: get returns the current nonce of an account, falling back to a real state database if the account is unknown.

declarations.name: newTxNoncer
declarations.doc: newTxNoncer creates a new virtual state database to track the pool nonces.

declarations.name: set
declarations.doc: set inserts a new virtual nonce into the virtual state database to be returned whenever the pool requests it instead of reaching into the real state database.

declarations.name: setAll
declarations.doc: setAll sets the nonces for all accounts to the given map.

declarations.name: setIfLower
declarations.doc: setIfLower updates a new virtual nonce into the virtual state database if the the new one is lower.

declarations.name: txNoncer
declarations.doc: txNoncer is a tiny virtual state database to manage the executable nonces of accounts in the pool, falling back to reading from a real state database if an account is unknown.

declarations.name: Add
declarations.doc: Add adds a transaction to the lookup.

declarations.name: AddLocal
declarations.doc: AddLocal enqueues a single local transaction into the pool if it is valid. This is a convenience wrapper aroundd AddLocals.

declarations.name: AddLocals
declarations.doc: AddLocals enqueues a batch of transactions into the pool if they are valid, marking the senders as a local ones, ensuring they go around the local pricing constraints. This method is used to add transactions from the RPC API and performs synchronous pool reorganization and event propagation.

declarations.name: AddRemote
declarations.doc: AddRemote enqueues a single transaction into the pool if it is valid. This is a convenience wrapper around AddRemotes. Deprecated: use AddRemotes

declarations.name: AddRemotes
declarations.doc: AddRemotes enqueues a batch of transactions into the pool if they are valid. If the senders are not among the locally tracked ones, full pricing constraints will apply. This method is used to add transactions from the p2p network and does not wait for pool reorganization and internal event propagation.

declarations.name: AddRemotesSync
declarations.doc: This is like AddRemotes, but waits for pool reorganization. Tests use this method.

declarations.name: Content
declarations.doc: Content retrieves the data content of the transaction pool, returning all the pending as well as queued transactions, grouped by account and sorted by nonce.

declarations.name: ContentFrom
declarations.doc: ContentFrom retrieves the data content of the transaction pool, returning the pending as well as queued transactions of this address, grouped by nonce.

declarations.name: Count
declarations.doc: Count returns the current number of transactions in the lookup.

declarations.name: GasPrice
declarations.doc: GasPrice returns the current gas price enforced by the transaction pool.

declarations.name: Get
declarations.doc: Get returns a transaction if it is contained in the pool and nil otherwise.

declarations.name: Get
declarations.doc: Get returns a transaction if it exists in the lookup, or nil if not found.

declarations.name: GetLocal
declarations.doc: GetLocal returns a transaction if it exists in the lookup, or nil if not found.

declarations.name: GetRemote
declarations.doc: GetRemote returns a transaction if it exists in the lookup, or nil if not found.

declarations.name: Has
declarations.doc: Has returns an indicator whether txpool has a transaction cached with the given hash.

declarations.name: LocalCount
declarations.doc: LocalCount returns the current number of local transactions in the lookup.

declarations.name: Locals
declarations.doc: Locals retrieves the accounts currently considered local by the pool.

declarations.name: NewTxPool
declarations.doc: NewTxPool creates a new transaction pool to gather, sort and filter inbound transactions from the network.

declarations.name: Nonce
declarations.doc: Nonce returns the next nonce of an account, with all transactions executable by the pool already applied on top.

declarations.name: Pending
declarations.doc: Pending retrieves all currently processable transactions, grouped by origin account and sorted by nonce. The returned transaction set is a copy and can be freely modified by calling code. The enforceTips parameter can be used to do an extra filtering on the pending transactions and only return those whose **effective** tip is large enough in the next pending execution environment.

declarations.name: PendingEmpty
declarations.doc: Checks if txpool.pending is empty or not

declarations.name: PendingOne
declarations.doc: Checks if txpool.pending has exactly one entry

declarations.name: Range
declarations.doc: Range calls f on each key and value present in the map. The callback passed should return the indicator whether the iteration needs to be continued. Callers need to specify which set (or both) to be iterated.

declarations.name: RemoteCount
declarations.doc: RemoteCount returns the current number of remote transactions in the lookup.

declarations.name: RemoteToLocals
declarations.doc: RemoteToLocals migrates the transactions belongs to the given locals to locals set. The assumption is held the locals set is thread-safe to be used.

declarations.name: RemotesBelowTip
declarations.doc: RemotesBelowTip finds all remote transactions below the given tip threshold.

declarations.name: Remove
declarations.doc: Remove removes a transaction from the lookup.

declarations.name: SetGasPrice
declarations.doc: SetGasPrice updates the minimum price required by the transaction pool for a new transaction, and drops all transactions below this threshold.

declarations.name: Slots
declarations.doc: Slots returns the current number of slots used in the lookup.

declarations.name: Stats
declarations.doc: Stats retrieves the current pool stats, namely the number of pending and the number of queued (non-executable) transactions.

declarations.name: Status
declarations.doc: Status returns the status (unknown/pending/queued) of a batch of transactions identified by their hashes.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop terminates the transaction pool.

declarations.name: SubscribeNewTxsEvent
declarations.doc: SubscribeNewTxsEvent registers a subscription of NewTxsEvent and starts sending event to the given channel.

declarations.name: add
declarations.doc: add validates a transaction and inserts it into the non-executable queue for later pending promotion and execution. If the transaction is a replacement for an already pending or queued one, it overwrites the previous transaction if its price is higher. If a newly added transaction is marked as local, its sending account will be be added to the allowlist, preventing any associated transaction from being dropped out of the pool due to pricing constraints.

declarations.name: add
declarations.doc: add inserts a new address into the set to track.

declarations.name: addRemoteSync
declarations.doc: This is like AddRemotes with a single transaction, but waits for pool reorganization. Tests use this method.

declarations.name: addTx
declarations.doc: addTx adds the sender of tx into the set.

declarations.name: addTxs
declarations.doc: addTxs attempts to queue a batch of transactions if they are valid.

declarations.name: addTxsLocked
declarations.doc: addTxsLocked attempts to queue a batch of transactions if they are valid. The transaction pool lock must be held.

declarations.name: contains
declarations.doc: contains checks if a given address is contained within the set.

declarations.name: containsTx
declarations.doc: containsTx checks if the sender of a given tx is within the set. If the sender cannot be derived, this method returns false.

declarations.name: demoteUnexecutables
declarations.doc: demoteUnexecutables removes invalid and processed transactions from the pools executable/pending queue and any subsequent transactions that become unexecutable are moved back into the future queue. Note: transactions are not marked as removed in the priced list because re-heaping is always explicitly triggered by SetBaseFee and it would be unnecessary and wasteful to trigger a re-heap is this function

declarations.name: enqueueTx
declarations.doc: enqueueTx inserts a new transaction into the non-executable transaction queue. Note, this method assumes the pool lock is held!

declarations.name: flatten
declarations.doc: flatten returns the list of addresses within this set, also caching it for later reuse. The returned slice should not be changed!

declarations.name: journalTx
declarations.doc: journalTx adds the specified transaction to the local disk journal if it is deemed to have been sent from a local account.

declarations.name: local
declarations.doc: local retrieves all currently known local transactions, grouped by origin account and sorted by nonce. The returned transaction set is a copy and can be freely modified by calling code.

declarations.name: loop
declarations.doc: loop is the transaction pool's main event loop, waiting for and reacting to outside blockchain events as well as for various reporting and transaction eviction events.

declarations.name: merge
declarations.doc: merge adds all addresses from the 'other' set into 'as'.

declarations.name: newAccountSet
declarations.doc: newAccountSet creates a new address set with an associated signer for sender derivations.

declarations.name: newTxLookup
declarations.doc: newTxLookup returns a new txLookup structure.

declarations.name: numSlots
declarations.doc: numSlots calculates the number of slots needed for a single transaction.

declarations.name: promoteExecutables
declarations.doc: promoteExecutables moves transactions that have become processable from the future queue to the set of pending transactions. During this process, all invalidated transactions (low nonce, low balance) are deleted.

declarations.name: promoteTx
declarations.doc: promoteTx adds a transaction to the pending (processable) list of transactions and returns whether it was inserted or an older was better. Note, this method assumes the pool lock is held!

declarations.name: queueTxEvent
declarations.doc: queueTxEvent enqueues a transaction event to be sent in the next reorg run.

declarations.name: removeTx
declarations.doc: removeTx removes a single transaction from the queue, moving all subsequent transactions back to the future queue.

declarations.name: requestPromoteExecutables
declarations.doc: requestPromoteExecutables requests transaction promotion checks for the given addresses. The returned channel is closed when the promotion checks have occurred.

declarations.name: requestReset
declarations.doc: requestReset requests a pool reset to the new head block. The returned channel is closed when the reset has occurred.

declarations.name: reset
declarations.doc: reset retrieves the current state of the blockchain and ensures the content of the transaction pool is valid with regard to the chain state.

declarations.name: runReorg
declarations.doc: runReorg runs reset and promoteExecutables on behalf of scheduleReorgLoop.

declarations.name: sanitize
declarations.doc: sanitize checks the provided user configurations and changes anything that's unreasonable or unworkable.

declarations.name: scheduleReorgLoop
declarations.doc: scheduleReorgLoop schedules runs of reset and promoteExecutables. Code above should not call those methods directly, but request them being run using requestReset and requestPromoteExecutables instead.

declarations.name: stats
declarations.doc: stats retrieves the current pool stats, namely the number of pending and the number of queued (non-executable) transactions.

declarations.name: truncatePending
declarations.doc: truncatePending removes transactions from the pending queue if the pool is above the pending limit. The algorithm tries to reduce transaction counts by an approximately equal number for all for accounts with many pending transactions.

declarations.name: truncateQueue
declarations.doc: truncateQueue drops the oldes transactions in the queue if the pool is above the global queue limit.

declarations.name: validateTx
declarations.doc: validateTx checks whether a transaction is valid according to the consensus rules and adheres to some heuristic limits of the local node (price and size).

declarations.name: TxPool
declarations.doc: TxPool contains all currently known transactions. Transactions enter the pool when they are received from the network or submitted locally. They exit the pool when they are included in the blockchain. The pool separates processable transactions (which can be applied to the current state) and future transactions. Transactions move between those two states over time as they are received and processed.

declarations.name: TxPoolConfig
declarations.doc: TxPoolConfig are the configuration parameters of the transaction pool.

declarations.name: TxStatus
declarations.doc: TxStatus is the current status of a transaction as seen by the pool.

declarations.name: accountSet
declarations.doc: accountSet is simply a set of addresses to check for existence, and a signer capable of deriving addresses from transactions.

declarations.name: addressByHeartbeat
declarations.doc: addressByHeartbeat is an account address tagged with its last activity timestamp.

declarations.name: blockChain
declarations.doc: blockChain provides the state of blockchain and current gas limit to do some pre checks in tx pool and event subscribers.

declarations.name: txLookup
declarations.doc: txLookup is used internally by TxPool to track transactions while allowing lookup without mutex contention. Note, although this type is properly protected against concurrent access, it is **not** a type that should ever be mutated or even exposed outside of the transaction pool, since its internal state is tightly coupled with the pools internal mechanisms. The sole purpose of the type is to permit out-of-bound peeking into the pool in TxPool.Get without having to acquire the widely scoped TxPool.mu mutex. This lookup set combines the notion of "local transactions", which is useful to build upper-level structure.

declarations.name: BenchmarkFuturePromotion100
declarations.doc: Benchmarks the speed of scheduling the contents of the future queue of the transaction pool.

declarations.name: BenchmarkPendingDemotion100
declarations.doc: Benchmarks the speed of validating the contents of the pending queue of the transaction pool.

declarations.name: BenchmarkPoolBatchInsert100
declarations.doc: Benchmarks the speed of batched transaction insertion.

declarations.name: BenchmarkPoolMultiAccountBatchInsert
declarations.doc: Benchmarks the speed of batch transaction insertion in case of multiple accounts.

declarations.name: State
declarations.doc: testChain.State() is used multiple times to reset the pending state. when simulate is true it will create a state that indicates that tx0 and tx1 are included in the chain.

declarations.name: TestDualHeapEviction
declarations.doc: Tests whether highest fee cap transaction is retained after a batch of high effective tip transactions are added and vice versa

declarations.name: TestStateChangeDuringTransactionPoolReset
declarations.doc: This test simulates a scenario where a new block is imported during a state reset and tests whether the pending state is in sync with the block head event that initiated the resetState().

declarations.name: TestTransactionAllowedTxSize
declarations.doc: Test the limit on transaction size is enforced correctly. This test verifies every transaction having allowed size is added to the pool, and longer transactions are rejected.

declarations.name: TestTransactionCapClearsFromAll
declarations.doc: Tests that if transactions start being capped, transactions are also removed from 'all'

declarations.name: TestTransactionDeduplication
declarations.doc: Tests that the pool rejects duplicate transactions.

declarations.name: TestTransactionDropping
declarations.doc: Tests that if an account runs out of funds, any pending and queued transactions are dropped.

declarations.name: TestTransactionGapFilling
declarations.doc: Tests that if the transaction pool has both executable and non-executable transactions from an origin account, filling the nonce gap moves all queued ones into the pending pool.

declarations.name: TestTransactionJournaling
declarations.doc: Tests that local transactions are journaled to disk, but remote transactions get discarded between restarts.

declarations.name: TestTransactionPendingGlobalLimiting
declarations.doc: Tests that if the transaction count belonging to multiple accounts go above some hard threshold, the higher transactions are dropped to prevent DOS attacks.

declarations.name: TestTransactionPendingLimiting
declarations.doc: Tests that even if the transaction count belonging to a single account goes above some threshold, as long as the transactions are executable, they are accepted.

declarations.name: TestTransactionPendingMinimumAllowance
declarations.doc: Tests that if the transaction count belonging to multiple accounts go above some hard threshold, if they are under the minimum guaranteed slot count then the transactions are still kept.

declarations.name: TestTransactionPoolRepricing
declarations.doc: Tests that setting the transaction pool gas price to a higher value correctly discards everything cheaper than that and moves any gapped transactions back from the pending pool to the queue. Note, local transactions are never allowed to be dropped.

declarations.name: TestTransactionPoolRepricingDynamicFee
declarations.doc: Tests that setting the transaction pool gas price to a higher value correctly discards everything cheaper (legacy & dynamic fee) than that and moves any gapped transactions back from the pending pool to the queue. Note, local transactions are never allowed to be dropped.

declarations.name: TestTransactionPoolRepricingKeepsLocals
declarations.doc: Tests that setting the transaction pool gas price to a higher value does not remove local transactions (legacy & dynamic fee).

declarations.name: TestTransactionPoolStableUnderpricing
declarations.doc: Tests that more expensive transactions push out cheap ones from the pool, but without producing instability by creating gaps that start jumping transactions back and forth between queued/pending.

declarations.name: TestTransactionPoolUnderpricing
declarations.doc: Tests that when the pool reaches its global transaction limit, underpriced transactions are gradually shifted out for more expensive ones and any gapped pending transactions are moved into the queue. Note, local transactions are never allowed to be dropped.

declarations.name: TestTransactionPoolUnderpricingDynamicFee
declarations.doc: Tests that when the pool reaches its global transaction limit, underpriced transactions (legacy & dynamic fee) are gradually shifted out for more expensive ones and any gapped pending transactions are moved into the queue. Note, local transactions are never allowed to be dropped.

declarations.name: TestTransactionPostponing
declarations.doc: Tests that if a transaction is dropped from the current pending pool (e.g. out of fund), all consecutive (still valid, but not executable) transactions are postponed back into the future queue to prevent broadcasting them.

declarations.name: TestTransactionQueueAccountLimiting
declarations.doc: Tests that if the transaction count belonging to a single account goes above some threshold, the higher transactions are dropped to prevent DOS attacks.

declarations.name: TestTransactionQueueGlobalLimiting
declarations.doc: Tests that if the transaction count belonging to multiple accounts go above some threshold, the higher transactions are dropped to prevent DOS attacks. This logic should not hold for local transactions, unless the local tracking mechanism is disabled.

declarations.name: TestTransactionQueueTimeLimiting
declarations.doc: Tests that if an account remains idle for a prolonged amount of time, any non-executable transactions queued up are dropped to prevent wasting resources on shuffling them around. This logic should not hold for local transactions, unless the local tracking mechanism is disabled.

declarations.name: TestTransactionReplacement
declarations.doc: Tests that the pool rejects replacement transactions that don't meet the minimum price bump required.

declarations.name: TestTransactionReplacementDynamicFee
declarations.doc: Tests that the pool rejects replacement dynamic fee transactions that don't meet the minimum price bump required.

declarations.name: TestTransactionSlotCount
declarations.doc: Test the transaction slots consumption is computed correctly

declarations.name: TestTransactionStatusCheck
declarations.doc: TestTransactionStatusCheck tests that the pool can correctly retrieve the pending status of individual transactions.

declarations.name: validateEvents
declarations.doc: validateEvents checks that the correct number of transaction addition events were fired on the pool's event feed.

declarations.name: validateTxPoolInternals
declarations.doc: validateTxPoolInternals checks various consistency invariants within the pool.

declarations.name: NewSenderResolver
declarations.doc: NewSenderResolver creates a new sender resolver worker pool

declarations.name: Post
declarations.doc: Post a new sender resolver task

declarations.name: ResolveSender
declarations.doc: ResolveSender resolves sender address from a transaction

declarations.name: ResolveSenders
declarations.doc: ResolveSenders resolves sender accounts from given transactions concurrently using SenderResolver worker pool.

declarations.name: Run
declarations.doc: sender resolver main loop

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop stops sender resolver

declarations.name: SenderResolver
declarations.doc: SenderResolver resolves sender accounts from transactions concurrently with worker threads

declarations.name: job
declarations.doc: job structure is needed because param is necessary due to evaluation order uncertainty with closure and channel.

declarations.name: Prefetcher
declarations.doc: Prefetcher is an interface for pre-caching transaction signatures and state.

declarations.name: Processor
declarations.doc: Processor is an interface for processing blocks using a given initial state.

declarations.name: Validator
declarations.doc: Validator is an interface which defines the standard for block validation. It is only responsible for validating block contents, as the header validation is done by the specific consensus engines.

declarations.name: Arg
declarations.doc: Arg returns the argument of the current instruction.

declarations.name: Disassemble
declarations.doc: Disassemble returns all disassembled EVM instructions in human-readable format.

declarations.name: Error
declarations.doc: Error returns any error that may have been encountered.

declarations.name: NewInstructionIterator
declarations.doc: NewInstructionIterator create a new instruction iterator.

declarations.name: Next
declarations.doc: Next returns true if there is a next instruction and moves on.

declarations.name: Op
declarations.doc: Op returns the opcode of the current instruction.

declarations.name: PC
declarations.doc: PC returns the PC of the current instruction.

declarations.name: PrintDisassembled
declarations.doc: PrintDisassembled pretty-print all disassembled EVM instructions to stdout.

declarations.name: instructionIterator
declarations.doc: Iterator for disassembled EVM instructions

declarations.name: TestInstructionIteratorEmpty
declarations.doc: Tests disassembling the instructions for empty evm code

declarations.name: TestInstructionIteratorInvalid
declarations.doc: Tests disassembling the instructions for invalid evm code

declarations.name: TestInstructionIteratorValid
declarations.doc: Tests disassembling the instructions for valid evm code

declarations.name: Compile
declarations.doc: Compile compiles the current tokens and returns a binary string that can be interpreted by the EVM and an error if it failed. compile is the second stage in the compile phase which compiles the tokens to EVM instructions.

declarations.name: Feed
declarations.doc: Feed feeds tokens in to ch and are interpreted by the compiler. feed is the first pass in the compile stage as it collects the used labels in the program and keeps a program counter which is used to determine the locations of the jump dests. The labels can than be used in the second stage to push labels and determine the right position.

declarations.name: NewCompiler
declarations.doc: NewCompiler returns a new allocated compiler.

declarations.name: compileElement
declarations.doc: compileElement compiles the element (push & label or both) to a binary representation and may error if incorrect statements where fed.

declarations.name: compileLabel
declarations.doc: compileLabel pushes a jumpdest to the binary slice.

declarations.name: compileLine
declarations.doc: compileLine compiles a single line instruction e.g. "push 1", "jump @label".

declarations.name: compileNumber
declarations.doc: compileNumber compiles the number to bytes

declarations.name: isJump
declarations.doc: isJump returns whether the string op is jump(i)

declarations.name: isPush
declarations.doc: isPush returns whether the string op is either any of push(N).

declarations.name: next
declarations.doc: next returns the next token and increments the position.

declarations.name: pushBin
declarations.doc: pushBin pushes the value v to the binary stack.

declarations.name: toBinary
declarations.doc: toBinary converts text to a vm.OpCode

declarations.name: Compiler
declarations.doc: Compiler contains information about the parsed source and holds the tokens for the program.

declarations.name: Lex
declarations.doc: Lex lexes the program by name with the given source. It returns a channel on which the tokens are delivered.

declarations.name: String
declarations.doc: String implements stringer

declarations.name: accept
declarations.doc: Accepts checks whether the given input matches the next rune

declarations.name: acceptRun
declarations.doc: acceptRun will continue to advance the seeker until valid can no longer be met.

declarations.name: acceptRunUntil
declarations.doc: acceptRunUntil is the inverse of acceptRun and will continue to advance the seeker until the rune has been found.

declarations.name: backup
declarations.doc: backup backsup the last parsed element (multi-character)

declarations.name: blob
declarations.doc: blob returns the current value

declarations.name: emit
declarations.doc: Emits a new token on to token channel for processing

declarations.name: ignore
declarations.doc: ignore advances the seeker and ignores the value

declarations.name: lexComment
declarations.doc: lexComment parses the current position until the end of the line and discards the text.

declarations.name: lexInsideString
declarations.doc: lexInsideString lexes the inside of a string until the state function finds the closing quote. It returns the lex text state function.

declarations.name: lexLabel
declarations.doc: lexLabel parses the current label, emits and returns the lex text state function to advance the parsing process.

declarations.name: lexLine
declarations.doc: lexLine is state function for lexing lines

declarations.name: next
declarations.doc: next returns the next rune in the program's source.

declarations.name: peek
declarations.doc: peek returns the next rune but does not advance the seeker

declarations.name: lexer
declarations.doc: lexer is the basic construct for parsing source code and turning them in to tokens. Tokens are interpreted by the compiler.

declarations.name: stateFn
declarations.doc: stateFn is used through the lifetime of the lexer to parse the different values at the current state.

declarations.name: token
declarations.doc: token is emitted when the lexer has discovered a new parsable token. These are delivered over the tokens channels of the lexer

declarations.name: tokenType
declarations.doc: tokenType are the different types the lexer is able to parse and return.

declarations.name: With
declarations.doc: With returns a copy of the error with a new embedded custom data field.

declarations.name: EngineAPIError
declarations.doc: EngineAPIError is a standardized error message between consensus and execution clients, also containing any custom error message Geth might include.

declarations.name: MarshalJSON
declarations.doc: MarshalJSON marshals as JSON.

declarations.name: UnmarshalJSON
declarations.doc: UnmarshalJSON unmarshals from JSON.

declarations.name: MarshalJSON
declarations.doc: MarshalJSON marshals as JSON.

declarations.name: UnmarshalJSON
declarations.doc: UnmarshalJSON unmarshals from JSON.

declarations.name: BlockToExecutableData
declarations.doc: BlockToExecutableData constructs the executableDataV1 structure by filling the fields from the given block. It assumes the given block is post-merge block.

declarations.name: ExecutableDataToBlock
declarations.doc: ExecutableDataToBlock constructs a block from executable data. It verifies that the following fields: len(extraData) <= 32 uncleHash = emptyUncleHash difficulty = 0 and that the blockhash of the constructed block matches the parameters.

declarations.name: ExecutableDataV1
declarations.doc: ExecutableDataV1 structure described at https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/src/engine/specification.md

declarations.name: PayloadAttributesV1
declarations.doc: PayloadAttributesV1 structure described at https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/74

declarations.name: PayloadID
declarations.doc: PayloadID is an identifier of the payload build process

declarations.name: executableDataMarshaling
declarations.doc: JSON type overrides for executableData.

declarations.name: payloadAttributesMarshaling
declarations.doc: JSON type overrides for PayloadAttributesV1.

declarations.name: AddBloom
declarations.doc: AddBloom takes a single bloom filter and sets the corresponding bit column in memory accordingly.

declarations.name: Bitset
declarations.doc: Bitset returns the bit vector belonging to the given bit index after all blooms have been added.

declarations.name: NewGenerator
declarations.doc: NewGenerator creates a rotated bloom generator that can iteratively fill a batched bloom filter's bits.

declarations.name: Generator
declarations.doc: Generator takes a number of bloom filters and generates the rotated bloom bits to be used for batched filtering.

declarations.name: TestGenerator
declarations.doc: Tests that batched bloom bits are correctly rotated from the input bloom filters.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close stops the matching process and waits for all subprocesses to terminate before returning. The timeout may be used for graceful shutdown, allowing the currently running retrievals to complete before this time.

declarations.name: Error
declarations.doc: Error returns any failure encountered during the matching session.

declarations.name: Multiplex
declarations.doc: Multiplex polls the matcher session for retrieval tasks and multiplexes it into the requested retrieval queue to be serviced together with other sessions. This method will block for the lifetime of the session. Even after termination of the session, any request in-flight need to be responded to! Empty responses are fine though in that case.

declarations.name: NewMatcher
declarations.doc: NewMatcher creates a new pipeline for retrieving bloom bit streams and doing address and topic filtering on them. Setting a filter component to `nil` is allowed and will result in that filter rule being skipped (OR 0x11...1).

declarations.name: Start
declarations.doc: Start starts the matching process and returns a stream of bloom matches in a given range of blocks. If there are no more matches in the range, the result channel is closed.

declarations.name: addScheduler
declarations.doc: addScheduler adds a bit stream retrieval scheduler for the given bit index if it has not existed before. If the bit is already selected for filtering, the existing scheduler can be used.

declarations.name: allocateRetrieval
