declarations.doc: allocateRetrieval assigns a bloom bit index to a client process that can either immediately request and fetch the section contents assigned to this bit or wait a little while for more sections to be requested.

declarations.name: allocateSections
declarations.doc: allocateSections assigns all or part of an already allocated bit-task queue to the requesting process.

declarations.name: calcBloomIndexes
declarations.doc: calcBloomIndexes returns the bloom filter bit indexes belonging to the given key.

declarations.name: deliverSections
declarations.doc: deliverSections delivers a batch of section bit-vectors for a specific bloom bit index to be injected into the processing pipeline.

declarations.name: distributor
declarations.doc: distributor receives requests from the schedulers and queues them into a set of pending requests, which are assigned to retrievers wanting to fulfil them.

declarations.name: pendingSections
declarations.doc: pendingSections returns the number of pending section retrievals belonging to the given bloom bit index.

declarations.name: run
declarations.doc: run creates a daisy-chain of sub-matchers, one for the address set and one for each topic set, each sub-matcher receiving a section only if the previous ones have all found a potential match in one of the blocks of the section, then binary AND-ing its own matches and forwarding the result to the next one. The method starts feeding the section indexes into the first sub-matcher on a new goroutine and returns a sink channel receiving the results.

declarations.name: subMatch
declarations.doc: subMatch creates a sub-matcher that filters for a set of addresses or topics, binary OR-s those matches, then binary AND-s the result to the daisy-chain input (source) and forwards it to the daisy-chain output. The matches of each address/topic are calculated by fetching the given sections of the three bloom bit indexes belonging to that address/topic, and binary AND-ing those vectors together.

declarations.name: Matcher
declarations.doc: Matcher is a pipelined system of schedulers and logic matchers which perform binary AND/OR operations on the bit-streams, creating a stream of potential blocks to inspect for data content.

declarations.name: MatcherSession
declarations.doc: MatcherSession is returned by a started matcher to be used as a terminator for the actively running matching operation.

declarations.name: Retrieval
declarations.doc: Retrieval represents a request for retrieval task assignments for a given bit with the given number of fetch elements, or a response for such a request. It can also have the actual results set to be used as a delivery data struct. The contest and error fields are used by the light client to terminate matching early if an error is encountered on some path of the pipeline.

declarations.name: bloomIndexes
declarations.doc: bloomIndexes represents the bit indexes inside the bloom filter that belong to some key.

declarations.name: partialMatches
declarations.doc: partialMatches with a non-nil vector represents a section in which some sub- matchers have already found potential matches. Subsequent sub-matchers will binary AND their matches with this vector. If vector is nil, it represents a section to be processed by the first sub-matcher.

declarations.name: TestMatcherContinuous
declarations.doc: Tests the matcher pipeline on a single continuous workflow without interrupts.

declarations.name: TestMatcherIntermittent
declarations.doc: Tests the matcher pipeline on a constantly interrupted and resumed work pattern with the aim of ensuring data items are requested only once.

declarations.name: TestMatcherRandom
declarations.doc: Tests the matcher pipeline on random input to hopefully catch anomalies.

declarations.name: TestMatcherShifted
declarations.doc: Tests that the matcher can properly find matches if the starting block is shifter from a multiple of 8. This is needed to cover an optimisation with bitset matching https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/15309.

declarations.name: TestMatcherWildcards
declarations.doc: Tests that wildcard filter rules (nil) can be specified and are handled well.

declarations.name: TestWildcardMatcher
declarations.doc: Tests that matching on everything doesn't crash (special case internally).

declarations.name: generateBitset
declarations.doc: generateBitset generates the rotated bitset for the given bloom bit and section numbers.

declarations.name: makeRandomIndexes
declarations.doc: makeRandomIndexes generates a random filter system, composed on multiple filter criteria, each having one bloom list component for the address and arbitrarily many topic bloom list components.

declarations.name: startRetrievers
declarations.doc: startRetrievers starts a batch of goroutines listening for section requests and serving them.

declarations.name: testMatcher

Since this method operates in head-towards-genesis mode, it will return an empty slice in case the head ('number') is missing. declarations.name: IndexTransactions
declarations.doc: IndexTransactions creates txlookup indices of the specified block range. The from is included while to is excluded. This function iterates canonical chain in reverse order, it has one main advantage: We can write tx index tail flag periodically even without the whole indexing procedure is finished. So that we can resume indexing procedure next time quickly. There is a passed channel, the whole procedure will be interrupted if any signal received.

declarations.name: NewFreezer
declarations.doc: NewFreezer creates a freezer instance for maintaining immutable ordered data according to the given parameters. The 'tables' argument defines the data tables. If the value of a map entry is true, snappy compression is disabled for the table.

declarations.name: ReadAncients

declarations.name: Sync

declarations.name: Tail

declarations.doc: repair truncates all data tables to the same length.

declarations.name: validate
declarations.doc: validate checks that every table has the same length. Used instead of `repair` in readonly mode.

declarations.name: Freezer
declarations.doc: Freezer is a memory mapped append-only database to store immutable ordered data into flat files: - The append-only nature ensures that disk writes are minimized. - The memory mapping ensures we can max out system memory for caching without reserving it for go-ethereum. This would also reduce the memory requirements of Geth, and thus also GC overhead.

declarations.name: convertLegacyFn
declarations.doc: convertLegacyFn takes a raw freezer entry in an older format and returns it in the new format.

declarations.name: Append
declarations.doc: Append adds an RLP-encoded item of the given kind.

declarations.name: Append
declarations.doc: Append rlp-encodes and adds data at the end of the freezer table. The item number is a precautionary parameter to ensure data correctness, but the table will reject already existing data.

declarations.name: AppendRaw
declarations.doc: AppendRaw adds an item of the given kind.

declarations.name: AppendRaw
declarations.doc: AppendRaw injects a binary blob at the end of the freezer table. The item number is a precautionary parameter to ensure data correctness, but the table will reject already existing data.

declarations.name: commit

declarations.name: commit

declarations.name: compress
declarations.doc: compress snappy-compresses the data.

declarations.name: maybeCommit
declarations.doc: maybeCommit writes the buffered data if the buffer is full enough.

declarations.name: newBatch
declarations.doc: newBatch creates a new batch for the freezer table.

declarations.doc: freezerTableBatch is a batch for a freezer table.

declarations.doc: snappyBuffer writes snappy in block format, and can be reused. It is reset when WriteTo is called.

declarations.name: writeBuffer
declarations.doc: writeBuffer implements io.Writer for a byte slice.

declarations.name: loadMetadata
declarations.doc: loadMetadata loads the metadata from the given metadata file. Initializes the metadata file with the given "actual tail" if it's empty.

declarations.name: newMetadata
declarations.doc: newMetadata initializes the metadata object with the given virtual tail.

declarations.name: readMetadata
declarations.doc: readMetadata reads the metadata of the freezer table from the given metadata file.

declarations.name: writeMetadata
declarations.doc: writeMetadata writes the metadata of the freezer table into the given metadata file.

declarations.doc: freezerTableMeta wraps all the metadata of the freezer table.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close closes all opened files.

declarations.name: DumpIndex
declarations.doc: DumpIndex is a debug print utility function, mainly for testing. It can also be used to analyse a live freezer table index.

declarations.name: NewFreezerTable
declarations.doc: NewFreezerTable opens the given path as a freezer table.

declarations.name: Retrieve
declarations.doc: Retrieve looks up the data offset of an item with the given number and retrieves the raw binary blob from the data file.

declarations.name: RetrieveItems
declarations.doc: RetrieveItems returns multiple items in sequence, starting from the index 'start'. It will return at most 'max' items, but will abort earlier to respect the 'maxBytes' argument. However, if the 'maxBytes' is smaller than the size of one item, it _will_ return one element and possibly overflow the maxBytes.

declarations.name: Sync
declarations.doc: Sync pushes any pending data from memory out to disk. This is an expensive operation, so use it with care.

declarations.name: advanceHead
declarations.doc: advanceHead should be called when the current head file would outgrow the file limits, and a new file must be opened. The caller of this method must hold the write-lock before calling this method.

declarations.name: append
declarations.doc: append adds the encoded entry to the end of b.

declarations.name: bounds
declarations.doc: bounds returns the start- and end- offsets, and the file number of where to read there data item marked by the two index entries. The two entries are assumed to be sequential.

declarations.name: getIndices
declarations.doc: getIndices returns the index entries for the given from-item, covering 'count' items. N.B: The actual number of returned indices for N items will always be N+1 (unless an error is returned). OBS: This method assumes that the caller has already verified (and/or trimmed) the range so that the items are within bounds. If this method is used to read out of bounds, it will return error.

declarations.name: has
declarations.doc: has returns an indicator whether the specified number data is still accessible in the freezer table.

declarations.name: newTable
declarations.doc: newTable opens a freezer table, creating the data and index files if they are non-existent. Both files are truncated to the shortest common length to ensure they don't go out of sync.

declarations.name: openFile
declarations.doc: openFile assumes that the write-lock is held by the caller

declarations.name: preopen
declarations.doc: preopen opens all files that the freezer will need. This method should be called from an init-context, since it assumes that it doesn't have to bother with locking The rationale for doing preopen is to not have to do it from within Retrieve, thus not needing to ever obtain a write-lock within Retrieve.

declarations.name: releaseFile
declarations.doc: releaseFile closes a file, and removes it from the open file cache. Assumes that the caller holds the write lock

declarations.name: releaseFilesAfter
declarations.doc: releaseFilesAfter closes all open files with a higher number, and optionally also deletes the files

declarations.name: releaseFilesBefore
declarations.doc: releaseFilesBefore closes all open files with a lower number, and optionally also deletes the files

declarations.name: repair
declarations.doc: repair cross-checks the head and the index file and truncates them to be in sync with each other after a potential crash / data loss.

declarations.name: retrieveItems
declarations.doc: retrieveItems reads up to 'count' items from the table. It reads at least one item, but otherwise avoids reading more than maxBytes bytes. It returns the (potentially compressed) data, and the sizes.

declarations.name: size
declarations.doc: size returns the total data size in the freezer table.

declarations.name: sizeNolock
declarations.doc: sizeNolock returns the total data size in the freezer table without obtaining the mutex first.

declarations.name: truncateHead
declarations.doc: truncateHead discards any recent data above the provided threshold number.

declarations.name: truncateTail
declarations.doc: truncateTail discards any recent data before the provided threshold number.

declarations.name: unmarshalBinary
declarations.doc: unmarshalBinary deserializes binary b into the rawIndex entry.

declarations.name: freezerTable
declarations.doc: freezerTable represents a single chained data table within the freezer (e.g. blocks). It consists of a data file (snappy encoded arbitrary data blobs) and an indexEntry file (uncompressed 64 bit indices into the data file).

declarations.name: indexEntry
declarations.doc: indexEntry contains the number/id of the file that the data resides in, aswell as the offset within the file to the end of the data. In serialized form, the filenum is stored as uint16.

declarations.doc: TestFreezerReadAndTruncate tests: - we have a table open - do some reads, so files are open in readonly - truncate so those files are 'removed' - check that we did not keep the rdonly file descriptors

declarations.doc: TestSequentialReadByteLimit does some more advanced tests on batch reads. These tests check that when the byte limit hits, we correctly abort in time, but also properly do all the deferred reads for the previous data, regardless of whether the data crosses a file boundary or not.

declarations.doc: copyFrom copies data from 'srcPath' at offset 'offset' into 'destPath'. The 'destPath' is created if it doesn't exist, otherwise it is overwritten. Before the copy is executed, there is a callback can be registered to manipulate the dest file. It is perfectly valid to have destPath == srcPath.

declarations.name: Compact
declarations.doc: Compact flattens the underlying data store for the given key range. In essence, deleted and overwritten versions are discarded, and the data is rearranged to reduce the cost of operations needed to access them. A nil start is treated as a key before all keys in the data store; a nil limit is treated as a key after all keys in the data store. If both is nil then it will compact entire data store.

declarations.name: Delete

declarations.name: Delete
declarations.doc: Delete inserts the a key removal into the batch for later committing.

declarations.name: Delete
declarations.doc: Delete implements the interface KeyValueWriter.

declarations.name: Error

declarations.doc: HasAncient is a noop passthrough that just forwards the request to the underlying database.

declarations.name: NewTable

declarations.doc: Sync is a noop passthrough that just forwards the request to the underlying database.

declarations.name: ContainsAddress

declarations.doc: Copy creates an independent copy of an accessList.

declarations.name: DeleteSlot

declarations.doc: retrieve pulls and caches the current state entry the iterator is traversing. The method returns whether there are any more data left for inspection.

declarations.name: step
declarations.doc: step moves the iterator to the next entry of the state trie.

declarations.name: NodeIterator
declarations.doc: NodeIterator is an iterator to traverse the entire state trie post-order, including all of the contract code and contract state tries.

declarations.name: TestNodeIteratorCoverage
declarations.doc: Tests that the node iterator indeed walks over the entire database contents.

declarations.name: append
declarations.doc: append inserts a new modification entry to the end of the change journal.

declarations.name: dirty
declarations.doc: dirty explicitly sets an address to dirty, even if the change entries would otherwise suggest it as clean. This method is an ugly hack to handle the RIPEMD precompile consensus exception.

declarations.name: length
declarations.doc: length returns the current number of entries in the journal.

declarations.name: newJournal
declarations.doc: newJournal creates a new initialized journal.

declarations.name: revert
declarations.doc: revert undoes a batch of journalled modifications along with any reverted dirty handling too.

declarations.name: accessListAddAccountChange
declarations.doc: Changes to the access list

declarations.name: balanceChange
declarations.doc: Changes to individual accounts.

declarations.name: createObjectChange
declarations.doc: Changes to the account trie.

declarations.name: journal
declarations.doc: journal contains the list of state modifications applied since the last state commit. These are tracked to be able to be reverted in the case of an execution exception or request for reversal.

declarations.name: journalEntry
declarations.doc: journalEntry is a modification entry in the state change journal that can be reverted on demand.

declarations.name: refundChange
declarations.doc: Changes to other state values.

declarations.name: AddBalance
declarations.doc: AddBalance adds amount to s's balance. It is used to add funds to the destination account of a transfer.

declarations.name: Address
declarations.doc: Returns the address of the contract/account

declarations.name: Code
declarations.doc: Code returns the contract code associated with this object, if any.

declarations.name: CodeSize
declarations.doc: CodeSize returns the size of the contract code associated with this object, or zero if none. This method is an almost mirror of Code, but uses a cache inside the database to avoid loading codes seen recently.

declarations.name: CommitTrie
declarations.doc: CommitTrie the storage trie of the object to db. This updates the trie root.

declarations.name: EncodeRLP
declarations.doc: EncodeRLP implements rlp.Encoder.

declarations.name: GetCommittedState
declarations.doc: GetCommittedState retrieves a value from the committed account storage trie.

declarations.name: GetState
declarations.doc: GetState retrieves a value from the account storage trie.

declarations.name: SetState
declarations.doc: SetState updates a value in account storage.

declarations.name: SetStorage
declarations.doc: SetStorage replaces the entire state storage with the given one. After this function is called, all original state will be ignored and state lookup only happens in the fake state storage. Note this function should only be used for debugging purpose.

declarations.name: SubBalance
declarations.doc: SubBalance removes amount from s's balance. It is used to remove funds from the origin account of a transfer.

declarations.name: Value
declarations.doc: Never called, but must be present to allow stateObject to be used as a vm.Account interface that also satisfies the vm.ContractRef interface. Interfaces are awesome.

declarations.name: empty
declarations.doc: empty returns whether the account is considered empty.

declarations.name: finalise
declarations.doc: finalise moves all dirty storage slots into the pending area to be hashed or committed later. It is invoked at the end of every transaction.

declarations.name: newObject
declarations.doc: newObject creates a state object.

declarations.name: setError
declarations.doc: setError remembers the first non-nil error it is called with.

declarations.name: updateRoot
declarations.doc: UpdateRoot sets the trie root to the current root hash of

declarations.name: updateTrie
declarations.doc: updateTrie writes cached storage modifications into the object's storage trie. It will return nil if the trie has not been loaded and no changes have been made

declarations.name: stateObject
declarations.doc: stateObject represents an Ethereum account which is being modified. The usage pattern is as follows: First you need to obtain a state object. Account values can be accessed and modified through the object. Finally, call CommitTrie to write the modified storage trie into a database.

declarations.name: AddAddressToAccessList
declarations.doc: AddAddressToAccessList adds the given address to the access list

declarations.name: AddBalance
declarations.doc: AddBalance adds amount to the account associated with addr.

declarations.name: AddPreimage
declarations.doc: AddPreimage records a SHA3 preimage seen by the VM.

declarations.name: AddRefund
declarations.doc: AddRefund adds gas to the refund counter

declarations.name: AddSlotToAccessList
declarations.doc: AddSlotToAccessList adds the given (address, slot)-tuple to the access list

declarations.name: AddressInAccessList
declarations.doc: AddressInAccessList returns true if the given address is in the access list.

declarations.name: Commit
declarations.doc: Commit writes the state to the underlying in-memory trie database.

declarations.name: Copy
declarations.doc: Copy creates a deep, independent copy of the state. Snapshots of the copied state cannot be applied to the copy.

declarations.name: CreateAccount
declarations.doc: CreateAccount explicitly creates a state object. If a state object with the address already exists the balance is carried over to the new account. CreateAccount is called during the EVM CREATE operation. The situation might arise that a contract does the following: 1. sends funds to sha(account ++ (nonce + 1)) 2. tx_create(sha(account ++ nonce)) (note that this gets the address of 1) Carrying over the balance ensures that Ether doesn't disappear.

declarations.name: Database
declarations.doc: Database retrieves the low level database supporting the lower level trie ops.

declarations.name: Empty
declarations.doc: Empty returns whether the state object is either non-existent or empty according to the EIP161 specification (balance = nonce = code = 0)

declarations.name: Exist
declarations.doc: Exist reports whether the given account address exists in the state. Notably this also returns true for suicided accounts.

declarations.name: Finalise
declarations.doc: Finalise finalises the state by removing the s destructed objects and clears the journal as well as the refunds. Finalise, however, will not push any updates into the tries just yet. Only IntermediateRoot or Commit will do that.

declarations.name: GetBalance
declarations.doc: GetBalance retrieves the balance from the given address or 0 if object not found

declarations.name: GetCommittedState
declarations.doc: GetCommittedState retrieves a value from the given account's committed storage trie.

declarations.name: GetOrNewStateObject
declarations.doc: GetOrNewStateObject retrieves a state object or create a new state object if nil.

declarations.name: GetProof
declarations.doc: GetProof returns the Merkle proof for a given account.

declarations.name: GetProofByHash
declarations.doc: GetProofByHash returns the Merkle proof for a given account.

declarations.name: GetRefund
declarations.doc: GetRefund returns the current value of the refund counter.

declarations.name: GetState
declarations.doc: GetState retrieves a value from the given account's storage trie.

declarations.name: GetStorageProof
declarations.doc: GetStorageProof returns the Merkle proof for given storage slot.

declarations.name: IntermediateRoot
declarations.doc: IntermediateRoot computes the current root hash of the state trie. It is called in between transactions to get the root hash that goes into transaction receipts.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New creates a new state from a given trie.

declarations.name: Preimages
declarations.doc: Preimages returns a list of SHA3 preimages that have been submitted.

declarations.name: Prepare
declarations.doc: Prepare sets the current transaction hash and index which are used when the EVM emits new state logs.

declarations.name: PrepareAccessList
declarations.doc: PrepareAccessList handles the preparatory steps for executing a state transition with regards to both EIP-2929 and EIP-2930: - Add sender to access list (2929) - Add destination to access list (2929) - Add precompiles to access list (2929) - Add the contents of the optional tx access list (2930) This method should only be called if Berlin/2929+2930 is applicable at the current number.

declarations.name: RevertToSnapshot
declarations.doc: RevertToSnapshot reverts all state changes made since the given revision.

declarations.name: SetStorage
declarations.doc: SetStorage replaces the entire storage for the specified account with given storage. This function should only be used for debugging.

declarations.name: SlotInAccessList
declarations.doc: SlotInAccessList returns true if the given (address, slot)-tuple is in the access list.

declarations.name: Snapshot
declarations.doc: Snapshot returns an identifier for the current revision of the state.

declarations.name: StartPrefetcher
declarations.doc: StartPrefetcher initializes a new trie prefetcher to pull in nodes from the state trie concurrently while the state is mutated so that when we reach the commit phase, most of the needed data is already hot.

declarations.name: StopPrefetcher
declarations.doc: StopPrefetcher terminates a running prefetcher and reports any leftover stats from the gathered metrics.

declarations.name: StorageTrie
declarations.doc: StorageTrie returns the storage trie of an account. The return value is a copy and is nil for non-existent accounts.

declarations.name: SubBalance
declarations.doc: SubBalance subtracts amount from the account associated with addr.

declarations.name: SubRefund
declarations.doc: SubRefund removes gas from the refund counter. This method will panic if the refund counter goes below zero

declarations.name: Suicide
declarations.doc: Suicide marks the given account as suicided. This clears the account balance. The account's state object is still available until the state is committed, getStateObject will return a non-nil account after Suicide.

declarations.name: TxIndex
declarations.doc: TxIndex returns the current transaction index set by Prepare.

declarations.name: createObject
declarations.doc: createObject creates a new state object. If there is an existing account with the given address, it is overwritten and returned as the second return value.

declarations.name: deleteStateObject
declarations.doc: deleteStateObject removes the given object from the state trie.

declarations.name: getDeletedStateObject
declarations.doc: getDeletedStateObject is similar to getStateObject, but instead of returning nil for a deleted state object, it returns the actual object with the deleted flag set. This is needed by the state journal to revert to the correct s- destructed object instead of wiping all knowledge about the state object.

declarations.name: getStateObject
declarations.doc: getStateObject retrieves a state object given by the address, returning nil if the object is not found or was deleted in this execution context. If you need to differentiate between non-existent/just-deleted, use getDeletedStateObject.

declarations.name: setError
declarations.doc: setError remembers the first non-nil error it is called with.

declarations.name: updateStateObject
declarations.doc: updateStateObject writes the given object to the trie.

declarations.name: StateDB
declarations.doc: StateDB structs within the ethereum protocol are used to store anything within the merkle trie. StateDBs take care of caching and storing nested states. It's the general query interface to retrieve: * Contracts * Accounts

declarations.name: Generate
declarations.doc: Generate returns a new snapshot test of the given size. All randomness is derived from r.

declarations.name: TestCopy
declarations.doc: TestCopy tests that copying a StateDB object indeed makes the original and the copy independent of each other. This test is a regression test against https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/15549.

declarations.name: TestCopyCommitCopy
declarations.doc: Tests a regression where committing a copy lost some internal meta information, leading to corrupted subsequent copies. See https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/20106.

declarations.name: TestCopyCopyCommitCopy
declarations.doc: Tests a regression where committing a copy lost some internal meta information, leading to corrupted subsequent copies. See https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/20106.

declarations.name: TestCopyOfCopy
declarations.doc: TestCopyOfCopy tests that modified objects are carried over to the copy, and the copy of the copy. See https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/15225#issuecomment-380191512

declarations.name: TestDeleteCreateRevert
declarations.doc: TestDeleteCreateRevert tests a weird state transition corner case that we hit while changing the internals of StateDB. The workflow is that a contract is self-destructed, then in a follow-up transaction (but same block) it's created again and the transaction reverted. The original StateDB implementation flushed dirty objects to the tries after each transaction, so this works ok. The rework accumulated writes in memory first, but the journal wiped the entire state object on create-revert.

declarations.name: TestIntermediateLeaks
declarations.doc: Tests that no intermediate state of an object is stored into the database, only the one right before the commit.

declarations.name: TestMissingTrieNodes
declarations.doc: TestMissingTrieNodes tests that if the StateDB fails to load parts of the trie, the Commit operation fails with an error If we are missing trie nodes, we should not continue writing to the trie

declarations.name: TestUpdateLeaks
declarations.doc: Tests that updating a state trie does not leak any database writes prior to actually committing the state.

declarations.name: checkEqual
declarations.doc: checkEqual checks that methods of state and checkstate return the same values.

declarations.name: newTestAction
declarations.doc: newTestAction creates a random action that changes state.

declarations.name: snapshotTest
declarations.doc: A snapshotTest checks that reverting StateDB snapshots properly undoes all changes captured by the snapshot. Instances of this test with pseudorandom content are created by Generate. The test works as follows: A new state is created and all actions are applied to it. Several snapshots are taken in between actions. The test then reverts each snapshot. For each snapshot the actions leading up to it are replayed on a fresh, empty state. The behaviour of all public accessor methods on the reverted state must match the return value of the equivalent methods on the replayed state.

declarations.name: NewStateSync
declarations.doc: NewStateSync create a new state trie download scheduler.

declarations.name: TestEmptyStateSync
declarations.doc: Tests that an empty state is not scheduled for syncing.

declarations.name: TestIncompleteStateSync
declarations.doc: Tests that at any point in time during a sync, only complete sub-tries are in the database.

declarations.name: TestIterativeDelayedStateSync
declarations.doc: Tests that the trie scheduler can correctly reconstruct the state even if only partial results are returned, and the others sent only later.

declarations.name: TestIterativeRandomDelayedStateSync
declarations.doc: Tests that the trie scheduler can correctly reconstruct the state even if only partial results are returned (Even those randomly), others sent only later.

declarations.name: TestIterativeRandomStateSyncIndividual
declarations.doc: Tests that given a root hash, a trie can sync iteratively on a single thread, requesting retrieval tasks and returning all of them in one go, however in a random order.

declarations.name: TestIterativeStateSyncIndividual
declarations.doc: Tests that given a root hash, a state can sync iteratively on a single thread, requesting retrieval tasks and returning all of them in one go.

declarations.name: checkStateAccounts
declarations.doc: checkStateAccounts cross references a reconstructed state with an expected account array.

declarations.name: checkStateConsistency
declarations.doc: checkStateConsistency checks that all data of a state root is present.

declarations.name: checkTrieConsistency
declarations.doc: checkTrieConsistency checks that all nodes in a (sub-)trie are indeed present.

declarations.name: makeTestState
declarations.doc: makeTestState create a sample test state to test node-wise reconstruction.

declarations.name: testAccount
declarations.doc: testAccount is the data associated with an account used by the state tests.

declarations.name: abort
declarations.doc: abort interrupts the subfetcher immediately. It is safe to call abort multiple times but it is not thread safe.

declarations.name: close
declarations.doc: close iterates over all the subfetchers, aborts any that were left spinning and reports the stats to the metrics subsystem.

declarations.name: copy
declarations.doc: copy creates a deep-but-inactive copy of the trie prefetcher. Any trie data already loaded will be copied over, but no goroutines will be started. This is mostly used in the miner which creates a copy of it's actively mutated state to be sealed while it may further mutate the state.

declarations.name: loop
declarations.doc: loop waits for new tasks to be scheduled and keeps loading them until it runs out of tasks or its underlying trie is retrieved for committing.

declarations.name: newSubfetcher
declarations.doc: newSubfetcher creates a goroutine to prefetch state items belonging to a particular root hash.

declarations.name: newTriePrefetcher
declarations.doc: newTriePrefetcher

declarations.name: peek
declarations.doc: peek tries to retrieve a deep copy of the fetcher's trie in whatever form it is currently.

declarations.name: prefetch
declarations.doc: prefetch schedules a batch of trie items to prefetch.

declarations.name: schedule
declarations.doc: schedule adds a batch of trie keys to the queue to prefetch.

declarations.name: trie
declarations.doc: trie returns the trie matching the root hash, or nil if the prefetcher doesn't have it.

declarations.name: used
declarations.doc: used marks a batch of state items used to allow creating statistics as to how useful or wasteful the prefetcher is.

declarations.name: subfetcher
declarations.doc: subfetcher is a trie fetcher goroutine responsible for pulling entries for a single trie. It is spawned when a new root is encountered and lives until the main prefetcher is paused and either all requested items are processed or if the trie being worked on is retrieved from the prefetcher.

declarations.name: triePrefetcher
declarations.doc: triePrefetcher is an active prefetcher, which receives accounts or storage items and does trie-loading of them. The goal is to get as much useful content into the caches as possible. Note, the prefetcher's API is not thread safe.

declarations.name: Commit
declarations.doc: Commit flushes the bloom filter content into the disk and marks the bloom as complete.

declarations.name: Contain
declarations.doc: Contain is the wrapper of the underlying contains function which reports whether the key is contained. - If it says yes, the key may be contained - If it says no, the key is definitely not contained.

declarations.name: Delete
declarations.doc: Delete removes the key from the key-value data store.

declarations.name: NewStateBloomFromDisk
declarations.doc: NewStateBloomFromDisk loads the state bloom from the given file. In this case the assumption is held the bloom filter is complete.

declarations.name: Put
declarations.doc: Put implements the KeyValueWriter interface. But here only the key is needed.

declarations.name: newStateBloomWithSize
declarations.doc: newStateBloomWithSize creates a brand new state bloom for state generation. The bloom filter will be created by the passing bloom filter size. According to the https://hur.st/bloomfilter/?n=600000000&p=&m=2048MB&k=4, the parameters are picked so that the false-positive rate for mainnet is low enough.

declarations.name: stateBloom
declarations.doc: stateBloom is a bloom filter used during the state convesion(snapshot->state). The keys of all generated entries will be recorded here so that in the pruning stage the entries belong to the specific version can be avoided for deletion. The false-positive is allowed here. The "false-positive" entries means they actually don't belong to the specific version but they are not deleted in the pruning. The downside of the false-positive allowance is we may leave some "dangling" nodes in the disk. But in practice the it's very unlike the dangling node is state root. So in theory this pruned state shouldn't be visited anymore. Another potential issue is for fast sync. If we do another fast sync upon the pruned database, it's problematic which will stop the expansion during the syncing. TODO address it @rjl493456442 @holiman @karalabe. After the entire state is generated, the bloom filter should be persisted into the disk. It indicates the whole generation procedure is finished.

declarations.name: stateBloomHasher
declarations.doc: stateBloomHasher is a wrapper around a byte blob to satisfy the interface API requirements of the bloom library used. It's used to convert a trie hash or contract code hash into a 64 bit mini hash.

declarations.name: NewPruner
declarations.doc: NewPruner creates the pruner instance.

declarations.name: Prune
declarations.doc: Prune deletes all historical state nodes except the nodes belong to the specified state version. If user doesn't specify the state version, use the bottom-most snapshot diff layer as the target.

declarations.name: RecoverPruning
declarations.doc: RecoverPruning will resume the pruning procedure during the system restart. This function is used in this case: user tries to prune state data, but the system was interrupted midway because of crash or manual-kill. In this case if the bloom filter for filtering active state is already constructed, the pruning can be resumed. What's more if the bloom filter is constructed, the pruning **has to be resumed**. Otherwise a lot of dangling nodes may be left in the disk.

declarations.name: extractGenesis
declarations.doc: extractGenesis loads the genesis state and commits all the state entries into the given bloomfilter.

declarations.name: Pruner
declarations.doc: Pruner is an offline tool to prune the stale state with the help of the snapshot. The workflow of pruner is very simple: - iterate the snapshot, reconstruct the relevant state - iterate the database, delete all other state entries which don't belong to the target state and the genesis state It can take several hours(around 2 hours for mainnet) to finish the whole pruning work. It's recommended to run this offline tool periodically in order to release the disk usage and improve the disk read performance to some extent.

declarations.name: FullAccount
declarations.doc: FullAccount decodes the data on the 'slim RLP' format and return the consensus format account.

declarations.name: FullAccountRLP
declarations.doc: FullAccountRLP converts data on the 'slim RLP' format into the full RLP-format.

declarations.name: SlimAccount
declarations.doc: SlimAccount converts a state.Account content into a slim snapshot account

declarations.name: SlimAccountRLP
declarations.doc: SlimAccountRLP converts a state.Account content into a slim snapshot version RLP encoded.

declarations.name: Account
declarations.doc: Account is a modified version of a state.Account, where the root is replaced with a byte slice. This format can be used to represent full-consensus format or slim-snapshot format which replaces the empty root and code hash as nil byte slice.

declarations.name: Log
declarations.doc: Log creates an contextual log with the given message and the context pulled from the internally maintained statistics.

declarations.name: close
declarations.doc: close releases all the held resources.

declarations.name: iterator
declarations.doc: iterator returns the corresponding iterator specified by the kind.

declarations.name: newGeneratorContext
declarations.doc: newGeneratorContext initializes the context for generation.

declarations.name: openIterator
declarations.doc: openIterator constructs global account and storage snapshot iterators at the interrupted position. These iterators should be reopened from time to time to avoid blocking leveldb compaction for a long time.

declarations.name: removeStorageAt
declarations.doc: removeStorageAt deletes all storage entries which are located in the specified account. When the iterator touches the storage entry which is outside the given account, it stops and holds the current iterated element locally. An error will be returned if the initial position of iterator is not in the given account.

declarations.name: removeStorageBefore
declarations.doc: removeStorageBefore deletes all storage entries which are located before the specified account. When the iterator touches the storage entry which is located in or outside the given account, it stops and holds the current iterated element locally.

declarations.name: removeStorageLeft
declarations.doc: removeStorageLeft deletes all storage entries which are located after the current iterator position.

declarations.name: reopenIterator
declarations.doc: reopenIterator releases the specified snapshot iterator and re-open it in the next position. It's aimed for not blocking leveldb compaction.

declarations.name: generatorContext
declarations.doc: generatorContext carries a few global values to be shared by all generation functions.

declarations.name: generatorStats
declarations.doc: generatorStats is a collection of statistics gathered by the snapshot generator for logging purposes.

declarations.name: GenerateAccountTrieRoot
declarations.doc: GenerateAccountTrieRoot takes an account iterator and reproduces the root hash.

declarations.name: GenerateStorageTrieRoot
declarations.doc: GenerateStorageTrieRoot takes a storage iterator and reproduces the root hash.

declarations.name: GenerateTrie
declarations.doc: GenerateTrie takes the whole snapshot tree as the input, traverses all the accounts as well as the corresponding storages and regenerate the whole state (account trie + all storage tries).

declarations.name: finishAccounts
declarations.doc: finishAccounts updates the gemerator stats for the finished account range.

declarations.name: finishContract
declarations.doc: finishContract updates the generator stats for a specific just-finished contract.

declarations.name: generateTrieRoot
declarations.doc: generateTrieRoot generates the trie hash based on the snapshot iterator. It can be used for generating account trie, storage trie or even the whole state which connects the accounts and the corresponding storages.

declarations.name: newGenerateStats
declarations.doc: newGenerateStats creates a new generator stats.

declarations.name: progressAccounts
declarations.doc: progressAccounts updates the generator stats for the account range.

declarations.name: progressContract
declarations.doc: progressContract updates the generator stats for a specific in-progress contract.

declarations.name: report
declarations.doc: report prints the cumulative progress statistic smartly.

declarations.name: reportDone
declarations.doc: reportDone prints the last log when the whole generation is finished.

declarations.name: runReport
declarations.doc: runReport periodically prints the progress information.

declarations.name: generateStats
declarations.doc: generateStats is a collection of statistics gathered by the trie generator for logging purposes.

declarations.name: leafCallbackFn
declarations.doc: leafCallbackFn is the callback invoked at the leaves of the trie, returns the subtrie root with the specified subtrie identifier.

declarations.name: trieGeneratorFn
declarations.doc: trieGeneratorFn is the interface of trie generation which can be implemented by different trie algorithm.

declarations.name: trieKV
declarations.doc: trieKV represents a trie key-value pair

declarations.name: CheckDanglingStorage
declarations.doc: CheckDanglingStorage iterates the snap storage data, and verifies that all storage also has corresponding account data.

declarations.name: checkDanglingDiskStorage
declarations.doc: checkDanglingDiskStorage checks if there is any 'dangling' storage data in the disk-backed snapshot layer.

declarations.name: checkDanglingJournalStorage
declarations.doc: loadDiffLayer reads the next sections of a snapshot journal, reconstructing a new diff and verifying that it can be linked to the requested parent.

declarations.name: checkDanglingMemStorage
declarations.doc: checkDanglingMemStorage checks if there is any 'dangling' storage in the journalled snapshot difflayers.

declarations.name: Account
declarations.doc: Account directly retrieves the account associated with a particular hash in the snapshot slim data format.

declarations.name: AccountList
declarations.doc: AccountList returns a sorted list of all accounts in this diffLayer, including the deleted ones. Note, the returned slice is not a copy, so do not modify it.

declarations.name: AccountRLP
declarations.doc: AccountRLP directly retrieves the account RLP associated with a particular hash in the snapshot slim data format. Note the returned account is not a copy, please don't modify it.

declarations.name: Parent
declarations.doc: Parent returns the subsequent layer of a diff layer.

declarations.name: Root
declarations.doc: Root returns the root hash for which this snapshot was made.

declarations.name: Stale
declarations.doc: Stale return whether this layer has become stale (was flattened across) or if it's still live.

declarations.name: Storage
declarations.doc: Storage directly retrieves the storage data associated with a particular hash, within a particular account. If the slot is unknown to this diff, it's parent is consulted. Note the returned slot is not a copy, please don't modify it.

declarations.name: StorageList
declarations.doc: StorageList returns a sorted list of all storage slot hashes in this diffLayer for the given account. If the whole storage is destructed in this layer, then an additional flag *destructed = true* will be returned, otherwise the flag is false. Besides, the returned list will include the hash of deleted storage slot. Note a special case is an account is deleted in a prior tx but is recreated in the following tx with some storage slots set. In this case the returned list is not empty but the flag is true. Note, the returned slice is not a copy, so do not modify it.

declarations.name: Update
declarations.doc: Update creates a new layer on top of the existing snapshot diff tree with the specified data items.

declarations.name: accountRLP
declarations.doc: accountRLP is an internal version of AccountRLP that skips the bloom filter checks and uses the internal maps to try and retrieve the data. It's meant to be used if a higher layer's bloom filter hit already.

declarations.name: flatten
declarations.doc: flatten pushes all data from this point downwards, flattening everything into a single diff at the bottom. Since usually the lowermost diff is the largest, the flattening builds up from there in reverse.

declarations.name: rebloom

declarations.name: storage
declarations.doc: storage is an internal version of Storage that skips the bloom filter checks and uses the internal maps to try and retrieve the data. It's meant to be used if a higher layer's bloom filter hit already.

declarations.name: accountBloomHasher
declarations.doc: accountBloomHasher is a wrapper around a common.Hash to satisfy the interface API requirements of the bloom library used. It's used to convert an account hash into a 64 bit mini hash.

declarations.name: destructBloomHasher
declarations.doc: destructBloomHasher is a wrapper around a common.Hash to satisfy the interface API requirements of the bloom library used. It's used to convert a destruct event into a 64 bit mini hash.

declarations.name: diffLayer
declarations.doc: diffLayer represents a collection of modifications made to a state snapshot after running a block on top. It contains one sorted list for the account trie and one-one list for each storage tries. The goal of a diff layer is to act as a journal, tracking recent modifications made to the state, that have not yet graduated into a semi-immutable state.

declarations.name: storageBloomHasher
declarations.doc: storageBloomHasher is a wrapper around a [2]common.Hash to satisfy the interface API requirements of the bloom library used. It's used to convert an account hash into a 64 bit mini hash.

Max will be assigned in order to limit the maximum amount of data involved in each iteration. The proof result will be returned if the range proving is finished, otherwise the error will be returned to abort the entire procedure.

declarations.name: onStateCallback
declarations.doc: onStateCallback is a function that is called by generateRange, when processing a range of accounts or storage slots. For each element, the callback is invoked. - If 'delete' is true, then this element (and potential slots) needs to be deleted from the snapshot. - If 'write' is true, then this element needs to be updated with the 'val'. - If 'write' is false, then this element is already correct, and needs no update. The 'val' is the canonical encoding of the value (not the slim format for accounts) However, for accounts, the storage trie of the account needs to be checked. Also, dangling storages(storage exists but the corresponding account is missing) need to be cleaned up.

declarations.name: proofResult

declarations.name: Cap
declarations.doc: Cap traverses downwards the snapshot tree from a head block hash until the number of allowed layers are crossed. All layers beyond the permitted number are flattened downwards. Note, the final diff layer count in general will be one more than the amount requested. This happens because the bottom-most diff layer is the accumulator which may or may not overflow and cascade to disk. Since this last layer's survival is only known *after* capping, we need to omit it from the count if we want to ensure that *at least* the requested number of diff layers remain.

declarations.name: Journal
declarations.doc: Journal commits an entire diff hierarchy to disk into a single journal entry. This is meant to be used during shutdown to persist the snapshot without flattening everything down (bad for reorgs). The method returns the root hash of the base layer that needs to be persisted to disk as a trie too to allow continuing any pending generation op.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New attempts to load an already existing snapshot from a persistent key-value store (with a number of memory layers from a journal), ensuring that the head of the snapshot matches the expected one. If the snapshot is missing or the disk layer is broken, the snapshot will be reconstructed using both the existing data and the state trie. The repair happens on a background thread. If the memory layers in the journal do not match the disk layer (e.g. there is a gap) or the journal is missing, there are two repair cases: - if the 'recovery' parameter is true, all memory diff-layers will be discarded. This case happens when the snapshot is 'ahead' of the state trie. - otherwise, the entire snapshot is considered invalid and will be recreated on a background thread.

declarations.name: cap
declarations.doc: cap traverses downwards the diff tree until the number of allowed layers are crossed. All diffs beyond the permitted number are flattened downwards. If the layer limit is reached, memory cap is also enforced (but not before). The method returns the new disk layer if diffs were persisted into it. Note, the final diff layer count in general will be one more than the amount requested. This happens because the bottom-most diff layer is the accumulator which may or may not overflow and cascade to disk. Since this last layer's survival is only known *after* capping, we need to omit it from the count if we want to ensure that *at least* the requested number of diff layers remain.

declarations.name: diffToDisk
declarations.doc: diffToDisk merges a bottom-most diff into the persistent disk layer underneath it. The method will panic if called onto a non-bottom-most diff layer. The disk layer persistence should be operated in an atomic way. All updates should be discarded if the whole transition if not finished.

declarations.name: Tree
declarations.doc: Tree is an Ethereum state snapshot tree. It consists of one persistent base layer backed by a key-value store, on top of which arbitrarily many in-memory diff layers are topped. The memory diffs can form a tree with branching, but the disk layer is singleton and common to all. If a reorg goes deeper than the disk layer, everything needs to be deleted. The goal of a state snapshot is twofold: to allow direct access to account and storage data to avoid expensive multi-level trie lookups; and to allow sorted, cheap iteration of the account/storage tries for sync aid.

declarations.name: gasSStoreEIP2200
declarations.doc: 0. If *gasleft* is less than or equal to 2300, fail the current call. 1. If current value equals new value (this is a no-op), SLOAD_GAS is deducted. 2. If current value does not equal new value: 2.1. If original value equals current value (this storage slot has not been changed by the current execution context): 2.1.1. If original value is 0, SSTORE_SET_GAS (20K) gas is deducted. 2.1.2. Otherwise, SSTORE_RESET_GAS gas is deducted. If new value is 0, add SSTORE_CLEARS_SCHEDULE to refund counter. 2.2. If original value does not equal current value (this storage slot is dirty), SLOAD_GAS gas is deducted. Apply both of the following clauses: 2.2.1. If original value is not 0: 2.2.1.1. If current value is 0 (also means that new value is not 0), subtract SSTORE_CLEARS_SCHEDULE gas from refund counter. 2.2.1.2. If new value is 0 (also means that current value is not 0), add SSTORE_CLEARS_SCHEDULE gas to refund counter. 2.2.2. If original value equals new value (this storage slot is reset): 2.2.2.1. If original value is 0, add SSTORE_SET_GAS - SLOAD_GAS to refund counter. 2.2.2.2. Otherwise, add SSTORE_RESET_GAS - SLOAD_GAS gas to refund counter.

declarations.name: opExtCodeHash
declarations.doc: opExtCodeHash returns the code hash of a specified account. There are several cases when the function is called, while we can relay everything to `state.GetCodeHash` function to ensure the correctness. (1) Caller tries to get the code hash of a normal contract account, state should return the relative code hash and set it as the result. (2) Caller tries to get the code hash of a non-existent account, state should return common.Hash{} and zero will be set as the result. (3) Caller tries to get the code hash for an account without contract code, state should return emptyCodeHash(0xc5d246...) as the result. (4) Caller tries to get the code hash of a precompiled account, the result should be zero or emptyCodeHash. It is worth noting that in order to avoid unnecessary create and clean, all precompile accounts on mainnet have been transferred 1 wei, so the return here should be emptyCodeHash. If the precompile account is not transferred any amount on a private or customized chain, the return value will be zero. (5) Caller tries to get the code hash for an account which is marked as suicided in the current transaction, the code hash of this account should be returned. (6) Caller tries to get the code hash for an account which is marked as deleted, this account should be regarded as a non-existent account and zero should be returned.

declarations.name: StateAtBlock
declarations.doc: StateAtBlock retrieves the state database associated with a certain block. If no state is locally available for the given block, a number of blocks are attempted to be reexecuted to generate the desired state. The optional base layer statedb can be passed then it's regarded as the statedb of the parent block. Parameters: - block: The block for which we want the state (== state at the stateRoot of the parent) - reexec: The maximum number of blocks to reprocess trying to obtain the desired state - base: If the caller is tracing multiple blocks, the caller can provide the parent state continuously from the callsite. - checklive: if true, then the live 'blockchain' state database is used. If the caller want to perform Commit or other 'save-to-disk' changes, this should be set to false to avoid storing trash persistently - preferDisk: this arg can be used by the caller to signal that even though the 'base' is provided, it would be preferrable to start from a fresh state, if we have it on disk.

declarations.name: TestNewPayloadOnInvalidChain
declarations.doc: TestNewPayloadOnInvalidChain sets up a valid chain and tries to feed blocks from an invalid chain to test if latestValidHash (LVH) works correctly. We set up the following chain where P1 ... Pn and P1” are valid while P1' is invalid. We expect (1) The LVH to point to the current inserted payload if it was valid. (2) The LVH to point to the valid parent on an invalid payload (if the parent is available). (3) If the parent is unavailable, the LVH should not be set. CommonAncestor◄─▲── P1 ◄── P2 ◄─ P3 ◄─ ... ◄─ Pn │ └── P1' ◄─ P2' ◄─ P3' ◄─ ... ◄─ Pn' │ └── P1''

declarations.name: Syncing

declarations.name: Unsubscribe
declarations.doc: Unsubscribe uninstalls the subscription from the DownloadAPI event loop. The status channel that was passed to subscribeSyncStatus isn't used anymore after this method returns.

declarations.name: eventLoop
declarations.doc: eventLoop runs a loop until the event mux closes. It will install and uninstall new sync subscriptions and broadcasts sync status updates to the installed sync subscriptions.

declarations.name: PublicDownloaderAPI
declarations.doc: PublicDownloaderAPI provides an API which gives information about the current synchronisation status. It offers only methods that operates on data that can be available to anyone without security risks.

declarations.name: SyncStatusSubscription

declarations.name: SyncingResult
declarations.doc: SyncingResult provides information about the current synchronisation status for this node.

declarations.name: uninstallSyncSubscriptionRequest
declarations.doc: uninstallSyncSubscriptionRequest uninstalles a syncing subscription in the API event loop.

declarations.name: BeaconExtend
declarations.doc: BeaconExtend is an optimistic version of BeaconSync, where an attempt is made to extend the current beacon chain with a new header, but in case of a mismatch, the old sync will not be terminated and reorged, rather the new head is dropped. This is useful if a beacon client is feeding us large chunks of payloads to run, but is not setting the head after each.

declarations.name: BeaconSync
declarations.doc: BeaconSync is the post-merge version of the chain synchronization, where the chain is not downloaded from genesis onward, rather from trusted head announces backwards. Internally backfilling and state sync is done the same way, but the header retrieval and scheduling is replaced.

declarations.name: beaconSync
declarations.doc: beaconSync is the post-merge version of the chain synchronization, where the chain is not downloaded from genesis onward, rather from trusted head announces backwards. Internally backfilling and state sync is done the same way, but the header retrieval and scheduling is replaced.

declarations.name: fetchBeaconHeaders
declarations.doc: fetchBeaconHeaders feeds skeleton headers to the downloader queue for scheduling until sync errors or is finished.

declarations.name: findBeaconAncestor
declarations.doc: findBeaconAncestor tries to locate the common ancestor link of the local chain and the beacon chain just requested. In the general case when our node was in sync and on the correct chain, checking the top N links should already get us a match. In the rare scenario when we ended up on a long reorganisation (i.e. none of the head links match), we do a binary search to find the ancestor.

declarations.name: newBeaconBackfiller
declarations.doc: newBeaconBackfiller is a helper method to create the backfiller.

declarations.name: resume
declarations.doc: resume starts the downloader threads for backfilling state and chain data.

declarations.name: setMode
declarations.doc: setMode updates the sync mode from the current one to the requested one. If there's an active sync in progress, it will be cancelled and restarted.

declarations.name: suspend
declarations.doc: suspend cancels any background downloader threads and returns the last header that has been successfully backfilled.

declarations.name: beaconBackfiller
declarations.doc: beaconBackfiller is the chain and state backfilling that can be commenced once the skeleton syncer has successfully reverse downloaded all the headers up to the genesis block or an existing header in the database. Its operation is fully directed by the skeleton sync's head/tail events.

declarations.name: Cancel
declarations.doc: Cancel aborts all of the operations and waits for all download goroutines to finish before returning.

declarations.name: DeliverSnapPacket
declarations.doc: DeliverSnapPacket is invoked from a peer's message handler when it transmits a data packet for the local node to consume.

declarations.name: LegacySync
declarations.doc: LegacySync tries to sync up our local block chain with a remote peer, both adding various sanity checks as well as wrapping it with various log entries.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New creates a new downloader to fetch hashes and blocks from remote peers.

declarations.name: Progress
declarations.doc: Progress retrieves the synchronisation boundaries, specifically the origin block where synchronisation started at (may have failed/suspended); the block or header sync is currently at; and the latest known block which the sync targets. In addition, during the state download phase of snap synchronisation the number of processed and the total number of known states are also returned. Otherwise these are zero.

declarations.name: RegisterLightPeer
declarations.doc: RegisterLightPeer injects a light client peer, wrapping it so it appears as a regular peer.

declarations.name: RegisterPeer
declarations.doc: RegisterPeer injects a new download peer into the set of block source to be used for fetching hashes and blocks from.

declarations.name: Synchronising
declarations.doc: Synchronising returns whether the downloader is currently retrieving blocks.

declarations.name: Terminate
declarations.doc: Terminate interrupts the downloader, canceling all pending operations. The downloader cannot be reused after calling Terminate.

declarations.name: UnregisterPeer
declarations.doc: UnregisterPeer remove a peer from the known list, preventing any action from the specified peer. An effort is also made to return any pending fetches into the queue.

declarations.name: calculateRequestSpan
declarations.doc: calculateRequestSpan calculates what headers to request from a peer when trying to determine the common ancestor. It returns parameters to be used for peer.RequestHeadersByNumber: from - starting block number count - number of headers to request skip - number of headers to skip and also returns 'max', the last block which is expected to be returned by the remote peers, given the (from,count,skip)

declarations.name: cancel
declarations.doc: cancel aborts all of the operations and resets the queue. However, cancel does not wait for the running download goroutines to finish. This method should be used when cancelling the downloads from inside the downloader.

declarations.name: fetchBodies
declarations.doc: fetchBodies iteratively downloads the scheduled block bodies, taking any available peers, reserving a chunk of blocks for each, waiting for delivery and also periodically checking for timeouts.

declarations.name: fetchHead
declarations.doc: fetchHead retrieves the head header and prior pivot block (if available) from a remote peer.

declarations.name: fetchHeaders
declarations.doc: fetchHeaders keeps retrieving headers concurrently from the number requested, until no more are returned, potentially throttling on the way. To facilitate concurrency but still protect against malicious nodes sending bad headers, we construct a header chain skeleton using the "origin" peer we are syncing with, and fill in the missing headers using anyone else. Headers from other peers are only accepted if they map cleanly to the skeleton. If no one can fill in the skeleton - not even the origin peer - it's assumed invalid and the origin is dropped.

declarations.name: fetchReceipts
declarations.doc: fetchReceipts iteratively downloads the scheduled block receipts, taking any available peers, reserving a chunk of receipts for each, waiting for delivery and also periodically checking for timeouts.

declarations.name: fillHeaderSkeleton
declarations.doc: fillHeaderSkeleton concurrently retrieves headers from all our available peers and maps them to the provided skeleton header chain. Any partial results from the beginning of the skeleton is (if possible) forwarded immediately to the header processor to keep the rest of the pipeline full even in the case of header stalls. The method returns the entire filled skeleton and also the number of headers already forwarded for processing.

declarations.name: findAncestor
declarations.doc: findAncestor tries to locate the common ancestor link of the local chain and a remote peers blockchain. In the general case when our node was in sync and on the correct chain, checking the top N links should already get us a match. In the rare scenario when we ended up on a long reorganisation (i.e. none of the head links match), we do a binary search to find the common ancestor.

declarations.name: processFullSyncContent
declarations.doc: processFullSyncContent takes fetch results from the queue and imports them into the chain.

declarations.name: processHeaders
declarations.doc: processHeaders takes batches of retrieved headers from an input channel and keeps processing and scheduling them into the header chain and downloader's queue until the stream ends or a failure occurs.

declarations.name: processSnapSyncContent
declarations.doc: processSnapSyncContent takes fetch results from the queue and writes them to the database. It also controls the synchronisation of state nodes of the pivot block.

declarations.name: readHeaderRange
declarations.doc: readHeaderRange returns a list of headers, using the given last header as the base, and going backwards towards genesis. This method assumes that the caller already has placed a reasonable cap on count.

declarations.name: spawnSync

declarations.name: synchronise
declarations.doc: synchronise will select the peer and use it for synchronising. If an empty string is given it will use the best peer possible and synchronize if its TD is higher than our own. If any of the checks fail an error will be returned. This method is synchronous

declarations.name: TestBeaconSync66Full
declarations.doc: Tests that peers below a pre-configured checkpoint block are prevented from being fast-synced from, avoiding potential cheap eclipse attacks.

declarations.name: TestBlockHeaderAttackerDropping65
declarations.doc: Tests that misbehaving peers are disconnected, whilst behaving ones are not.

declarations.name: TestBoundedForkedSync65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that chain forks are contained within a certain interval of the current chain head, ensuring that malicious peers cannot waste resources by feeding long dead chains.

declarations.name: TestBoundedHeavyForkedSync65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that chain forks are contained within a certain interval of the current chain head for short but heavy forks too. These are a bit special because they take different ancestor lookup paths.

declarations.name: TestCancel65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that a canceled download wipes all previously accumulated state.

declarations.name: TestCheckpointEnforcement65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that peers below a pre-configured checkpoint block are prevented from being fast-synced from, avoiding potential cheap eclipse attacks.

declarations.name: TestEmptyShortCircuit65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that if a block is empty (e.g. header only), no body request should be made, and instead the header should be assembled into a whole block in itself.

declarations.name: TestFailedSyncProgress65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that if synchronisation is aborted due to some failure, then the progress origin is not updated in the next sync cycle, as it should be considered the continuation of the previous sync and not a new instance.

declarations.name: TestFakedSyncProgress65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that if an attacker fakes a chain height, after the attack is detected, the progress height is successfully reduced at the next sync invocation.

declarations.name: TestForkedSync65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that simple synchronization against a forked chain works correctly. In this test common ancestor lookup should *not* be short circuited, and a full binary search should be executed.

declarations.name: TestForkedSyncProgress65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that synchronisation progress (origin block number and highest block number) is tracked and updated correctly in case of a fork (or manual head revertal).

declarations.name: TestHeavyForkedSync65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that synchronising against a much shorter but much heavyer fork works corrently and is not dropped.

declarations.name: TestHighTDStarvationAttack65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that a peer advertising a high TD doesn't get to stall the downloader afterwards by not sending any useful hashes.

declarations.name: TestInvalidHeaderRollback65Snap
declarations.doc: Tests that upon detecting an invalid header, the recent ones are rolled back for various failure scenarios. Afterwards a full sync is attempted to make sure no state was corrupted.

declarations.name: TestMissingHeaderAttack65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that headers are enqueued continuously, preventing malicious nodes from stalling the downloader by feeding gapped header chains.

declarations.name: TestMultiProtoSynchronisation65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that synchronisations behave well in multi-version protocol environments and not wreak havoc on other nodes in the network.

declarations.name: TestMultiSynchronisation65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that synchronisation from multiple peers works as intended (multi thread sanity test).

declarations.name: TestShiftedHeaderAttack65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that if requested headers are shifted (i.e. first is missing), the queue detects the invalid numbering.

declarations.name: TestSyncProgress65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that synchronisation progress (origin block number, current block number and highest block number) is tracked and updated correctly.

declarations.name: TestThrottling65Full
declarations.doc: Tests that if a large batch of blocks are being downloaded, it is throttled until the cached blocks are retrieved.
