declarations.doc: DeliverBodies injects a block body retrieval response into the results queue. The method returns the number of blocks bodies accepted from the delivery and also wakes any threads waiting for data delivery.

declarations.name: DeliverHeaders
declarations.doc: DeliverHeaders injects a header retrieval response into the header results cache. This method either accepts all headers it received, or none of them if they do not map correctly to the skeleton. If the headers are accepted, the method makes an attempt to deliver the set of ready headers to the processor to keep the pipeline full. However, it will not block to prevent stalling other pending deliveries.

declarations.name: DeliverReceipts
declarations.doc: DeliverReceipts injects a receipt retrieval response into the results queue. The method returns the number of transaction receipts accepted from the delivery and also wakes any threads waiting for data delivery.

declarations.name: Done
declarations.doc: Done checks if the given type is done already

declarations.name: ExpireBodies
declarations.doc: ExpireBodies checks for in flight block body requests that exceeded a timeout allowance, canceling them and returning the responsible peers for penalisation.

declarations.name: ExpireHeaders
declarations.doc: ExpireHeaders cancels a request that timed out and moves the pending fetch task back into the queue for rescheduling.

declarations.name: ExpireReceipts
declarations.doc: ExpireReceipts checks for in flight receipt requests that exceeded a timeout allowance, canceling them and returning the responsible peers for penalisation.

declarations.name: Idle
declarations.doc: Idle returns if the queue is fully idle or has some data still inside.

declarations.name: InFlightBlocks
declarations.doc: InFlightBlocks retrieves whether there are block fetch requests currently in flight.

declarations.name: InFlightReceipts
declarations.doc: InFlightReceipts retrieves whether there are receipt fetch requests currently in flight.

declarations.name: PendingBodies
declarations.doc: PendingBodies retrieves the number of block body requests pending for retrieval.

declarations.name: PendingHeaders
declarations.doc: PendingHeaders retrieves the number of header requests pending for retrieval.

declarations.name: PendingReceipts
declarations.doc: PendingReceipts retrieves the number of block receipts pending for retrieval.

declarations.name: Prepare
declarations.doc: Prepare configures the result cache to allow accepting and caching inbound fetch results.

declarations.name: ReserveBodies
declarations.doc: ReserveBodies reserves a set of body fetches for the given peer, skipping any previously failed downloads. Beside the next batch of needed fetches, it also returns a flag whether empty blocks were queued requiring processing.

declarations.name: ReserveHeaders
declarations.doc: ReserveHeaders reserves a set of headers for the given peer, skipping any previously failed batches.

declarations.name: ReserveReceipts
declarations.doc: ReserveReceipts reserves a set of receipt fetches for the given peer, skipping any previously failed downloads. Beside the next batch of needed fetches, it also returns a flag whether empty receipts were queued requiring importing.

declarations.name: Reset
declarations.doc: Reset clears out the queue contents.

declarations.name: Results
declarations.doc: Results retrieves and permanently removes a batch of fetch results from the cache. the result slice will be empty if the queue has been closed. Results can be called concurrently with Deliver and Schedule, but assumes that there are not two simultaneous callers to Results

declarations.name: RetrieveHeaders
declarations.doc: RetrieveHeaders retrieves the header chain assemble based on the scheduled skeleton.

declarations.name: Revoke
declarations.doc: Revoke cancels all pending requests belonging to a given peer. This method is meant to be called during a peer drop to quickly reassign owned data fetches to remaining nodes.

declarations.name: Schedule
declarations.doc: Schedule adds a set of headers for the download queue for scheduling, returning the new headers encountered.

declarations.name: ScheduleSkeleton
declarations.doc: ScheduleSkeleton adds a batch of header retrieval tasks to the queue to fill up an already retrieved header skeleton.

declarations.name: SetBodyDone
declarations.doc: SetBodyDone flags the body as finished.

declarations.name: SetReceiptsDone
declarations.doc: SetReceiptsDone flags the receipts as finished.

declarations.name: deliver
declarations.doc: deliver injects a data retrieval response into the results queue. Note, this method expects the queue lock to be already held for writing. The reason this lock is not obtained in here is because the parameters already need to access the queue, so they already need a lock anyway.

declarations.name: expire
declarations.doc: expire is the generic check that moves a specific expired task from a pending pool back into a task pool. Note, this method expects the queue lock to be already held. The reason the lock is not obtained in here is that the parameters already need to access the queue, so they already need a lock anyway.

declarations.name: newQueue
declarations.doc: newQueue creates a new download queue for scheduling block retrieval.

declarations.name: reserveHeaders
declarations.doc: reserveHeaders reserves a set of data download operations for a given peer, skipping any previously failed ones. This method is a generic version used by the individual special reservation functions. Note, this method expects the queue lock to be already held for writing. The reason the lock is not obtained in here is because the parameters already need to access the queue, so they already need a lock anyway. Returns: item - the fetchRequest progress - whether any progress was made throttle - if the caller should throttle for a while

declarations.name: fetchRequest
declarations.doc: fetchRequest is a currently running data retrieval operation.

declarations.name: fetchResult
declarations.doc: fetchResult is a struct collecting partial results from data fetchers until all outstanding pieces complete and the result as a whole can be processed.

declarations.name: queue
declarations.doc: queue represents hashes that are either need fetching or are being fetched

declarations.name: XTestDelivery
declarations.doc: XTestDelivery does some more extensive testing of events that happen, blocks that become known and peers that make reservations and deliveries. disabled since it's not really a unit-test, but can be executed to test some more advanced scenarios

declarations.name: makeChain
declarations.doc: makeChain creates a chain of n blocks starting at and including parent. the returned hash chain is ordered head->parent. In addition, every 3rd block contains a transaction and every 5th an uncle to allow testing correct block reassembly.

declarations.name: network
declarations.doc: represents the network

declarations.name: AddFetch
declarations.doc: AddFetch adds a header for body/receipt fetching. This is used when the queue wants to reserve headers for fetching. It returns the following: stale - if true, this item is already passed, and should not be requested again throttled - if true, the store is at capacity, this particular header is not prio now item - the result to store data into err - any error that occurred

declarations.name: GetCompleted
declarations.doc: GetCompleted returns the next batch of completed fetchResults

declarations.name: GetDeliverySlot
declarations.doc: GetDeliverySlot returns the fetchResult for the given header. If the 'stale' flag is true, that means the header has already been delivered 'upstream'. This method does not bubble up the 'throttle' flag, since it's moot at the point in time when the item is downloaded and ready for delivery

declarations.name: HasCompletedItems
declarations.doc: hasCompletedItems returns true if there are processable items available this method is cheaper than countCompleted

declarations.name: Prepare
declarations.doc: Prepare initialises the offset with the given block number

declarations.name: SetThrottleThreshold
declarations.doc: SetThrottleThreshold updates the throttling threshold based on the requested limit and the total queue capacity. It returns the (possibly capped) threshold

declarations.name: countCompleted
declarations.doc: countCompleted returns the number of items ready for delivery, stopping at the first non-complete item. The mthod assumes (at least) rlock is held.

declarations.name: getFetchResult
declarations.doc: getFetchResult returns the fetchResult corresponding to the given item, and the index where the result is stored.

declarations.name: resultStore
declarations.doc: resultStore implements a structure for maintaining fetchResults, tracking their download-progress and delivering (finished) results.

declarations.name: Bounds
declarations.doc: Bounds retrieves the current head and tail tracked by the skeleton syncer. This method is used by the backfiller, whose life cycle is controlled by the skeleton syncer. Note, the method will not use the internal state of the skeleton, but will rather blindly pull stuff from the database. This is fine, because the back- filler will only run when the skeleton chain is fully downloaded and stable. There might be new heads appended, but those are atomic from the perspective of this method. Any head reorg will first tear down the backfiller and only then make the modification.

declarations.name: Header
declarations.doc: Header retrieves a specific header tracked by the skeleton syncer. This method is meant to be used by the backfiller, whose life cycle is controlled by the skeleton syncer. Note, outside the permitted runtimes, this method might return nil results and subsequent calls might return headers from different chains.

declarations.name: Sync
declarations.doc: Sync starts or resumes a previous sync cycle to download and maintain a reverse header chain starting at the head and leading towards genesis to an available ancestor. This method does not block, rather it just waits until the syncer receives the fed header. What the syncer does with it is the syncer's problem.

declarations.name: Terminate
declarations.doc: Terminate tears down the syncer indefinitely.

declarations.name: assignTasks
declarations.doc: assignTasks attempts to match idle peers to pending header retrievals.

declarations.name: cleanStales
declarations.doc: cleanStales removes previously synced beacon headers that have become stale due to the downloader backfilling past the tracked tail.

declarations.name: executeTask
declarations.doc: executeTask executes a single fetch request, blocking until either a result arrives or a timeouts / cancellation is triggered. The method should be run on its own goroutine and will deliver on the requested channels.

declarations.name: initSync
declarations.doc: initSync attempts to get the skeleton sync into a consistent state wrt any past state on disk and the newly requested head to sync to. If the new head is nil, the method will return and continue from the previous head.

declarations.name: newSkeleton
declarations.doc: newSkeleton creates a new sync skeleton that tracks a potentially dangling header chain until it's linked into an existing set of blocks.

declarations.name: processNewHead
declarations.doc: processNewHead does the internal shuffling for a new head marker and either accepts and integrates it into the skeleton or requests a reorg. Upon reorg, the syncer will tear itself down and restart with a fresh head. It is simpler to reconstruct the sync state than to mutate it and hope for the best.

declarations.name: revertRequest
declarations.doc: revertRequest cleans up a request and returns all failed retrieval tasks to the scheduler for reassignment. Note, this needs to run on the event runloop thread to reschedule to idle peers. On peer threads, use scheduleRevertRequest.

declarations.name: revertRequests
declarations.doc: revertRequests locates all the currently pending reuqests from a particular peer and reverts them, rescheduling for others to fulfill.

declarations.name: saveSyncStatus
declarations.doc: saveSyncStatus marshals the remaining sync tasks into leveldb.

declarations.name: scheduleRevertRequest
declarations.doc: scheduleRevertRequest asks the event loop to clean up a request and return all failed retrieval tasks to the scheduler for reassignment.

declarations.name: startup
declarations.doc: startup is an initial background loop which waits for an event to start or tear the syncer down. This is required to make the skeleton sync loop once per process but at the same time not start before the beacon chain announces a new (existing) head.

declarations.name: sync
declarations.doc: sync is the internal version of Sync that executes a single sync cycle, either until some termination condition is reached, or until the current cycle merges with a previously aborted run.

declarations.name: backfiller
declarations.doc: backfiller is a callback interface through which the skeleton sync can tell the downloader that it should suspend or resume backfilling on specific head events (e.g. suspend on forks or gaps, resume on successful linkups).

declarations.name: headUpdate
declarations.doc: headUpdate is a notification that the beacon sync should switch to a new target. The update might request whether to forcefully change the target, or only try to extend it and fail if it's not possible.

declarations.name: headerRequest
declarations.doc: headerRequest tracks a pending header request to ensure responses are to actual requests and to validate any security constraints. Concurrency note: header requests and responses are handled concurrently from the main runloop to allow Keccak256 hash verifications on the peer's thread and to drop on invalid response. The request struct must contain all the data to construct the response without accessing runloop internals (i.e. subchains). That is only included to allow the runloop to match a response to the task being synced without having yet another set of maps.

declarations.name: headerResponse
declarations.doc: headerResponse is an already verified remote response to a header request.

declarations.name: skeleton
declarations.doc: skeleton represents a header chain synchronized after the merge where blocks aren't validated any more via PoW in a forward fashion, rather are dictated and extended at the head via the beacon chain and backfilled on the original Ethereum block sync protocol. Since the skeleton is grown backwards from head to genesis, it is handled as a separate entity, not mixed in with the logical sequential transition of the blocks. Once the skeleton is connected to an existing, validated chain, the headers will be moved into the main downloader for filling and execution. Opposed to the original Ethereum block synchronization which is trustless (and uses a master peer to minimize the attack surface), post-merge block sync starts from a trusted head. As such, there is no need for a master peer any more and headers can be requested fully concurrently (though some batches might be discarded if they don't link up correctly). Although a skeleton is part of a sync cycle, it is not recreated, rather stays alive throughout the lifetime of the downloader. This allows it to be extended concurrently with the sync cycle, since extensions arrive from an API surface, not from within (vs. legacy Ethereum sync). Since the skeleton tracks the entire header chain until it is consumed by the forward block filling, it needs 0.5KB/block storage. At current mainnet sizes this is only possible with a disk backend. Since the skeleton is separate from the node's header chain, storing the headers ephemerally until sync finishes is wasted disk IO, but it's a price we're going to pay to keep things simple for now.

declarations.name: skeletonProgress
declarations.doc: skeletonProgress is a database entry to allow suspending and resuming a chain sync. As the skeleton header chain is downloaded backwards, restarts can and will produce temporarily disjoint subchains. There is no way to restart a suspended skeleton sync without prior knowledge of all prior suspension points.

declarations.name: subchain
declarations.doc: subchain is a contiguous header chain segment that is backed by the database, but may not be linked to the live chain. The skeleton downloader may produce a new one of these every time it is restarted until the subchain grows large enough to connect with a previous subchain. The subchains use the exact same database namespace and are not disjoint from each other. As such, extending one to overlap the other entails reducing the second one first. This combined buffer model is used to avoid having to move data on disk when two subchains are joined together.

declarations.name: RequestHeadersByNumber
declarations.doc: RequestHeadersByNumber constructs a GetBlockHeaders function based on a numbered origin; associated with a particular peer in the download tester. The returned function can be used to retrieve batches of headers from the particular peer.

declarations.name: TestSkeletonSyncExtend
declarations.doc: Tests that a running skeleton sync can be extended with properly linked up headers but not with side chains.

declarations.name: TestSkeletonSyncInit
declarations.doc: Tests various sync initialzations based on previous leftovers in the database and announced heads.

declarations.name: TestSkeletonSyncRetrievals
declarations.doc: Tests that the skeleton sync correctly retrieves headers from one or more peers without duplicates or other strange side effects.

declarations.name: newHookedBackfiller
declarations.doc: newHookedBackfiller creates a hooked backfiller with all callbacks disabled, essentially acting as a noop.

declarations.name: newSkeletonTestPeer
declarations.doc: newSkeletonTestPeer creates a new mock peer to test the skeleton sync with.

declarations.name: newSkeletonTestPeerWithHook
declarations.doc: newSkeletonTestPeer creates a new mock peer to test the skeleton sync with, and sets an optional serve hook that can return headers for delivery instead of the predefined chain. Useful for emulating malicious behavior that would otherwise require dedicated peer types.

declarations.name: resume
declarations.doc: resume requests the backfiller to start running fill or snap sync based on the skeleton chain as it has successfully been linked. Appending new heads to the end of the chain will not result in suspend/resume cycles.

declarations.name: suspend
declarations.doc: suspend requests the backfiller to abort any running full or snap sync based on the skeleton chain as it might be invalid. The backfiller should gracefully handle multiple consecutive suspends without a resume, even on initial sartup.

declarations.name: hookedBackfiller
declarations.doc: hookedBackfiller is a tester backfiller with all interface methods mocked and hooked so tests can implement only the things they need.

declarations.name: skeletonTestPeer
declarations.doc: skeletonTestPeer is a mock peer that can only serve header requests from a pre-perated header chain (which may be arbitrarily wrong for testing). Requesting anything else from these peers will hard panic. Note, do *not* implement any other methods. We actually want to make sure that the skeleton syncer only depends on - and will only ever do so - on header requests.

declarations.name: Cancel
declarations.doc: Cancel cancels the sync and waits until it has shut down.

declarations.name: Wait
declarations.doc: Wait blocks until the sync is done or canceled.

declarations.name: newStateSync
declarations.doc: newStateSync creates a new state trie download scheduler. This method does not yet start the sync. The user needs to call run to initiate.

declarations.name: run
declarations.doc: run starts the task assignment and response processing loop, blocking until it finishes, and finally notifying any goroutines waiting for the loop to finish.

declarations.name: runStateSync
declarations.doc: runStateSync runs a state synchronisation until it completes or another root hash is requested to be switched over to.

declarations.name: stateFetcher
declarations.doc: stateFetcher manages the active state sync and accepts requests on its behalf.

declarations.name: syncState
declarations.doc: syncState starts downloading state with the given root hash.

declarations.name: stateSync
declarations.doc: stateSync schedules requests for downloading a particular state trie defined by a given state root.

declarations.name: generate
declarations.doc: generate creates a chain of n blocks starting at and including parent. the returned hash chain is ordered head->parent. In addition, every 22th block contains a transaction and every 5th an uncle to allow testing correct block reassembly.

declarations.name: makeFork
declarations.doc: makeFork creates a fork on top of the test chain.

declarations.name: newTestBlockchain
declarations.doc: newTestBlockchain creates a blockchain database built by running the given blocks, either actually running them, or reusing a previously created one. The returned chains are *shared*, so *do not* mutate them.

declarations.name: newTestChain
declarations.doc: newTestChain creates a blockchain of the given length.

declarations.name: shorten
declarations.doc: shorten creates a copy of the chain with the given length. It panics if the length is longer than the number of available blocks.

declarations.name: CreateConsensusEngine
declarations.doc: CreateConsensusEngine creates a consensus engine for the given chain configuration.

declarations.name: Config
declarations.doc: Config contains configuration options for of the ETH and LES protocols.

declarations.name: MarshalTOML
declarations.doc: MarshalTOML marshals as TOML.

declarations.name: UnmarshalTOML
declarations.doc: UnmarshalTOML unmarshals from TOML.

declarations.name: Enqueue
declarations.doc: Enqueue tries to fill gaps the fetcher's future import queue.

declarations.name: FilterBodies
declarations.doc: FilterBodies extracts all the block bodies that were explicitly requested by the fetcher, returning those that should be handled differently.

declarations.name: FilterHeaders
declarations.doc: FilterHeaders extracts all the headers that were explicitly requested by the fetcher, returning those that should be handled differently.

declarations.name: NewBlockFetcher
declarations.doc: NewBlockFetcher creates a block fetcher to retrieve blocks based on hash announcements.

declarations.name: Notify
declarations.doc: Notify announces the fetcher of the potential availability of a new block in the network.

declarations.name: Start
declarations.doc: Start boots up the announcement based synchroniser, accepting and processing hash notifications and block fetches until termination requested.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop terminates the announcement based synchroniser, canceling all pending operations.

declarations.name: enqueue
declarations.doc: enqueue schedules a new header or block import operation, if the component to be imported has not yet been seen.

declarations.name: forgetBlock
declarations.doc: forgetBlock removes all traces of a queued block from the fetcher's internal state.

declarations.name: forgetHash
declarations.doc: forgetHash removes all traces of a block announcement from the fetcher's internal state.

declarations.name: hash
declarations.doc: number returns the block hash of the injected object.

declarations.name: importBlocks
declarations.doc: importBlocks spawns a new goroutine to run a block insertion into the chain. If the block's number is at the same height as the current import phase, it updates the phase states accordingly.

declarations.name: importHeaders
declarations.doc: importHeaders spawns a new goroutine to run a header insertion into the chain. If the header's number is at the same height as the current import phase, it updates the phase states accordingly.

declarations.name: loop
declarations.doc: Loop is the main fetcher loop, checking and processing various notification events.

declarations.name: number
declarations.doc: number returns the block number of the injected object.

declarations.name: rescheduleComplete
declarations.doc: rescheduleComplete resets the specified completion timer to the next fetch timeout.

declarations.name: rescheduleFetch
declarations.doc: rescheduleFetch resets the specified fetch timer to the next blockAnnounce timeout.

declarations.name: BlockFetcher
declarations.doc: BlockFetcher is responsible for accumulating block announcements from various peers and scheduling them for retrieval.

declarations.name: HeaderRetrievalFn
declarations.doc: HeaderRetrievalFn is a callback type for retrieving a header from the local chain.

declarations.name: blockAnnounce
declarations.doc: blockAnnounce is the hash notification of the availability of a new block in the network.

declarations.name: blockBroadcasterFn
declarations.doc: blockBroadcasterFn is a callback type for broadcasting a block to connected peers.

declarations.name: blockOrHeaderInject
declarations.doc: blockOrHeaderInject represents a schedules import operation.

declarations.name: blockRetrievalFn
declarations.doc: blockRetrievalFn is a callback type for retrieving a block from the local chain.

declarations.name: bodyFilterTask
declarations.doc: bodyFilterTask represents a batch of block bodies (transactions and uncles) needing fetcher filtering.

declarations.name: bodyRequesterFn
declarations.doc: bodyRequesterFn is a callback type for sending a body retrieval request.

declarations.name: chainHeightFn
declarations.doc: chainHeightFn is a callback type to retrieve the current chain height.

declarations.name: chainInsertFn
declarations.doc: chainInsertFn is a callback type to insert a batch of blocks into the local chain.

declarations.name: headerFilterTask
declarations.doc: headerFilterTask represents a batch of headers needing fetcher filtering.

declarations.name: headerRequesterFn
declarations.doc: headerRequesterFn is a callback type for sending a header retrieval request.

declarations.name: headerVerifierFn
declarations.doc: headerVerifierFn is a callback type to verify a block's header for fast propagation.

declarations.name: headersInsertFn
declarations.doc: headersInsertFn is a callback type to insert a batch of headers into the local chain.

declarations.name: peerDropFn
declarations.doc: peerDropFn is a callback type for dropping a peer detected as malicious.

declarations.name: TestBlockMemoryExhaustionAttack
declarations.doc: Tests that blocks sent to the fetcher (either through propagation or via hash announces and retrievals) don't pile up indefinitely, exhausting available system memory.

declarations.name: TestDistantPropagationDiscarding
declarations.doc: Tests that blocks with numbers much lower or higher than out current head get discarded to prevent wasting resources on useless blocks from faulty peers.

declarations.name: TestEmptyBlockShortCircuit
declarations.doc: Tests that if a block is empty (i.e. header only), no body request should be made, and instead the header should be assembled into a whole block in itself.

declarations.name: TestFullConcurrentAnnouncements
declarations.doc: Tests that if blocks are announced by multiple peers (or even the same buggy peer), they will only get downloaded at most once.

declarations.name: TestFullDistantAnnouncementDiscarding
declarations.doc: Tests that announcements with numbers much lower or higher than out current head get discarded to prevent wasting resources on useless blocks from faulty peers.

declarations.name: TestFullInvalidNumberAnnouncement
declarations.doc: Tests that peers announcing blocks with invalid numbers (i.e. not matching the headers provided afterwards) get dropped as malicious.

declarations.name: TestFullOverlappingAnnouncements
declarations.doc: Tests that announcements arriving while a previous is being fetched still results in a valid import.

declarations.name: TestFullPendingDeduplication
declarations.doc: Tests that announces already being retrieved will not be duplicated.

declarations.name: TestFullRandomArrivalImport
declarations.doc: Tests that announcements retrieved in a random order are cached and eventually imported when all the gaps are filled in.

declarations.name: TestFullSequentialAnnouncements
declarations.doc: Tests that a fetcher accepts block/header announcements and initiates retrievals for them, successfully importing into the local chain.

declarations.name: TestHashMemoryExhaustionAttack
declarations.doc: Tests that a peer is unable to use unbounded memory with sending infinite block announcements to a node, but that even in the face of such an attack, the fetcher remains operational.

declarations.name: TestImportDeduplication
declarations.doc: Tests that blocks arriving from various sources (multiple propagations, hash announces, etc) do not get scheduled for import multiple times.

declarations.name: TestQueueGapFill
declarations.doc: Tests that direct block enqueues (due to block propagation vs. hash announce) are correctly schedule, filling and import queue gaps.

declarations.name: broadcastBlock
declarations.doc: broadcastBlock is a nop placeholder for the block broadcasting.

declarations.name: chainHeight
declarations.doc: chainHeight retrieves the current height (block number) of the chain.

declarations.name: dropPeer
declarations.doc: dropPeer is an emulator for the peer removal, simply accumulating the various peers dropped by the fetcher.

declarations.name: getBlock
declarations.doc: getBlock retrieves a block from the tester's block chain.

declarations.name: getHeader
declarations.doc: getHeader retrieves a header from the tester's block chain.

declarations.name: insertChain
declarations.doc: insertChain injects a new blocks into the simulated chain.

declarations.name: insertHeaders
declarations.doc: insertChain injects a new headers into the simulated chain.

declarations.name: makeBodyFetcher
declarations.doc: makeBodyFetcher retrieves a block body fetcher associated with a simulated peer.

declarations.name: makeChain
declarations.doc: makeChain creates a chain of n blocks starting at and including parent. the returned hash chain is ordered head->parent. In addition, every 3rd block contains a transaction and every 5th an uncle to allow testing correct block reassembly.

declarations.name: makeHeaderFetcher
declarations.doc: makeHeaderFetcher retrieves a block header fetcher associated with a simulated peer.

declarations.name: newTester
declarations.doc: newTester creates a new fetcher test mocker.

declarations.name: verifyChainHeight
declarations.doc: verifyChainHeight verifies the chain height is as expected.

declarations.name: verifyCompletingEvent
declarations.doc: verifyCompletingEvent verifies that one single event arrive on an completing channel.

declarations.name: verifyFetchingEvent
declarations.doc: verifyFetchingEvent verifies that one single event arrive on a fetching channel.

declarations.name: verifyHeader
declarations.doc: verifyHeader is a nop placeholder for the block header verification.

declarations.name: verifyImportCount
declarations.doc: verifyImportCount verifies that exactly count number of events arrive on an import hook channel.

declarations.name: verifyImportDone
declarations.doc: verifyImportDone verifies that no more events are arriving on an import channel.

declarations.name: verifyImportEvent
declarations.doc: verifyImportEvent verifies that one single event arrive on an import channel.

declarations.name: fetcherTester
declarations.doc: fetcherTester is a test simulator for mocking out local block chain.

declarations.name: Drop
declarations.doc: Drop should be called when a peer disconnects. It cleans up all the internal data structures of the given node.

declarations.doc: Enqueue imports a batch of received transaction into the transaction pool and the fetcher. This method may be called by both transaction broadcasts and direct request replies. The differentiation is important so the fetcher can re-shedule missing transactions as soon as possible.

declarations.name: NewTxFetcher
declarations.doc: NewTxFetcher creates a transaction fetcher to retrieve transaction based on hash announcements.

declarations.name: NewTxFetcherForTests
declarations.doc: NewTxFetcherForTests is a testing method to mock out the realtime clock with a simulated version and the internal randomness with a deterministic one.

declarations.name: Notify
declarations.doc: Notify announces the fetcher of the potential availability of a new batch of transactions in the network.

declarations.doc: Start boots up the announcement based synchroniser, accepting and processing hash notifications and block fetches until termination requested.

declarations.name: rescheduleTimeout
declarations.doc: rescheduleTimeout iterates over all the transactions currently in flight and schedules a cleanup run when the first would trigger. The method has a granularity of 'gatherSlack', since there's not much point in spinning over all the transactions just to maybe find one that should trigger a few ms earlier. This method is a bit "flaky" "by design". In theory the timeout timer only ever should be rescheduled if some request is pending. In practice, a timeout will cause the timer to be rescheduled every 5 secs (until the peer comes through or disconnects). This is a limitation of the fetcher code because we don't trac pending requests and timed out requests separatey. Without double tracking, if we simply didn't reschedule the timer on all-timeout then the timer would never be set again since len(request) > 0 => something's running.

declarations.name: rescheduleWait
declarations.doc: rescheduleWait iterates over all the transactions currently in the waitlist and schedules the movement into the fetcher for the earliest. The method has a granularity of 'gatherSlack', since there's not much point in spinning over all the transactions just to maybe find one that should trigger a few ms earlier.

declarations.name: TxFetcher
declarations.doc: TxFetcher is responsible for retrieving new transaction based on announcements. The fetcher operates in 3 stages: - Transactions that are newly discovered are moved into a wait list. - After ~500ms passes, transactions from the wait list that have not been broadcast to us in whole are moved into a queueing area. - When a connected peer doesn't have in-flight retrieval requests, any transaction queued up (and announced by the peer) are allocated to the peer and moved into a fetching status until it's fulfilled or fails. The invariants of the fetcher are: - Each tracked transaction (hash) must only be present in one of the three stages. This ensures that the fetcher operates akin to a finite state automata and there's do data leak. - Each peer that announced transactions may be scheduled retrievals, but only ever one concurrently. This ensures we can immediately know what is missing from a reply and reschedule it.

declarations.name: FeeHistory
declarations.doc: FeeHistory returns data relevant for fee estimation based on the specified range of blocks. The range can be specified either with absolute block numbers or ending with the latest or pending block. Backends may or may not support gathering data from the pending block or blocks older than a certain age (specified in maxHistory). The first block of the actually processed range is returned to avoid ambiguity when parts of the requested range are not available or when the head has changed during processing this request. Three arrays are returned based on the processed blocks: - reward: the requested percentiles of effective priority fees per gas of transactions in each block, sorted in ascending order and weighted by gas used. - baseFee: base fee per gas in the given block - gasUsedRatio: gasUsed/gasLimit in the given block Note: baseFee includes the next block after the newest of the returned range, because this value can be derived from the newest block.

If there are no retrievable blocks in the specified range then zero block count is returned with no error.

A naive way to represent trie nodes would be a simple list of `account || storage` path segments concatenated, but that would be very wasteful on the network. Instead, this array special cases the first element as the path in the account trie and the remaining elements as paths in the storage trie. To address an account node, the slice should have a length of 1 consisting of only the account path. There's no need to be able to address both an account node and a storage node in the same request as it cannot happen that a slot is accessed before the account path is fully expanded.

declarations.name: Syncer
declarations.doc: Syncer is an Ethereum account and storage trie syncer based on snapshots and the snap protocol. It's purpose is to download all the accounts and storage slots from remote peers and reassemble chunks of the state trie, on top of which a state sync can be run to fix any gaps / overlaps. Every network request has a variety of failure events: - The peer disconnects after task assignment, failing to send the request - The peer disconnects after sending the request, before delivering on it - The peer remains connected, but does not deliver a response in time - The peer delivers a stale response after a previous timeout - The peer delivers a refusal to serve the requested state

declarations.name: accountRequest
declarations.doc: accountRequest tracks a pending account range request to ensure responses are to actual requests and to validate any security constraints. Concurrency note: account requests and responses are handled concurrently from the main runloop to allow Merkle proof verifications on the peer's thread and to drop on invalid response. The request struct must contain all the data to construct the response without accessing runloop internals (i.e. task). That is only included to allow the runloop to match a response to the task being synced without having yet another set of maps.

declarations.name: accountResponse
declarations.doc: accountResponse is an already Merkle-verified remote response to an account range request. It contains the subtrie for the requested account range and the database that's going to be filled with the internal nodes on commit.

declarations.name: bytecodeHealRequest
declarations.doc: bytecodeHealRequest tracks a pending bytecode request to ensure responses are to actual requests and to validate any security constraints. Concurrency note: bytecode requests and responses are handled concurrently from the main runloop to allow Keccak256 hash verifications on the peer's thread and to drop on invalid response. The request struct must contain all the data to construct the response without accessing runloop internals (i.e. task). That is only included to allow the runloop to match a response to the task being synced without having yet another set of maps.

The request struct must contain all the data to construct the response without accessing runloop internals (i.e. task). declarations.name: storageRequest
declarations.doc: storageRequest tracks a pending storage ranges request to ensure responses are to actual requests and to validate any security constraints. Concurrency note: storage requests and responses are handled concurrently from the main runloop to allow Merkle proof verifications on the peer's thread and to drop on invalid response. The request struct must contain all the data to construct the response without accessing runloop internals (i.e. tasks). That is only included to allow the runloop to match a response to the task being synced without having yet another set of maps.

declarations.name: trienodeHealRequest
declarations.doc: trienodeHealRequest tracks a pending state trie request to ensure responses are to actual requests and to validate any security constraints. Concurrency note: trie node requests and responses are handled concurrently from the main runloop to allow Keccak256 hash verifications on the peer's thread and to drop on invalid response. The request struct must contain all the data to construct the response without accessing runloop internals (i.e. task). That is only included to allow the runloop to match a response to the task being synced without having yet another set of maps.

declarations.name: CaptureExit
declarations.doc: CaptureExit is called when EVM exits a scope, even if the scope didn't execute any code.

declarations.name: CaptureFault
declarations.doc: CaptureFault implements the EVMLogger interface to trace an execution fault.

declarations.name: CaptureStart
declarations.doc: CaptureStart implements the EVMLogger interface to initialize the tracing operation.

declarations.name: CaptureState
declarations.doc: CaptureState implements the EVMLogger interface to trace a single step of VM execution.

declarations.name: GetResult
declarations.doc: GetResult returns the json-encoded nested list of call traces, and any error arising from the encoding or forceful termination (via `Stop`).

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop terminates execution of the tracer at the first opportune moment.

declarations.name: lookupAccount
declarations.doc: lookupAccount fetches details of an account and adds it to the prestate if it doesn't exist there.

declarations.name: lookupStorage
declarations.doc: lookupStorage fetches the requested storage slot and adds it to the prestate of the given contract. It assumes `lookupAccount` has been performed on the contract before.

declarations.name: init
declarations.doc: init registers itself this packages as a lookup for tracers.

declarations.name: lookup
declarations.doc: lookup returns a tracer, if one can be matched to the given name.

declarations.name: register
declarations.doc: register is used by native tracers to register their presence.

declarations.name: ctorFn
declarations.doc: ctorFn is the constructor signature of a native tracer.

declarations.name: DisablePreseal
declarations.doc: DisablePreseal turns off the preseal mining feature. It's necessary for some fake consensus engine which can seal blocks instantaneously. Note this function shouldn't be exposed to API, it's unnecessary for users (miners) to actually know the underlying detail. It's only for outside project which uses this library.

declarations.name: EnablePreseal
declarations.doc: EnablePreseal turns on the preseal mining feature. It's enabled by default. Note this function shouldn't be exposed to API, it's unnecessary for users (miners) to actually know the underlying detail. It's only for outside project which uses this library.

declarations.name: GetSealingBlockAsync
declarations.doc: GetSealingBlockAsync requests to generate a sealing block according to the given parameters. Regardless of whether the generation is successful or not, there is always a result that will be returned through the result channel. The difference is that if the execution fails, the returned result is nil and the concrete error is dropped silently.

declarations.name: GetSealingBlockSync
declarations.doc: GetSealingBlockSync creates a sealing block according to the given parameters. If the generation is failed or the underlying work is already closed, an error will be returned.

declarations.name: Pending
declarations.doc: Pending returns the currently pending block and associated state.

declarations.name: PendingBlock
declarations.doc: PendingBlock returns the currently pending block. Note, to access both the pending block and the pending state simultaneously, please use Pending(), as the pending state can change between multiple method calls

declarations.name: PendingBlockAndReceipts
declarations.doc: PendingBlockAndReceipts returns the currently pending block and corresponding receipts.

declarations.name: SetGasCeil
declarations.doc: SetGasCeil sets the gaslimit to strive for when mining blocks post 1559. For pre-1559 blocks, it sets the ceiling.

declarations.name: SetRecommitInterval
declarations.doc: SetRecommitInterval sets the interval for sealing work resubmitting.

declarations.name: SubscribePendingLogs
declarations.doc: SubscribePendingLogs starts delivering logs from pending transactions to the given channel.

declarations.name: update
declarations.doc: update keeps track of the downloader events. Please be aware that this is a one shot type of update loop. It's entered once and as soon as `Done` or `Failed` has been broadcasted the events are unregistered and the loop is exited. This to prevent a major security vuln where external parties can DOS you with blocks and halt your mining operation for as long as the DOS continues.

declarations.name: Backend
declarations.doc: Backend wraps all methods required for mining. Only full node is capable to offer all the functions here.

declarations.name: Config
declarations.doc: Config is the configuration parameters of mining.

declarations.name: Miner
declarations.doc: Miner creates blocks and searches for proof-of-work values.

declarations.name: TestMinerDownloaderFirstFails
declarations.doc: TestMinerDownloaderFirstFails tests that mining is only permitted to run indefinitely once the downloader sees a DoneEvent (success). An initial FailedEvent should allow mining to stop on a subsequent downloader StartEvent.

declarations.name: TestMinerSetEtherbase
declarations.doc: TestMinerSetEtherbase checks that etherbase becomes set even if mining isn't possible at the moment

declarations.name: waitForMiningState
declarations.doc: waitForMiningState waits until either * the desired mining state was reached * a timeout was reached which fails the test

declarations.name: pull
declarations.doc: lock should be held by the caller

declarations.name: Insert
declarations.doc: Insert adds a new block to the set of unconfirmed ones.

declarations.name: Shift
declarations.doc: Shift drops all unconfirmed blocks from the set which exceed the unconfirmed sets depth allowance, checking them against the canonical chain for inclusion or staleness report.

declarations.name: newUnconfirmedBlocks
declarations.doc: newUnconfirmedBlocks returns new data structure to track currently unconfirmed blocks.

declarations.name: chainRetriever
declarations.doc: chainRetriever is used by the unconfirmed block set to verify whether a previously mined block is part of the canonical chain or not.

declarations.name: unconfirmedBlock
declarations.doc: unconfirmedBlock is a small collection of metadata about a locally mined block that is placed into a unconfirmed set for canonical chain inclusion tracking.

declarations.name: unconfirmedBlocks
declarations.doc: unconfirmedBlocks implements a data structure to maintain locally mined blocks have not yet reached enough maturity to guarantee chain inclusion. It is used by the miner to provide logs to the user when a previously mined block has a high enough guarantee to not be reorged out of the canonical chain.

declarations.name: TestUnconfirmedInsertBounds
declarations.doc: Tests that inserting blocks into the unconfirmed set accumulates them until the desired depth is reached, after which they begin to be dropped.

declarations.name: TestUnconfirmedShifts
declarations.doc: Tests that shifting blocks out of the unconfirmed set works both for normal cases as well as for corner cases such as empty sets, empty shifts or full shifts.

declarations.name: noopChainRetriever
declarations.doc: noopChainRetriever is an implementation of headerRetriever that always returns nil for any requested headers.

declarations.name: ancestorTimes
declarations.doc: collects ancestors' block times for possible throttling

declarations.name: close
declarations.doc: close terminates all background threads maintained by the worker. Note the worker does not support being closed multiple times.

declarations.name: commit
declarations.doc: nolint: govet commit runs any post-transaction state modifications, assembles the final block and commits new work if consensus engine is running. Note the assumption is held that the mutation is allowed to the passed env, do the deep copy first.

declarations.name: commitEx
declarations.doc: In Wemix, uncles are not welcome and difficulty is so low, there's no reason to run miners asynchronously.

declarations.name: commitUncle
declarations.doc: commitUncle adds the given block to uncle block set, returns error if failed to add.

declarations.name: commitWork
declarations.doc: commitWork generates several new sealing tasks based on the parent block and submit them to the sealer.

declarations.name: copy
declarations.doc: copy creates a deep copy of environment.

declarations.name: copyReceipts
declarations.doc: copyReceipts makes a deep copy of the given receipts.

declarations.name: disablePreseal
declarations.doc: disablePreseal disables pre-sealing feature

declarations.name: discard
declarations.doc: discard terminates the background prefetcher go-routine. It should always be called for all created environment instances otherwise the go-routine leak can happen.

declarations.name: enablePreseal
declarations.doc: enablePreseal enables pre-sealing feature

declarations.name: fillTransactions
declarations.doc: fillTransactions retrieves the pending transactions from the txpool and fills them into the given sealing block. The transaction selection and ordering strategy can be customized with the plugin in the future.

declarations.name: generateWork
declarations.doc: generateWork generates a sealing block based on the given parameters.

declarations.name: getSealingBlock
declarations.doc: getSealingBlock generates the sealing block based on the given parameters. The generation result will be passed back via the given channel no matter the generation itself succeeds or not.

declarations.name: isRunning
declarations.doc: isRunning returns an indicator whether worker is running or not.

declarations.name: isTTDReached
declarations.doc: isTTDReached returns the indicator if the given block has reached the total terminal difficulty for The Merge transition.

declarations.name: mainLoop
declarations.doc: mainLoop is responsible for generating and submitting sealing work based on the received event. It can support two modes: automatically generate task and submit it or return task according to given parameters for various proposes.

declarations.name: makeEnv
declarations.doc: makeEnv creates a new environment for the sealing block.

declarations.name: newWorkLoop
declarations.doc: newWorkLoop is a standalone goroutine to submit new sealing work upon received events.

declarations.name: newWorkLoopEx
declarations.doc: newWorkLoopEx is Wemix's standalone goroutine to submit new mining work upon received events.

declarations.name: pending
declarations.doc: pending returns the pending state and corresponding block.

declarations.name: pendingBlock
declarations.doc: pendingBlock returns pending block.

declarations.name: pendingBlockAndReceipts
declarations.doc: pendingBlockAndReceipts returns pending block and corresponding receipts.

declarations.name: postSideBlock
declarations.doc: postSideBlock fires a side chain event, only use it for testing.

declarations.name: prepareWork
declarations.doc: prepareWork constructs the sealing task according to the given parameters, either based on the last chain head or specified parent. In this function the pending transactions are not filled yet, only the empty task returned.

declarations.name: recalcRecommit
declarations.doc: recalcRecommit recalculates the resubmitting interval upon feedback.

declarations.name: refreshPending
declarations.doc: refreshPending reinitialize pending state

declarations.name: resultLoop
declarations.doc: resultLoop is a standalone goroutine to handle sealing result submitting and flush relative data to the database.

declarations.name: setEtherbase
declarations.doc: setEtherbase sets the etherbase used to initialize the block coinbase field.

declarations.name: setExtra
declarations.doc: setExtra sets the content used to initialize the block extra field.

declarations.name: setRecommitInterval
declarations.doc: setRecommitInterval updates the interval for miner sealing work recommitting.

declarations.name: start
declarations.doc: start sets the running status as 1 and triggers new work submitting.

declarations.name: stop
declarations.doc: stop sets the running status as 0.

declarations.name: taskLoop
declarations.doc: taskLoop is a standalone goroutine to fetch sealing task from the generator and push them to consensus engine.

declarations.name: throttleMining
declarations.doc: returns throttle delay if necessary in seconds & seconds from the parent blocks seconds seconds per 10 1 0.1 50 10 0.2 100 50 0.5 500 500 1 1000 2000 2

declarations.name: totalFees
declarations.doc: totalFees computes total consumed miner fees in ETH. Block transactions and receipts have to have the same order.

declarations.name: txFitsSize
declarations.doc: txFitsSize reports whether the transaction fits into the block size limit.

declarations.name: unclelist
declarations.doc: unclelist returns the contained uncles as the list format.

declarations.name: updateSnapshot
declarations.doc: updateSnapshot updates pending snapshot block, receipts and state.

declarations.name: environment
declarations.doc: environment is the worker's current environment and holds all information of the sealing block generation.

declarations.name: generateParams
declarations.doc: generateParams wraps various of settings for generating sealing task.

declarations.name: getWorkReq
declarations.doc: getWorkReq represents a request for getting a new sealing work with provided parameters.

declarations.name: intervalAdjust
declarations.doc: intervalAdjust represents a resubmitting interval adjustment.

declarations.name: newWorkReq
declarations.doc: newWorkReq represents a request for new sealing work submitting with relative interrupt notifier.

declarations.name: task
declarations.doc: task contains all information for consensus engine sealing and result submitting.

declarations.name: worker
declarations.doc: worker is the main object which takes care of submitting new work to consensus engine and gathering the sealing result.

declarations.name: testCommitBlockSizeLimit
declarations.doc: testCommitBlockSizeLimit feeds an oversized set of pending transactions into the given commit loop and asserts packing stops before the block exceeds the size limit.

declarations.name: testWorkerBackend
declarations.doc: testWorkerBackend implements worker.Backend interfaces and wraps all information needed during the testing.

declarations.name: makeGenesis
declarations.doc: makeGenesis creates a custom Ethash genesis block based on some pre-defined faucet accounts.

declarations.name: makeGenesis
declarations.doc: makeGenesis creates a custom Ethash genesis block based on some pre-defined faucet accounts.

declarations.name: makeGenesis
declarations.doc: makeGenesis creates a custom Clique genesis block based on some pre-defined signer and faucet accounts.

declarations.name: makeGenesis
declarations.doc: makeGenesis creates a custom Ethash genesis block based on some pre-defined faucet accounts.

declarations.name: addStatic
declarations.doc: addStatic adds a static dial candidate.

declarations.name: checkDial
declarations.doc: checkDial returns an error if node n should not be dialed.

declarations.name: dial
declarations.doc: dial performs the actual connection attempt.

declarations.name: expireHistory
declarations.doc: expireHistory removes expired items from d.history.

declarations.name: freeDialSlots
declarations.doc: freeDialSlots returns the number of free dial slots. The result can be negative when peers are connected while their task is still running.

declarations.name: logStats
declarations.doc: logStats prints dialer statistics to the log. The message is suppressed when enough peers are connected because users should only see it while their client is starting up or comes back online.

declarations.name: loop
declarations.doc: loop is the main loop of the dialer.

declarations.name: peerAdded
declarations.doc: peerAdded updates the peer set.

declarations.name: peerRemoved
declarations.doc: peerRemoved updates the peer set.

declarations.name: readNodes
declarations.doc: readNodes runs in its own goroutine and delivers nodes from the input iterator to the nodesIn channel.

declarations.name: rearmHistoryTimer
declarations.doc: rearmHistoryTimer configures d.historyTimer to fire when the next item in d.history expires.

declarations.name: removeFromStaticPool
declarations.doc: removeFromStaticPool removes the task at idx from staticPool. It does that by moving the current last element of the pool to idx and then shortening the pool by one.

declarations.name: removeStatic
declarations.doc: removeStatic removes a static dial candidate.

declarations.name: resolve
declarations.doc: resolve attempts to find the current endpoint for the destination using discovery. Resolve operations are throttled with backoff to avoid flooding the discovery network with useless queries for nodes that don't exist. The backoff delay resets when the node is found.

declarations.name: startDial
declarations.doc: startDial runs the given dial task in a separate goroutine.

declarations.name: startStaticDials
declarations.doc: startStaticDials starts n static dial tasks.

declarations.name: stop
declarations.doc: stop shuts down the dialer, canceling all current dial tasks.

declarations.name: stopHistoryTimer
declarations.doc: stopHistoryTimer stops the timer and drains the channel it sends on.

declarations.name: updateStaticPool
declarations.doc: updateStaticPool attempts to move the given static dial back into staticPool.

declarations.name: NodeDialer
declarations.doc: NodeDialer is used to connect to nodes in the network, typically by using an underlying net.Dialer but also using net.Pipe in tests.

declarations.name: dialScheduler
declarations.doc: dialer creates outbound connections and submits them into Server. Two types of peer connections can be created: - static dials are pre-configured connections. The dialer attempts keep these nodes connected at all times. - dynamic dials are created from node discovery results. The dialer continuously reads candidate nodes from its input iterator and attempts to create peer connections to nodes arriving through the iterator.

declarations.name: dialTask
declarations.doc: A dialTask generated for each node that is dialed.

declarations.name: tcpDialer
declarations.doc: tcpDialer implements NodeDialer using real TCP connections.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close ends the iterator, unblocking Next.

declarations.name: Dial
declarations.doc: Dial implements NodeDialer.

declarations.name: Next
declarations.doc: Next moves to the next node.

declarations.name: Node
declarations.doc: Node returns the current node.

declarations.name: TestDialSchedDynDial
declarations.doc: This test checks that dynamic dials are launched from discovery results.

declarations.name: TestDialSchedHistory
declarations.doc: This test checks that past dials are not retried for some time.

declarations.name: TestDialSchedManyStaticNodes
declarations.doc: This test checks that static dials are selected at random.

declarations.name: TestDialSchedNetRestrict
declarations.doc: This test checks that candidates that do not match the netrestrict list are not dialed.

declarations.name: TestDialSchedRemoveStatic
declarations.doc: This test checks that removing static nodes stops connecting to them.

declarations.name: TestDialSchedStaticDial
declarations.doc: This test checks that static dials work and obey the limits.

declarations.name: addNodes
declarations.doc: addNodes adds nodes to the iterator buffer and unblocks Next.

declarations.name: completeDials
declarations.doc: completeDials unblocks calls to Dial for the given nodes.

declarations.name: waitForDials
declarations.doc: waitForDials waits for calls to Dial with the given nodes as argument. Those calls will be held blocking until completeDials is called with the same nodes.

declarations.name: dialTestDialer
declarations.doc: dialTestDialer is the NodeDialer used by runDialTest.

declarations.name: dialTestIterator
declarations.doc: dialTestIterator is the input iterator for dialer tests. This works a bit like a channel with infinite buffer: nodes are added to the buffer with addNodes, which unblocks Next and returns them from the iterator.

declarations.name: dialTestResolver
declarations.doc: dialTestResolver tracks calls to resolve.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close unblocks any pending ReadMsg and WriteMsg calls on both ends of the pipe. They will return ErrPipeClosed. Close also interrupts any reads from a message payload.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close closes the underlying MsgReadWriter if it implements the io.Closer interface

declarations.name: Decode
declarations.doc: Decode parses the RLP content of a message into the given value, which must be a pointer. For the decoding rules, please see package rlp.

declarations.name: Discard
declarations.doc: Discard reads any remaining payload data into a black hole.

declarations.name: ExpectMsg
declarations.doc: ExpectMsg reads a message from r and verifies that its code and encoded RLP content match the provided values. If content is nil, the payload is discarded and not verified.

declarations.name: MsgPipe
declarations.doc: MsgPipe creates a message pipe. Reads on one end are matched with writes on the other. The pipe is full-duplex, both ends implement MsgReadWriter.

declarations.name: Read
declarations.doc: note: when using eofSignal to detect whether a message payload has been read, Read might not be called for zero sized messages.

declarations.name: ReadMsg
declarations.doc: ReadMsg returns a message sent on the other end of the pipe.

declarations.name: ReadMsg
declarations.doc: ReadMsg reads a message from the underlying MsgReadWriter and emits a "message received" event

declarations.name: Send
declarations.doc: Send writes an RLP-encoded message with the given code. data should encode as an RLP list.

declarations.name: SendItems
declarations.doc: SendItems writes an RLP with the given code and data elements. For a call such as: SendItems(w, code, e1, e2, e3) the message payload will be an RLP list containing the items: [e1, e2, e3]

declarations.name: WriteMsg
declarations.doc: WriteMsg sends a message on the pipe. It blocks until the receiver has consumed the message payload.

declarations.name: WriteMsg
declarations.doc: WriteMsg writes a message to the underlying MsgReadWriter and emits a "message sent" event

declarations.name: newMsgEventer
declarations.doc: newMsgEventer returns a msgEventer which sends message events to the given feed

declarations.name: Msg
declarations.doc: Msg defines the structure of a p2p message. Note that a Msg can only be sent once since the Payload reader is consumed during sending. It is not possible to create a Msg and send it any number of times. If you want to reuse an encoded structure, encode the payload into a byte array and create a separate Msg with a bytes.Reader as Payload for each send.

declarations.name: MsgPipeRW
declarations.doc: MsgPipeRW is an endpoint of a MsgReadWriter pipe.

declarations.name: MsgReadWriter
declarations.doc: MsgReadWriter provides reading and writing of encoded messages. Implementations should ensure that ReadMsg and WriteMsg can be called simultaneously from multiple goroutines.

declarations.name: eofSignal
declarations.doc: eofSignal wraps a reader with eof signaling. the eof channel is closed when the wrapped reader returns an error or when count bytes have been read.

declarations.name: msgEventer
declarations.doc: msgEventer wraps a MsgReadWriter and sends events whenever a message is sent or received

declarations.name: TestMsgPipeConcurrentClose
declarations.doc: This test should panic if concurrent close isn't implemented correctly.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close delegates a close operation to the underlying connection, unregisters the peer from the traffic registries and emits close event.

declarations.name: Read
declarations.doc: Read delegates a network read to the underlying connection, bumping the common and the peer ingress traffic meters along the way.

declarations.name: Write
declarations.doc: Write delegates a network write to the underlying connection, bumping the common and the peer egress traffic meters along the way.

declarations.name: newMeteredConn
declarations.doc: newMeteredConn creates a new metered connection, bumps the ingress or egress connection meter and also increases the metered peer count. If the metrics system is disabled, function returns the original connection.

declarations.name: meteredConn
declarations.doc: meteredConn is a wrapper around a net.Conn that meters both the inbound and outbound network traffic.

declarations.name: Caps
declarations.doc: Caps returns the capabilities (supported subprotocols) of the remote peer.

declarations.name: Disconnect
declarations.doc: Disconnect terminates the peer connection with the given reason. It returns immediately and does not wait until the connection is closed.

declarations.name: Fullname
declarations.doc: Fullname returns the node name that the remote node advertised.

declarations.name: ID
declarations.doc: ID returns the node's public key.

declarations.name: Inbound
declarations.doc: Inbound returns true if the peer is an inbound connection

declarations.name: Info
declarations.doc: Info gathers and returns a collection of metadata known about a peer.

declarations.name: LocalAddr
declarations.doc: LocalAddr returns the local address of the network connection.

declarations.name: Name
declarations.doc: Name returns an abbreviated form of the name

declarations.name: NewPeer
declarations.doc: NewPeer returns a peer for testing purposes.

declarations.name: NewPeerPipe
declarations.doc: NewPeerPipe creates a peer for testing purposes. The message pipe given as the last parameter is closed when Disconnect is called on the peer.

declarations.name: Node
declarations.doc: Node returns the peer's node descriptor.

declarations.name: RemoteAddr
declarations.doc: RemoteAddr returns the remote address of the network connection.

declarations.name: RunningCap
declarations.doc: RunningCap returns true if the peer is actively connected using any of the enumerated versions of a specific protocol, meaning that at least one of the versions is supported by both this node and the peer p.

declarations.name: String
declarations.doc: String implements fmt.Stringer.

declarations.name: getProto
declarations.doc: getProto finds the protocol responsible for handling the given message code.

declarations.name: matchProtocols
declarations.doc: matchProtocols creates structures for matching named subprotocols.

declarations.name: Peer
declarations.doc: Peer represents a connected remote node.

declarations.name: PeerEvent
declarations.doc: PeerEvent is an event emitted when peers are either added or dropped from a p2p.Server or when a message is sent or received on a peer connection

declarations.name: PeerEventType
declarations.doc: PeerEventType is the type of peer events emitted by a p2p.Server

declarations.name: PeerInfo
declarations.doc: PeerInfo represents a short summary of the information known about a connected peer. Sub-protocol independent fields are contained and initialized here, with protocol specifics delegated to all connected sub-protocols.

declarations.name: protoHandshake
declarations.doc: protoHandshake is the RLP structure of the protocol handshake.

declarations.name: TestPeerDisconnect
declarations.doc: This test checks that a disconnect message sent by a peer is returned as the error from Peer.run.

declarations.name: TestPeerDisconnectRace
declarations.doc: This test is supposed to verify that Peer can reliably handle multiple causes of disconnection occurring at the same time.

declarations.name: newNode
declarations.doc: newNode creates a node record with the given address.

declarations.name: uintID
declarations.doc: uintID encodes i into a node ID.

declarations.name: Cap
declarations.doc: Cap is the structure of a peer capability.

declarations.name: Protocol
declarations.doc: Protocol represents a P2P subprotocol implementation.

declarations.name: AddPeer
declarations.doc: AddPeer adds the given node to the static node set. When there is room in the peer set, the server will connect to the node. If the connection fails for any reason, the server will attempt to reconnect the peer.

declarations.name: AddTrustedPeer
declarations.doc: AddTrustedPeer adds the given node to a reserved trusted list which allows the node to always connect, even if the slot are full.

declarations.name: Close
declarations.doc: Close implements discover.UDPConn

declarations.name: LocalNode
declarations.doc: LocalNode returns the local node record.

declarations.name: NodeInfo
declarations.doc: NodeInfo gathers and returns a collection of metadata known about the host.

declarations.name: PeerCount
declarations.doc: PeerCount returns the number of connected peers.

declarations.name: PeerInfo
declarations.doc: PeerInfo returns a collection of metadata known about the given node

declarations.name: Peers
declarations.doc: Peers returns all connected peers.

declarations.name: PeersInfo
declarations.doc: PeersInfo returns an array of metadata objects describing connected peers.

declarations.name: ReadFromUDP
declarations.doc: ReadFromUDP implements discover.UDPConn

declarations.name: RemovePeer
declarations.doc: RemovePeer removes a node from the static node set. It also disconnects from the given node if it is currently connected as a peer. This method blocks until all protocols have exited and the peer is removed. Do not use RemovePeer in protocol implementations, call Disconnect on the Peer instead.

declarations.name: RemoveTrustedPeer
declarations.doc: RemoveTrustedPeer removes the given node from the trusted peer set.

declarations.name: Self
declarations.doc: Self returns the local node's endpoint information.

declarations.name: SetupConn
declarations.doc: SetupConn runs the handshakes and attempts to add the connection as a peer. It returns when the connection has been added as a peer or the handshakes have failed.

declarations.name: Start
declarations.doc: Start starts running the server. Servers can not be re-used after stopping.

declarations.name: Stop
declarations.doc: Stop terminates the server and all active peer connections. It blocks until all active connections have been closed.

declarations.name: SubscribeEvents
declarations.doc: SubscribeEvents subscribes the given channel to peer events

declarations.name: checkpoint
declarations.doc: checkpoint sends the conn to run, which performs the post-handshake checks for the stage (posthandshake, addpeer).

declarations.name: doPeerOp
declarations.doc: doPeerOp runs fn on the main loop.

declarations.name: listenLoop
declarations.doc: listenLoop runs in its own goroutine and accepts inbound connections.

declarations.name: run
declarations.doc: run is the main loop of the server.

declarations.name: runPeer

declarations.doc: dispatch runs in its own goroutine, handles incoming packets and deals with calls. For any destination node there is at most one 'active call', stored in the t.activeCall* maps. A call is made active when it is sent. The active call can be answered by a matching response, in which case c.ch receives the response; or by timing out, in which case c.err receives the error. When the function that created the call signals the active call is done through callDone, the next call from the call queue is started. Calls may also be answered by a WHOAREYOU packet referencing the call packet's authTag. When that happens the call is simply re-sent to complete the handshake. We allow one handshake attempt per call.

declarations.name: FairMix
declarations.doc: FairMix aggregates multiple node iterators. The mixer itself is an iterator which ends only when Close is called. Source iterators added via AddSource are removed from the mix when they end. The distribution of nodes returned by Next is approximately fair, i.e. FairMix attempts to draw from all sources equally often. However, if a certain source is slow and doesn't return a node within the configured timeout, a node from any other source will be returned. It's safe to call AddSource and Close concurrently with Next.

declarations.name: ParseV4
declarations.doc: ParseV4 parses a node URL. There are two basic forms of node URLs: - incomplete nodes, which only have the public key (node ID) - complete nodes, which contain the public key and IP/Port information For incomplete nodes, the designator must look like one of these enode://<hex node id> <hex node id> For complete nodes, the node ID is encoded in the username portion of the URL, separated from the host by an @ sign. The hostname can only be given as an IP address or using DNS domain name. The port in the host name section is the TCP listening port. If the TCP and UDP (discovery) ports differ, the UDP port is specified as query parameter "discport". In the following example, the node URL describes a node with IP address 10.3.58.6, TCP listening port 30303 and UDP discovery port 30301. enode://<hex node id>@10.3.58.6:30303?discport=30301

declarations.name: Capacity
declarations.doc: Capacity calculates the number of items the peer is estimated to be able to retrieve within the alloted time slot. The method will round up any division errors and will add an additional overestimation ratio on top. The reason for overshooting the capacity is because certain message types might not increase the load proportionally to the requested items, so fetching a bit more might still take the same RTT. By forcefully overshooting by a small amount, we can avoid locking into a lower-that-real capacity.

declarations.name: Capacity
declarations.doc: Capacity is a helper function to access a specific tracker without having to track it explicitly outside.

declarations.name: MeanCapacities
declarations.doc: MeanCapacities returns the capacities averaged across all the added trackers. The purpos of the mean capacities are to initialize a new peer with some sane starting values that it will hopefully outperform. If the mean overshoots, the peer will be cut back to minimal capacity and given another chance.

declarations.name: MedianRoundTrip
declarations.doc: MedianRoundTrip returns the median RTT across all known trackers. The purpose of the median RTT is to initialize a new peer with sane statistics that it will hopefully outperform. If it seriously underperforms, there's a risk of dropping the peer, but that is ok as we're aiming for a strong median.

declarations.name: NewTracker
declarations.doc: NewTracker creates a new message rate tracker for a specific peer. An initial RTT is needed to avoid a peer getting marked as an outlier compared to others right after joining. It's suggested to use the median rtt across all peers to init a new peer tracker.

declarations.name: NewTrackers
declarations.doc: NewTrackers creates an empty set of trackers to be filled with peers.

declarations.name: TargetRoundTrip
declarations.doc: TargetRoundTrip returns the current target round trip time for a request to complete in.The returned RTT is slightly under the estimated RTT. The reason is that message rate estimation is a 2 dimensional problem which is solvable for any RTT. The goal is to gravitate towards smaller RTTs instead of large messages, to result in a stabler download stream.

declarations.name: TargetTimeout
declarations.doc: TargetTimeout returns the timeout allowance for a single request to finish under. The timeout is proportional to the roundtrip, but also takes into consideration the tracker's confidence in said roundtrip and scales it accordingly. The final value is capped to avoid runaway requests.

declarations.name: Update
declarations.doc: Update modifies the peer's capacity values for a specific data type with a new measurement. If the delivery is zero, the peer is assumed to have either timed out or to not have the requested data, resulting in a slash to 0 capacity. This avoids assigning the peer retrievals that it won't be able to honour.

declarations.name: detune

declarations.name: Tracker
declarations.doc: Tracker estimates the throughput capacity of a peer with regard to each data type it can deliver. The goal is to dynamically adjust request sizes to max out network throughput without overloading either the peer or th elocal node. By tracking in real time the latencies and bandiwdths peers exhibit for each packet type, it's possible to prevent overloading by detecting a slowdown on one type when another type is pushed too hard. Similarly, real time measurements also help avoid overloading the local net connection if our peers would otherwise be capable to deliver more, but the local link is saturated. In that case, the live measurements will force us to reduce request sizes until the throughput gets stable. Lastly, message rate measurements allows us to detect if a peer is unsuaully slow compared to other peers, in which case we can decide to keep it around or free up the slot so someone closer. Since throughput tracking and estimation adapts dynamically to live network conditions, it's fine to have multiple trackers locally track the same peer in different subsystem. The throughput will simply be distributed across the two trackers if both are highly active.

declarations.name: Trackers

All callbacks of an operation are running from the thread/goroutine of the initial caller and parallel operations are not permitted. Therefore the callback is never called concurrently. It is the responsibility of the implemented state logic to avoid deadlocks and to reach a stable state in a finite amount of steps. State subscriptions should be installed before loading the node database or making the first state update.
